name: AgentEvolver
org_or_authors: Alibaba Tongyi Lab / ModelScope (Yunpeng Zhai, Shuchang Tao, Cheng Chen, Anni Zou, ..., Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou; 13 authors)
last_activity: 2026-04-01 (last push; last substantive master commit 2026-01-30 'online observer'; SeeUPO branch 2026-04-01). Issues still being filed through 2026-08 with no maintainer replies.
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2511.10395 (cs.LG), Nov 2025; no venue. Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar 429). Follow-ups from same group: CuES (arXiv 2512.01311, curiosity-driven task synthesis) and SeeUPO (sequence-level agentic RL, Mar 2026 branch).
mechanism:
Outer loop is standard GRPO on veRL/Ray updating Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct weights (lr 1e-6, batch 32, n=8 rollouts/task, KL 0.001, max 30 env steps, 8xA100). Three LLM-driven modules feed it:

1) Self-questioning (Task Manager): a human-written Environment Profile JSON (entities/attributes/operations + task_preference difficulty knobs) seeds a random-walk exploration by an external LLM (Qwen-Plus, temp 1.0; breadth-first Nb steps then depth-first Nd) against the sandboxed env_service. Trajectories are summarized into TaskObjective = {query, ground_truth action_sequence}. Curation: lexical dedup (0.8), FeasibilityFilter re-executes the reference solution, UnifiedMixtureStrategy mixes synthetic with original tasks. Synthetic tasks are graded by an LLM judge (Qwen3-235B) that sees the reference solution (`llm-binary-gt-no_constraint`); original tasks use env reward.

2) Self-navigating (Experience Manager + ReMe service): before training, the initial policy does 4 rollouts/task; ReMe runs success/failure/comparative extraction -> LLM validation -> dedup -> vector store. At rollout, top-k (3) experiences are retrieved by cosine similarity and prepended for eta=0.5 of each group ('mixed'); experience text is regex-stripped before the gradient ('alldiscard') so the policy must internalize it; positive-advantage experience samples get a wider PPO upper clip (0.6 vs 0.28) via an exp_mask heterogeneous loss. Reference config sets updated_freq: 0, so the pool is static after cold-start (code supports periodic async re-summarization).

3) Self-attributing (ADCA-GRPO): Qwen-Max labels every step GOOD/BAD in one pass given the trajectory and outcome; mapped to +/-0.2, z-scored per group at trajectory level, fused with separately z-scored outcome reward at the terminal step (alpha=1.0), suffix-summed into step advantages and broadcast to tokens.

Single policy; no population, no archive, no acceptance gate — every RL step is applied.
eval_loop: Signal = benchmark scores on held-out AppWorld (TGC, test-normal) and BFCL v3 multi-turn val splits, avg@8/best@8, run before training and periodically; validation rollouts use no experience injection (woexp) so it measures internalized capability. Training reward: env verifier for original tasks, reference-grounded LLM judge for synthetic tasks (judge sees ground truth, actor does not — but this isolation is not machine-checked, see issue #48). Drift/hacking guards: feasibility re-execution of reference solutions, dedup filters, experience stripping before gradient, separate normalization of process vs outcome signals, KL penalty. There is NO fitness-based acceptance or rollback of weight updates, no held-out-environment generalization test, and the judges/attributors are fixed frontier models that are never audited during training. Reproducibility is contested: issue #46 reports far lower step-0 and post-training BFCL/AppWorld numbers (TGC@8 <10%), unanswered.
key_results: Qwen2.5-7B: AppWorld avg@8 1.8 -> 32.4 (best@8 5.6 -> 51.2), BFCL v3 29.8 -> 57.9; avg 15.8 -> 45.2. Qwen2.5-14B: AppWorld 18.0 -> 48.7, BFCL 41.6 -> 66.5; avg 29.8 -> 57.6. The trained 7B (45.2) beats the untrained 14B base (29.8) — the 'small beats 14B' claim compares to an un-finetuned baseline, not a 14B trained with plain GRPO. Ablations: +Questioning alone gives most of the gain (7B avg 15.8 -> 36.1); +Navigating adds ~3.7, +Attributing adds ~5.2, all three 45.2. Docs claim ADCA-GRPO gives ~10% improvement and ~40% fewer training steps vs GRPO. Paper claims synthetic tasks match ground-truth data and reference-grounded judge beats naive LLM judging (numbers not extractable from HTML).
limitations: (1) Not truly 'self': exploration, task synthesis, reward judging, step attribution and experience summarization all call stronger external teacher models (Qwen-Plus/Qwen-Max/Qwen3-235B) — the evolving policy is distilling from fixed frontier models. (2) Requires manual Environment Profile per environment plus a sandboxed env_service. (3) Experience pool is static after cold start in the reference config (updated_freq: 0); no experience retirement or utility tracking; experience unused at test. (4) No acceptance test/rollback/best-checkpoint gating of weight updates. (5) Evaluated only on two tool-use benchmarks; mixture uses original benchmark tasks (use_original_tasks: true) so gains are not purely from synthetic data. (6) Heavy: 8xA100, Ray+veRL+vLLM+ReMe services; OOM reports (#30, #41). (7) Reproducibility contested (#46, #45), BFCL training script missing (#32), no HF checkpoint export (#29). (8) Master effectively unmaintained since ~Feb 2026; security issue (#50: env_service unauthenticated, code execution) open. (9) Modules are independent; no coupling of attribution/experience back into task generation (listed as 'upcoming').
key_insight: Turn the three bottlenecks of agentic RL (no tasks, blind exploration, sparse credit) into LLM-generated signals that are kept OUT of the gradient path: tasks come from environment exploration with executable reference solutions for grounded judging; retrieved experience is injected only at rollout and stripped before the policy update (with a looser off-policy clip) so it is distilled into weights instead of memorized; and per-step GOOD/BAD attribution is z-scored separately from the outcome reward so dense process credit cannot swamp the sparse success signal.
open_gaps: Evaluator/teacher does not evolve: judges (Qwen3-235B, Qwen-Max) and explorer (Qwen-Plus) are fixed external APIs; no self-consistency check of judge against env ground truth during training and no mechanism to detect judge exploitation
No acceptance gate or rollback: every RL step is applied regardless of validation; no best-checkpoint selection, no regression detection on held-out tasks

Experience pool is cold-start only (updated_freq: 0 in overall.yaml); no online curation, no per-experience utility scoring, no retirement of stale/harmful experiences, and experience is never used at inference time
Task curriculum is static: difficulty set by hand-tuned task_preference in the Environment Profile, not adapted to the policy's current pass rate (no targeting of 20-80% success band)
Environment Profile (entities/attributes/operations) must be hand-written per environment; no automatic schema induction from API specs or exploration
Ground-truth/reference-solution isolation from the actor is not machine-checked (issue #48 asks for a canary test) — a leak would let the policy learn the answer channel
Weights-only evolution requiring 8xA100 + Ray/veRL/vLLM/ReMe; nothing here is usable by an application developer who cannot fine-tune
Three modules run independently; attribution labels are not fed back to task generation or experience extraction, and no multi-agent co-evolution despite the separate Game Arena
No cross-environment transfer: experiences and synthetic tasks are per-workspace; generalization is only tested on the same benchmark's held-out split
Reproducibility unresolved: multiple users report much lower AppWorld/BFCL numbers than the paper (#46), BFCL training script absent (#32), and master has had no maintainer response since ~Mar 2026
safety_measures: Sandboxed env_service for exploration/rollouts (but unauthenticated, binds 0.0.0.0, /step executes code — open issue #50). FeasibilityFilter re-executes reference solutions to drop hallucinated tasks; lexical/semantic dedup. Reference solution is passed only to the judge path by design but without a regression test. KL penalty (0.001) and PPO clipping bound policy drift; experience stripping prevents memorizing injected text. No guard against judge-model reward hacking, no rollback of bad updates, no human-in-the-loop.

name: Absolute Zero Reasoner (AZR)
org_or_authors: Andrew Zhao, Yiran Wu, Yang Yue, Tong Wu, Quentin Xu, Matthieu Lin, Shenzhi Wang, Qingyun Wu, Zilong Zheng, Gao Huang — Tsinghua LeapLab / BIGAI / Penn State
venue_or_citations: NeurIPS 2025 (Semantic Scholar venue; scout reports spotlight, not independently verified). 314 citations / 29 influential (Semantic Scholar, 2026-09). 299 forks. Public W&B logs + HF checkpoints (3B/7B/14B Coder, 7B/14B Base, Llama3.1-8B).
mechanism: One policy π plays two roles over three code-task types (deduction: predict o from (p,i); abduction: predict i from (p,o); induction: synthesize p from ≤10 (i,o) pairs + message). Each training step (verified in azr_ray_trainer.fit): for each task type, (1) PROPOSE: prompt π with K=6 reference triplets uniformly sampled from that type's buffer (K=1 program for induction) to write a new, "sufficiently different, challenging" program+input; (2) validate via Python executor: AST check, banned-module list (random, os, sys, time, hashlib, threading...), 10s timeout, determinism check by executing twice; (3) learnability reward: run the current solver G=8 times at T=1.0 on the new task, r_propose = 1 - mean_acc if 0<acc, else 0; invalid proposals treated as acc=1 → reward 0; (4) valid triplets appended to buffer regardless of reward (cap 16384; code truncates with [:max] so newest are dropped once full); (5) SOLVE: sample 64 tasks per type from buffer ("max_new": prefer last step's additions, fill uniformly), reward = binary executor equality (induction: all hidden IO pairs). Composite: r_role if formatted+correct, -0.5 if formatted but wrong/invalid, -1 if malformed. All 6 (role×task) batches of 64 are concatenated (384/step) and updated with TRR++ = REINFORCE++ with a separate mean/std baseline per (task,role); no critic, no KL, no ref policy, lr 1e-6, rollout.n=1. Seed = identity function → S×B=256 self-generated triplets before self-play. Evolution is purely in the weights plus a growing self-proposed task buffer.
eval_loop: Fitness is entirely executor-grounded: solver gets binary Python value-equality against ground truth produced by running the proposed program; proposer gets 1 - Monte-Carlo solve rate (G=8 samples of current policy), zero for unsolvable, plus format penalties (-0.5/-1). Drift/hacking prevention: hard validity gates (AST, banned modules, determinism via double execution, timeout), invalid proposals scored as trivially solvable (reward 0 then -0.5), per-(task,role) baseline normalization (TRR++). External benchmarks (HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench, AIME24/25, AMC, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench) are report-only; CruxEval/LCB-execution validated every 10 steps for monitoring, NOT used as checkpoint acceptance. No KL anchor, no held-out gating, no rollback (remove_previous_ckpt_in_save=True keeps only latest). Solver reward is unhackable (executor), but proposer learnability can be satisfied by brittle-format tasks rather than genuinely harder reasoning; paper flags better learning-progress estimation (MAGELLAN) as future work.
key_results: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B + AZR: Code avg 61.6 (+5.0), Math avg 39.1 (+15.2), overall 50.4 (+10.2), beating best zero-setting models trained on 2k–484k curated examples by 1.8 avg. 14B-Coder: +13.2 overall (+22.8 math). 3B-Coder: +5.7. Llama3.1-8B: only +3.2. Ablations on 7B-Base (full 46.8): deduction-only 43.3; no induction 43.8; no reference conditioning (K=0) 43.8 (math -5.3); solve-only (proposer not trained) 45.4 (-1.4). Larger models keep improving past 200 steps; 3B plateaus. Emergent: interleaved comment-plans in induction, trial-and-error in abduction with largest token growth; Llama "uh-oh moment" safety-concerning CoT.
limitations: Task space restricted to deterministic, side-effect-free Python (p,i,o) triplets; no stochastic programs, tools, multi-turn, or natural-language domains. Gains depend heavily on base-model priors (Qwen ≫ Llama). Ablations only on 7B-Base due to compute. Learnability = current solve rate, not learning progress. No safety oversight; authors observed concerning CoT. Executor is raw exec with a banned-word list, "not secure for production." Main branch marked "UNDER TESTING" after veRL upgrade; reproduce from `paper` branch. Diversity/complexity intrinsic rewards exist in code but are disabled (coef 0) in all released runs; composite-function scheduler disabled. Buffer cap drops newest tasks once full. Repo inactive since 2025-08.
key_insight: A single model can bootstrap reasoning with zero external data if you (a) pick a task space whose ground truth is generated by executing the model's own proposal, so verification is free and unhackable, and (b) pay the proposer with 1 - (solver's current success rate), which auto-tunes a curriculum to the edge of competence; the same open-ended executor-verified loop transfers out of domain (code → math +15 pts).
open_gaps: Verification is limited to deterministic Python value-equality; no path to self-generating verifiable tasks for tool use, multi-turn agents, stochastic programs, or natural-language work
Proposer reward is instantaneous solve-rate (G=8 MC samples), not learning progress; no mechanism detects tasks that are 'hard' only because of brittle formatting or answer extraction
No explicit diversity/novelty pressure: intrinsic diversity/complexity rewards are implemented but disabled (coef=0); dedup and curriculum scheduling absent, buffer sampled uniformly
Task buffer is a flat list capped at 16384 that silently drops newest entries once full; no difficulty/age-aware archive, no priority replay, no cross-run or cross-model task library reuse
No regression protection: checkpoint acceptance is not gated by held-out eval, only the latest checkpoint is kept, no rollback, no KL anchor to reference policy
Only weights evolve; the proposer prompts, validity filters, reward function, and executor are fixed by hand and never self-modified
Requires full-parameter RL (veRL+vLLM+Ray) on 2-8x80GB GPUs; unusable for app developers who cannot fine-tune, and nothing transfers to closed-API models
Executor is unsandboxed raw exec with a banned-word list; no isolation, resource limits beyond timeout, or safety oversight despite observed concerning CoT on Llama
Improvement is bounded by base-model priors (Llama +3.2 vs Qwen-14B +13.2) and plateaus for small models; no evidence of open-ended, unbounded self-improvement
Single policy playing two roles; no separate evolving verifier/judge, no population or multi-agent diversity, no evaluation of whether proposed tasks drift toward degenerate families over long runs
safety_measures: AST check + banned-module list (os/sys/subprocess/threading/random/time/hashlib etc.), 10s execution timeout, determinism double-execution, format penalties; periodic executor cleanup. No sandboxing (SandboxFusion optional since 2025-07), no oversight of CoT; authors explicitly state safety management of self-improving components is unaddressed and report concerning 'uh-oh moment' outputs from Llama3.1-8B.
sources_read: absolute_zero_reasoner/trainer/ppo/azr_ray_trainer.py (fit loop, DatasetManager, buffer truncation, pred data mix)

name: GEPA (Genetic-Pareto Reflective Evolution)
org_or_authors: Lakshya A Agrawal, Shangyin Tan, Omar Khattab, Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica, Dan Klein, Koushik Sen, Alexandros Dimakis et al. (UC Berkeley / Stanford / Databricks / MIT; 17 authors)
venue_or_citations: arXiv 2507.19457 (v2 Feb 2026), accepted ICLR 2026 (Oral); ~366 citations per scout; 543 forks; 123 open issues; PyPI releases through v0.1.4 (Jul 2026); integrated into DSPy, MLflow, Opik, Pydantic AI, Google ADK, OpenAI/HF cookbooks
mechanism: Core loop (src/gepa/core/engine.py + proposer/reflective_mutation): (1) Seed candidate = dict of named text components (prompts, code, skill files, configs) is fully evaluated on a validation set D_pareto; state stores per-candidate, per-instance score vectors. (2) Each iteration, ParetoCandidateSelector builds the per-instance Pareto front (best score on each val example), removes globally dominated candidates, and samples a parent with probability proportional to how many instances it wins (frontier_type can be per-instance, per-objective, hybrid, or cartesian). (3) A round-robin component selector picks which text field to mutate; the parent is run on a minibatch of the train split with capture_traces=True, and the adapter's make_reflective_dataset turns trajectories plus evaluator-supplied Actionable Side Information (error messages, profiler output, judge feedback, images) into a reflective dataset. (4) A reflection LM (single call by default; ComBEE map-reduce or a Claude Code agent as alternatives) receives current text + examples + feedback and writes a replacement text. (5) Gate: child is re-run on the same minibatch; StrictImprovementAcceptance requires sum(new) > sum(old); passing children get a full valset evaluation and are added to the pool with ancestry; Pareto front updated. (6) Merge proposer: after new programs are found, sample two frontier candidates with a common ancestor whose components diverged, recombine component-wise, accept if minibatch score >= max(parents). PxNSampling (P parents x N mutations per step) batches proposals. optimize_anything wraps this as a black-box evaluator API and now also dispatches to AutoResearch (a Claude Code session owning the whole loop) and Meta-Harness engines, composable via optimize_sequential/best_of/adaptive_sequential.
eval_loop: Fitness = user-supplied scalar metric per example plus optional textual/structured side_info (ASI) used only by the reflection LM. Two-stage acceptance prevents drift: a cheap minibatch strict-improvement gate on the train split, then a full validation-set evaluation before a candidate enters the pool; per-instance Pareto tracking keeps specialists alive so greedy collapse does not occur (paper Table 3: Pareto +12.44% vs SelectBestCandidate +6.05% vs BeamSearch +5.11%). Final selection = best aggregate validation score; papers/blogs report separate held-out test scores (paper Fig 16 generalization gap; parallel-proposals post shows val overfitting: single-mutation had a 9-point val-to-test gap on LiveBench-Math vs 2 for 2x4). Nothing prevents reward hacking of a weak evaluator or LLM judge beyond the user's metric design; evaluation cache namespaced by split so val rollouts cannot be reused from train (PR #425).
key_results: Paper (ICLR 2026 Oral): Qwen3-8B aggregate +9.62% (GEPA) vs +3.68% (GRPO, 24k rollouts) across HotpotQA/IFBench/HoVer/PUPA/AIME/LiveBench-Math, up to 35x fewer rollouts (GEPA reaches optimum in 79-737 train rollouts); vs MIPROv2 +13.33% vs +5.64% on GPT-4.1-mini; prompts up to 9.2x shorter than MIPROv2; NPUEval vector utilization 4.25% -> 30.52% mean; KernelBench fast_1 ~0% -> >20%. Repo/blogs: AIME-2025 GPT-4.1-mini 46.6% -> 56.6-60%; ARC-AGI agent architecture (Gemini 3 Flash) 32.5% -> 89.5% test; CloudCast scheduling policy 40.2% test cost savings; gskill: Mini-SWE-Agent resolve rate 55% -> 82% (Jinja) and 24% -> 93% (Bleve) on held-out test with <300 rollouts, skills transfer to Claude Code Haiku 4.5 (79.3% -> 98.3% on Bleve); parallel proposals (Jul 2026): 3-4x wall-clock speedup and held-out test 68.9% -> 72.1% (LiveBench-Math), 49.0% -> 60.0% (HoVer); omni meta-optimizer 63.2 vs best standalone 55.4 on Frontier-CS at $20; FST (May 2026) interleaves GEPA with CISPO RL for ~70% lower KL at matched accuracy. Databricks: open models + GEPA beat Claude Opus 4.1 at 90x lower cost.
limitations: Most rollout budget is spent on full validation evals (paper-stated; PxN mitigates but full-val is still the bottleneck). Merge is hyperparameter-sensitive (hurt Qwen3-8B: +7.17% vs +9.62% without). Quality depends entirely on evaluator feedback richness (feedback engineering is on the user). Optimizes toward a fixed validation set; measurable val-to-test gap, and single-mutation runs overfit val (9-point gap). Reflection is stateless by default: rejected proposals are forgotten so the same parent repeats failed mutations (issue #379); truncated LM outputs can be adopted as candidates (#390). No cross-task/cross-run memory of lessons; each run starts from scratch. Component selection is round-robin, not credit-assigned. Evaluator cost/latency for agentic tasks (Docker, SWE tasks) is the real bottleneck. omni results are 10 problems at $20 each; ARC-AGI/AIME test sets are small. The agent-architecture and code claims are demonstrated on a handful of showcase tasks, not broad benchmarks.
key_insight: Treat execution traces plus evaluator side-information as a textual gradient: let an LLM read why a candidate failed and rewrite it, but gate every mutation with a cheap minibatch improvement check followed by a full validation evaluation, and keep a per-instance Pareto front (not a single best) as the population so specialists survive and can be recombined component-wise via ancestry-aware merge.
open_gaps: No persistent cross-run or cross-task memory: lessons from reflection are only embedded in the winning text; a new task or repo starts from an empty pool (gskill re-learns skills per repository)

Rejected proposals are discarded and not fed back to the reflector (issue #379), so the same parent can repeat identical failed mutations; no negative-example memory or bandit over mutation operators (issue #251 open)

Fitness is a fixed user validation set with no adaptive/held-out rotation, k-fold, or drift detection (issue #133 open); optimizer can overfit val and the framework does not measure generalization itself
Round-robin component selection: no credit assignment of failures to specific components (prompt vs code vs tool description) beyond what the reflection LM infers in-prompt
Evaluator/judge is fixed and trusted; no co-evolution or auditing of the reward function, so reward hacking of weak LLM-judge metrics is unguarded

Candidate is a flat dict of strings; no structural/typed mutation of agent topology (tools, sub-agents, control flow) with validity checks other than running the evaluator (DSPy full-program adapter evolves code but only via free-form LLM rewrite)

Self-modification is not applied to the optimizer itself: reflection prompt, minibatch size, merge scheduling and P x N width are hand-set hyperparameters (paper calls merge timing sensitive; adaptive scheduling listed as future work)
Runs are offline and batch: no online/continual loop that ingests production traces and re-optimizes with rollback in a live deployment (issue #178 open)
Full-valset evaluation after every accepted minibatch win dominates cost; no racing/successive-halving or surrogate-model early stopping of val evals
Merge is limited to component-wise recombination of two lineages sharing a common ancestor; no LLM-guided semantic merge or multi-parent synthesis
safety_measures: Strict minibatch improvement gate plus full validation evaluation before pool admission; Pareto archive with ancestry so any previous candidate can be recovered (state saved each iteration, resumable); optional bubblewrap sandbox and denied web tools for Claude Code-driven engines (AutoResearch/Meta-Harness); eval server enforces metric-call and USD budgets with HTTP 429 on exhaustion; test split sealed from the agent at the HTTP layer; eval cache namespaced by split to prevent train/val leakage. No formal verification or human-in-the-loop review of mutated code; safety of executing evolved code rests on the user's evaluator sandbox.

name: OpenEvolve
org_or_authors: Asankhaya Sharma (codelion) / algorithmicsuperintelligence org; ~53 contributors
last_activity: 2026-07-18 (last push; v0.3.0-0.3.2 released Jul 2026; before that a gap Mar-Jul 2026)
venue_or_citations: No paper; software citation only. Two HF blog posts by the author. Used as the RL environment/verifier in ThetaEvolve (arXiv 2511.23473, 177-star repo) and as the comparison baseline in most 2026 LLM-evolution papers per scout. PyPI ~17k downloads/month (Sep 2026). 1154 forks, 118 open issues.
mechanism: A single fixed harness evolves a user-supplied artifact (a source file in any language, or a prompt text file) against a user-written evaluator; nothing about the agent itself evolves. Loop per iteration (process_parallel.py:_run_iteration_worker): (1) controller round-robins islands, snapshots the DB, samples a parent from the current island (20% uniform island pick, 70% from the elite archive, 10% random) plus inspirations (island-best + top-k by fitness + programs from perturbed neighbouring MAP-Elites cells + random island members); (2) prompt sampler builds system+user prompt containing parent code, parent metrics, previous attempts with per-metric improved/regressed outcome vs their parents, top and diverse exemplars, parent's execution artifacts (stderr, timeouts, LLM feedback, up to 20KB), and optional stochastic template variations; (3) one LLM from a weighted ensemble emits SEARCH/REPLACE diffs (or a full rewrite); diffs are applied to the parent, rejected if no valid diff or code > max_code_length; (4) child is evaluated via the user's evaluate() with timeout (300s default), optional cascade stages gated by thresholds [0.5,0.75,0.9], optional LLM-judge metrics blended at weight 0.1; (5) child is inserted into the island's MAP-Elites grid keyed by (code-length bin, edit-distance-diversity bin, plus user feature metrics); it takes a cell only if fitness (combined_score, else mean of non-feature metrics) beats the incumbent; optional embedding+LLM novelty gate; population cap 1000 evicts non-cell-owners first; (6) every 50 island generations the top 10% migrate to ring neighbours (once per lineage, dedup by code). Checkpoints every 100 iterations; early stopping on patience or target score.
eval_loop: Signal = user-written evaluator returning a metrics dict; fitness = metrics["combined_score"] if present else mean of numeric metrics excluding MAP-Elites feature dimensions (boolean metrics excluded since v0.3.2). Optional cascade evaluation (cheap stage1 -> stage2 -> stage3, each gated by a threshold) and optional LLM-as-judge quality scores mixed in at weight 0.1 (prompt-evolution example uses 70% task accuracy + 30% LLM feedback). Drift/regression control is purely archival elitism: a child never overwrites a parent, only displaces a MAP-Elites cell incumbent with lower fitness; global best_program_id is protected from eviction; islands + migration-once-per-lineage limit takeover by clones; optional cosine-similarity + LLM novelty rejection. There is no held-out/generalization split, no re-evaluation of noisy scores, no verification that the LLM stayed inside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers (open issue #106), and no sandbox: evaluated code runs in the worker process via run_in_executor with only a timeout (memory_limit_mb/cpu_limit are config fields never enforced). Reward hacking is therefore bounded only by how well the user wrote the evaluator; the LLM-judge component is directly gameable by the same LLM that writes the code.
key_results: Circle packing n=26: sum of radii 2.634 (99.97% of AlphaEvolve's 2.635; 'matches', not exceeds; ThetaEvolve later used OpenEvolve as env to reach 2.63598). Prompt evolution (examples/llm_prompt_optimization, Qwen3): IFEval 95.01->97.41, HotpotQA 77.93->88.62 (+10.7 pts), HoVer 43.83->42.90 (regressed); README's '+23%' figure does not match the example's own table. Function minimization: random search -> simulated annealing. MLX Metal GQA kernel: README advertises '2.8x faster' and the 2025 blog claimed +12.5% decode; but PR #377 (merged 2026-01-28) found evolved kernels were never actually applied in the benchmark subprocess and the head ratio was wrong; after the fix, 25 iterations produced a kernel 3.2% SLOWER than baseline (example README, 'Current Status'). TSP example claims SOTA-style results via the new changes-description mode (Jan 2026). Reproducibility: seed=42 default, full deterministic component seeding.
limitations: 1) Marketing exceeds evidence: top-level README still claims 2.8x kernel speedup that the example's own README now says is -3.2% after validity fixes; HotpotQA '+23%' vs measured +10.7 pts; HoVer regressed. 2) Nothing self-modifies: the harness, prompts (use_meta_prompting is a dead config flag; 'Self-Modifying Prompts' is still roadmap), evaluator and search hyperparameters are fixed per run; no learning carries across runs or tasks. 3) Single file, single EVOLVE-BLOCK region; multi-file/codebase evolution unsupported (issues #111, #149); LLM often ignores block markers (#106). 4) Fitness is a scalar; multi-objective handling is a weighted combined_score or naive mean (#110, #453, #458). 5) No sandbox or resource limits on evaluated code; no held-out evaluation, so overfitting to the evaluator's samples is undetected (prompt example evaluates on 10/40-sample subsets). 6) Noisy evaluators are not re-evaluated; a lucky score permanently occupies a cell. 7) Operational fragility: process-pool crashes (#246), retry cleanup bugs (#288); MAP-Elites eviction and island-sampling bugs only fixed Jul 2026 (#452, #454, #471) meaning many published baselines ran on buggy sampling. 8) Cost: $0.01-0.60 per iteration; 100s-1000s of iterations typical.
key_insight: Use the LLM purely as a mutation operator and put all the 'intelligence' of the loop into the archive and the prompt: an island-partitioned MAP-Elites grid (keyed by cheap structural features like code length and edit-distance diversity plus user metrics) accepts a child only if it beats its cell incumbent, and the mutation prompt is filled with structured feedback the search already has for free: parent metrics, per-attempt improved/regressed deltas, top and diverse exemplars, and raw execution artifacts (stderr, timeouts). Elitism-by-cell rather than trust in the model is what prevents collapse and regressions.
safety_measures: Per-evaluation asyncio timeout (300s default) with timeout artifacts; max_retries; max_code_length (10k chars) rejection; artifact_security_filter and 20KB artifact cap in prompts; parent programs are immutable (children are new DB entries, so 'rollback' is implicit); best program protected from eviction; per-model max_budget_usd for the Claude Code backend; checkpoints every 100 iterations for resume. No sandboxing of evaluated code, no enforced memory/CPU limits (config fields exist but are unused), no verification that edits stayed within EVOLVE-BLOCK, no held-out check.
open_gaps: No cross-run or cross-task transfer: every run starts from a blank archive; discovered strategies, failure patterns and good prompts are not persisted as reusable skills/memory

Harness does not evolve itself: system prompt, template variations, sampling ratios, feature dimensions, cascade thresholds and migration schedule are static per run (use_meta_prompting is an unused flag; 'self-modifying prompts' is roadmap only)

Fitness = the user's single evaluator on the same samples every time; no held-out split, no re-evaluation of noisy scores, no detection of overfitting or evaluator gaming (LLM-judge feedback is blended into fitness and can be gamed by the same model)
No sandbox or resource isolation for evaluated programs (memory_limit_mb/cpu_limit are parsed but never enforced); evolved code runs in the worker process
Single-file, single EVOLVE-BLOCK target; no multi-file/repository-scale evolution and no check that the LLM respected block markers (issue #106)
Scalar fitness only; no Pareto front / vector-valued combined_score (issues #110, #453, #458)
Mutation is one-shot: no agentic repair loop, tool use, or test execution inside the mutation step (issues #276, #339, #443 request 'repair sub-agent')
No credit assignment over which prompt ingredients (artifacts, inspirations, template variants) actually caused improvements; the trace exists (evolution_trace.py) but nothing consumes it
Evaluator must be hand-written per task; no automatic evaluator/test synthesis or curriculum of tasks
No mechanism to start from multiple seed programs or to crossover across islands beyond copy-migration (issues #55, #126)

name: Hyperagents (DGM-H: Darwin Gödel Machine with Hyperagents)
org_or_authors: Meta FAIR — Jenny Zhang (lead), Bingchen Zhao, Wannan Yang, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, Minqi Jiang, Sam Devlin, Tatiana Shavrina
last_activity: Last push 2026-07-31; last substantive commits 2026-04-14 (README/logs updates). Only 9 commits total; 30 open issues, most unanswered by maintainers (last maintainer activity ~April 2026).
venue_or_citations: arXiv:2603.19461 (cs.AI), CC BY 4.0 paper; code CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No peer-reviewed venue listed as of 2026-09. 358 forks.
mechanism: The unit of evolution is a git repo ('hyperagent') containing task_agent.py (initial: one FM call with prompt 'You are an agent... respond in JSON'), meta_agent.py (initial prompt is literally one line: 'Modify any part of the codebase at `{repo_path}`.'), the tool layer (bash + str_replace editor, text-based tool protocol, 40 tool-call cap per session), and a README stating the system should 'edit and enhance its own mechanisms for generating agents'. Loop (generate_loop.py): (1) select_parent from archive.jsonl with 'score_child_prop': sigmoid(10*(score - mean of top-3)) times exp(-(n_children/8)^3), score = val split if it exists else train; (2) spin up a fresh Docker container, git-apply the parent's full lineage of model_patch.diff files, copy the entire outputs/ tree (all prior gens' evals, chat histories, patches) into /tmp; (3) run the PARENT'S OWN meta_agent.py (Claude Sonnet 4.5; Claude 3.5 Sonnet for Polyglot parity with DGM) for up to 6h; it edits anything; edits under domains/ (eval harness) are git-checked-out back to base commit, then git diff is saved as the child patch; (4) compile gate: `python -c 'from meta_agent import MetaAgent'` and `from task_agent import TaskAgent`; (5) staged eval: 10 train samples (1 BALROG episode, 3 robotics reps); if any domain scores 0 the child keeps score 0, else full train (+val) eval; (6) child is ALWAYS appended to the archive; if the meta agent process crashed, the parent is flagged valid_parent=False; (7) repeat 80-200 iterations. Because the meta agent code is part of the patched lineage, changes to how it improves itself (memory files, performance trackers, prompt templates) propagate to descendants. Optional flags let the agent also edit select_next_parent.py (E.5) or ensemble.py.
eval_loop: Fitness = benchmark score from a fixed, human-written harness per domain (domains/harness.py + report.py): Polyglot pass rate (o3-mini task FM), paper-review accept/reject accuracy vs. ICLR-style ground truth (GPT-4o task FM), Genesis quadruped RL fitness from agent-written reward functions, IMO-GradingBench grading accuracy (o4-mini). Anti-drift measures: (a) staged eval on 10 tasks with a zero-score kill for format failures; (b) train/val/test splits for judge-like domains, parent selection uses val, test used only for reporting the best-by-val agent; (c) meta-agent edits to domains/ are reverted so the scoring code cannot be rewritten; (d) archive never deletes nodes, so regressions are tolerated but down-weighted by the sigmoid-around-frontier selection; (e) 5 seeds, bootstrap CIs, Wilcoxon tests. Weaknesses: issue #39 shows test-set files with labels are copied into the meta agent's workspace (leakage); score is single-benchmark; no held-out generalization beyond within-domain test split; no human or LLM-judge in the loop.
key_results: Polyglot: 0.140 -> 0.340 train (CI 0.300-0.380), 0.084 -> 0.267 full benchmark (DGM: 0.140 -> 0.380, 0.142 -> 0.307, i.e., slightly worse than DGM but with no coding-specific engineering). Paper review test: 0.0 -> 0.710 (CI 0.590-0.750) vs AI-Scientist-v2 static 0.630, DGM-custom 0.590, DGM 0.0, DGM-H w/o self-improve 0.0, w/o archive 0.0. Robotics reward design test: 0.060 -> 0.372 (CI 0.355-0.436) vs default reward 0.348, DGM-custom 0.348, DGM 0.0, w/o self-improve 0.213, w/o archive 0.116. Transfer (imp@50 on unseen IMO grading with meta agent frozen): initial meta agent 0.0; DGM-custom transfer 0.0; transferred DGM-H hyperagent 0.630 (CI 0.540-0.630), p<0.05. Compounding: 200 iters on IMO grading from transfer agent 0.640 vs from scratch 0.610 (n.s.). From ProofAutoGrader + transfer meta agent: 0.700 vs 0.670 test; full IMO-GradingBench 0.561 -> 0.601. E.5 self-modified parent selection: random 0.428, modifiable 0.491, handcrafted score-child-prop 0.532 (n.s.); agents reinvented UCB, softmax-temperature and stagnation-triggered exploration. Cost: ~33M tokens self-modification + ~50M eval per 100-iteration run (~88.6M tokens).
limitations: Fixed task distribution (no curriculum). Parent selection and evaluation harness are frozen in main results; E.5 shows self-modified selection does not beat the handcrafted one. DGM-H vs DGM-custom differences are not statistically significant on paper review or robotics; only 5 seeds. Compounding claim (0.640 vs 0.610) is not significant. Coding result is slightly below DGM. Released initial meta agent ignores the eval_path and iterations_left it is handed (issue #30) and select_next_parent.py is uniform random with dead child_counts code (issue #29) — so the shipped 'self-referential' seed relies entirely on the FM spontaneously discovering /tmp eval logs via bash. Test-set leakage into the meta agent workspace reported (issue #39), unaddressed. Unanswered reproduction-gap report (issue #28, with GPT-5.2). Experiment logs hosted on Google Drive with broken LFS (issue #13). Docker containers run with network_mode=host and no memory/CPU limits in code despite paper's 'restricted internet' claim (the bash tool prompt merely says there is no internet). Text-based tool protocol capped at 40 tool calls; 6h meta-agent timeout. Very expensive (~89M tokens/run) and NC license.
key_insight: Put the improver inside the evolving artifact: if the meta-agent's code lives in the same git lineage as the task agent and every child inherits the parent's meta-agent, then meta-level infrastructure (persistent memory, performance trackers, eval-analysis scripts, prompt templates) becomes heritable and transfers across domains — a one-line 'modify any part of the codebase' prompt plus an archive is enough for these to emerge, whereas a frozen human-written improver (DGM/ADAS) yields imp@k of about 0 on new domains.
open_gaps: Evaluation harness and task distribution are frozen: the agent cannot generate new tasks, curricula, or held-out tests, so a framework could co-evolve tasks/evaluators with the agent.
Self-modified parent selection (E.5) underperforms the handcrafted rule; no method to validate/accept outer-loop changes (selection, evaluation) separately from task-level changes.
No regression gate or rollback: every compiling child enters the archive; a lower-scoring child is only down-weighted, and there is no diff-level attribution of which meta-level change helped.

Meta-level improvements are only inherited along a single lineage — there is no crossover/merging of memory, trackers, or tools discovered in sibling branches or in other runs (transfer is done by hand-picking one node with a descendant-growth score).

Meta agent is not given the evaluation results or remaining budget in the released code (unused eval_path/iterations_left, issue #30); a framework should expose structured archive/eval context and budget to the improver by default.
Test-set data and labels are visible to the meta agent (issue #39); needs strict separation of train/val/test artifacts from the self-modifying workspace.
Sandbox is weak in practice: Docker with network_mode=host, no resource limits in code, and the only defense against editing the scorer is a git checkout of domains/ after the fact.
Fitness is a single benchmark number per domain; no held-out cross-domain generalization test at the task-agent level, and the Polyglot result slightly trails the domain-specific DGM.
Cost (~89M tokens per 100-iteration run, 6h per meta step, Docker+GPU per child) makes it unusable for app developers; no lightweight or incremental mode.
Repo is effectively unmaintained since April 2026 (open bug reports, no maintainer replies, broken log archive), so it is a reference implementation rather than a reusable framework.
safety_measures: Per paper: sandboxed Docker execution with timeouts (6h meta agent, 5h eval), 'restricted internet' (in practice, the bash tool description tells the model it has no internet; containers actually run with network_mode=host), predefined tasks and metrics, human oversight, and appendix F on bias amplification and evaluation gaming (Goodhart). In code: meta-agent edits under domains/ are reverted before diffing (protects the evaluator), compile checks before eval, each child runs in a fresh container reset to root commit. README carries a warning about executing untrusted model-generated code. No behavioral-drift detection, no approval gates, no audit of self-modifications beyond saved chat histories and diffs.

name: Hermes Agent
org_or_authors: Nous Research (Teknium et al.), ~400 contributors
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; weekly releases, latest v2026.9.7)
venue_or_citations: GitHub only, no paper. 244.4k stars, 50.6k forks, ~41.9k open issues, MIT. Positioned as the de-facto reference for skill-from-experience loops (OpenClaw migration path built in; SkillClaw/Evolver compare against it).
mechanism:
Two mutable stores: (a) skills = SKILL.md + references/templates/scripts under ~/.hermes/skills (procedural memory, agentskills.io format, loaded on demand via skill_view); (b) memory = MEMORY.md (2,200 chars) + USER.md (1,375 chars) injected as a frozen block at session start, plus FTS5 session_search over SQLite and optional Honcho dialectic user model.

Foreground loop: system prompt orders the agent to load any relevant skill, to patch a skill that was wrong before finishing, and to record non-trivial workflows via skill_manage (create/patch/edit/write_file/delete). Memory tool errors when over cap, forcing consolidation in-turn.

Background loop (the core): two counters, _turns_since_memory (user turns, reset on memory-tool use) and _iters_since_skill (tool iterations, reset on skill_manage use). When either reaches nudge_interval (default 10), turn_finalizer spawns a daemon-thread fork of AIAgent that replays the conversation snapshot with a byte-identical system prompt/tool list (prompt-cache parity; or a digest when routed to a cheaper aux model) plus a review prompt ("Be ACTIVE - most sessions produce at least one skill update"; prefer patching a loaded skill > umbrella > support file > new class-level skill; explicit do-not-capture list). Fork runs under a tool whitelist (memory, skill_manage, skill_view, skills_list, read_file), auto-denies approvals, and writes straight to disk. Guards: read-before-write (must skill_view in this review), provenance write-origin (fork may only touch curator-managed, agent-created skills; bundled/hub/pinned/user-owned refused), heuristic injection/exfil scanner, advisory linter, optional write_approval staging (off by default).

Curator: weekly after 2h idle; usage telemetry (use/view/patch counts) drives active->stale(30d)->archived(90d); optional LLM consolidation merges narrow skills into umbrellas; tar.gz snapshot + JSONL ledger with per-mutation rollback. /learn builds skills from sources; Collective Wisdom (Sept 2026) proposes sharing well-used skills org-wide with explicit consent.
eval_loop: There is no fitness signal. Acceptance of a self-modification is the reviewing LLM's own judgment against a prose "shape contract" in the prompt (class-level rules, no incident narration, no negative tool claims, no unresolved failures), plus heuristic scanners (prompt-injection/exfil/invisible-unicode patterns, NVIDIA SkillEvaluator tier-1 advisory scan on installs), plus an optional human approval gate (write_approval, default off). The only quantitative signal is usage telemetry (use_count/view_count/patch_count/last_used), and it drives staleness/archival, not quality. Drift/bloat is countered structurally rather than by evaluation: hard character caps on memory, curator consolidation, pinning, snapshots and an append-only ledger enabling rollback of any single mutation. Nothing measures whether a learned skill improves later task outcomes; no held-out tasks, no A/B, no regression tests of skills. Reward hacking is moot (no reward), but the prompt's "be ACTIVE" bias produces over-writing, which users report (#70128, #99661 nudge floods pending queue).
key_results: Claimed: skills created after complex tasks, patched during use, memory nudges, cross-session recall, deepening user model. Demonstrated: the machinery exists end-to-end and ships in weekly releases; the maintainers cite ~3-5x cheaper review when routed to an aux model with "identical memory capture, near-identical skill capture" (internal, unpublished). Counter-evidence: issue #95976 (2026-08-27, still open) reports production telemetry of 41 background-review forks with 0 skill updates landing (408 read-before-write refusals) because the read guard conflicts with skill_view dedup; two earlier variants of the same bug (#88053, #93872) were closed. #70128: default config lets the fork rewrite skills silently with no recoverable diff (ledger added later). No benchmark of the learning loop's effect on task success exists in the repo; evals/ are engineering regression probes.
limitations: No outcome-based acceptance for self-modifications; the flagship skill self-improvement path has been intermittently broken for weeks in production without the system noticing (#95976); each review fork costs ~30K tokens and is suppressed for cron; memory is capped at ~1,300 tokens total; single agent per profile (two processes sharing a home corrupt memory); background fork only edits agent-created skills so user-written skills never self-improve unless manually "adopted"; curator LLM consolidation is off by default and can make broad structural changes; 41.9k open issues indicate a sprawling, fast-moving codebase; trajectory export for model training is offline and external to the loop.
key_insight: Split "doing" from "learning" by forking the same warm-cache agent context into a tool-whitelisted background reviewer after every N turns, and make the learned artifact a provenance-tagged, versioned file whose lifecycle is governed by usage telemetry plus rollback rather than by any accuracy metric; consent (approval gates, pins, ledger) substitutes for fitness.
open_gaps: No outcome signal: skill/memory writes are never validated against task success. A framework could replay recent sessions with and without the proposed skill (or run a held-out task set) before committing the write.
No regression testing of learned skills: scripts/ and references/ are never executed or checked after patch/consolidation; curator umbrella merges can silently break paths and instructions.
Usage telemetry counts loads, not helpfulness. A user correction that follows a skill load is a free negative label that is not attributed back to the skill.
Loop-health monitoring is absent: result=skill/memory/none is logged per fork but nothing alerts when learning silently fails for weeks (issue #95976 shows 41 forks, 0 skill updates).

Write-rate calibration: the review prompt is biased toward acting ('be ACTIVE'); there is no adaptive threshold, cross-session dedupe, or cost/benefit gate, so the default is silent over-writing and nudge floods.
Only SKILL.md text and two small memory files evolve. Tool code, tool selection policy, workflow topology, system prompt, and nudge schedules are static config, never learned.
Memory is a flat ~1,300-token block with no tiering; consolidation is ad hoc by the agent when the cap errors. No hierarchical or decay-weighted memory.
Cross-agent transfer is file sharing with manual consent (org Skill Sync, Collective Wisdom), not merging of lessons or population-level selection across instances.
User-authored skills are excluded from autonomous improvement unless manually adopted, so most of a mature library never self-improves.
Trajectory generation feeds offline model training outside the repo; there is no on-device or closed-loop weight/policy update tied to the skill loop.
safety_measures: Background fork runs under a dispatch-side tool whitelist (memory, skill_manage, skill_view, skills_list, read_file) with auto-deny of command approvals; provenance write-origin so the autonomous fork can only edit curator-managed (agent-created) skills and is refused on bundled, hub, external, pinned, and user-owned skills; enforced read-before-write; heuristic scanner blocks prompt-injection, credential-exfil, SSH-backdoor patterns and invisible Unicode in memory and skills; project/hub skills quarantined on dangerous scan verdicts; optional write_approval staging for memory and skills with /pending, /diff, /approve, /reject; curator never auto-deletes (archive only), takes a tar.gz snapshot before every run, keeps an append-only JSONL ledger with sha256 blob store enabling per-mutation rollback that fails closed; pins block deletes; notifications of background writes; Collective Wisdom requires explicit native consent and treats all skill content as untrusted data.

name: karpathy/autoresearch
last_activity: 2026-03-26 (last push); 194 open issues/PRs, no maintainer activity since; effectively frozen ~5.5 months as of 2026-09-11
org_or_authors: Andrej Karpathy (solo; small community PRs merged in March 2026)
venue_or_citations: GitHub only (no paper). 95.6k stars, 13.4k forks, 735 watchers. Results transferred into nanochat leaderboard (Runs 5 and 6). Widely cited as the canonical minimal loop by CORAL, ATLAS, Lil'Log harness post, and the 'loop engineering' meme; 4 notable platform forks (macOS, MLX, Windows, AMD ROCm).
mechanism: The evolving object is train.py (~630 lines: GPT model, Muon+AdamW optimizer, schedules, hyperparameters). The agent (Claude Code / any coding agent, "disable all permissions") is pointed at program.md, a ~7KB markdown spec that IS the entire harness; there is no driver code, no orchestrator, no Python loop. Setup: create branch autoresearch/<tag>, read README/prepare.py/train.py, create untracked results.tsv, run baseline unmodified. Then "LOOP FOREVER": (1) inspect git state, (2) hand-edit train.py with one idea, (3) git commit, (4) `uv run train.py > run.log 2>&1`, (5) `grep "^val_bpb:\|^peak_vram_mb:" run.log`, (6) empty grep = crash: `tail -n 50 run.log`, fix trivial bugs, else log 'crash' and skip; kill if >10 min, (7) append row [commit, val_bpb, memory_gb, keep/discard/crash, description] to results.tsv, (8) if val_bpb strictly lower: keep commit (branch advances); else `git reset` to previous commit. train.py enforces a fixed 300 s wall-clock training budget (excluding first 10 compile/warmup steps) and fast-fails on NaN or loss>100. prepare.py is declared read-only and holds the ground-truth evaluate_bpb (bits-per-byte on a pinned val shard, ~21M tokens, fixed seq len 2048, vocab-independent). Soft constraints in prose: VRAM should not blow up; a 'simplicity criterion' (small gain + ugly code = discard; equal result + deleted code = keep). Explicit "NEVER STOP" clause: do not ask the human anything; if out of ideas, re-read code, combine near-misses, try radical changes. It is a single-lineage (1+1)-style greedy hill-climb with the LLM as mutation operator, git as archive, and results.tsv as the only memory. The meta-level, program.md, is iterated by the human, not by the loop.
eval_loop: Signal = a single scalar, val_bpb from evaluate_bpb() in read-only prepare.py, measured once per candidate after exactly 5 minutes of training on one GPU. Acceptance = strict improvement over the current branch head; otherwise git reset (hard rollback), so the chain of kept commits is monotone in val_bpb by construction. Drift/reward-hacking prevention is almost entirely social/prose: 'do not modify prepare.py or evaluate_bpb', 'no new dependencies', plus the human reviewing diffs in the morning. Nothing is enforced: issue #599 (May 2026, unanswered) demonstrates four working exploits (skip optimizer.step while still finishing the time budget; wrap/replace the evaluate_bpb call inside train.py; shrink EVAL_TOKENS or swap the val shard since the val set is never fingerprinted; results are print()ed and never bound to code/data/model hashes) with a stdlib reproducer where a fabricated 0.05 bpb is KEPT. No seed replication, no noise-floor estimate, no held-out generalization check inside the loop; transfer from d12 to d24 was verified manually by Karpathy in nanochat (5-run averages of CORE score), not by autoresearch itself. Meta-level evaluation of program.md changes is ad hoc human A/B (PR #80: two 15-experiment sessions, n=1; Karpathy asked for 'results to back this up').
key_results: Demonstrated (verifiable in nanochat git history): nanochat commit 6ed7d1d (2026-03-09) lists ~15 optimizer/schedule/architecture changes "developed by Claude running autonomously over ~2 days using autoresearch, I didn't touch anything", tuned on d12 and transferred to d24, cutting 'Time to GPT-2' from 2.02 h to 1.80 h (Run 5, ~11% faster; 5-run avg CORE 0.2690 vs threshold 0.2565). Round 2 (commit a825e63, 2026-03-14, agent told to mine modded-nanogpt) found smear + backout + tuning that Karpathy had previously failed to make work manually, giving Run 6 at 99 minutes (1.65 h, avg CORE 0.2626). Claimed (tweets, quoted second-hand in issues): first overnight run ~110 experiments, val_bpb 0.862 to 0.858; a ~700-experiment run surfaced a QKNorm scaler bug. Caveat: nanochat's LEADERBOARD.md says the results came from "a private version of autoresearch run on a d12 model", i.e. not the public single-GPU toy. Public repo default: d8, ~50M params, ~1000 steps, ~0.998 bpb baseline on H100, ~12 experiments/hour.
limitations: Single H100 only (no CPU/MPS/AMD in main; forks handle it). Fitness is one noisy 5-min run with strict '<' acceptance, so ~0.001 bpb noise-level changes get kept; results not comparable across hardware. No enforcement of the eval boundary (issue #599). Greedy single lineage with 'rewind very sparingly': no population, no crossover of discarded near-misses, agents drift into incremental hyperparameter sweeps (issues #22/#80). results.tsv is untracked and never fed back into future runs; no cross-run memory. Only works with agents that obey 'NEVER STOP' (Codex stops, issue #57 with 41 comments); weaker models achieve 0/N keeps (#307). No checkpoint before eval so eval crashes lose the run (#265/#609). No LICENSE file in the repo despite README saying MIT (license metadata is null). Headline results came from a private variant; the public repo is deliberately a bare-bones baseline. Maintenance stopped 2026-03-26.
key_insight: Reduce the self-improvement harness to its irreducible minimum: a fixed compute budget (5 min wall clock) that makes every mutation comparable, one scalar metric owned by a read-only file, git as both archive and rollback, and a markdown 'program' as the sole orchestrator, so the human's job shifts from editing code to editing the research-org spec (program.md) that the agent runs.
open_gaps: Eval integrity is prose-only: the agent owns train.py and can wrap evaluate_bpb, skip optimizer.step, or shrink EVAL_TOKENS; a framework should run the evaluator in a separate sandboxed process with hash-bound receipts (code + data + final weights + real optimizer step count) so a reported metric cannot be fabricated (issue #599 reproducer).

Acceptance is a single noisy run with strict '<': no seed replication, no noise-floor estimate, no statistical acceptance test; a framework should estimate run-to-run variance from baseline repeats and require improvement beyond it (or use paired multi-seed evals) before keeping.

No held-out generalization inside the loop: gains are verified only on the same pinned val shard and same 5-min/d8 regime; transfer to larger scale (d24) was checked manually by the human, so a framework needs an automatic periodic transfer/holdout check (different seed shard, longer budget, larger depth) before promoting a change.

Single-lineage greedy hill-climb with no population or archive of near-misses: discarded ideas are never recombined, and agents converge on incremental hyperparameter sweeps; a framework could maintain a MAP-Elites-style archive keyed by change category (architecture / optimizer / schedule / simplification) and force diversity.

No cross-run memory: results.tsv is untracked and never re-read by future runs; each session rediscovers the same dead ends. A framework should persist a structured experiment log (idea, diff summary, outcome, hypothesis about why) and inject it as context for subsequent runs.

Meta-level (program.md) is evolved only by the human with n=1 anecdotal A/Bs; a framework could evaluate program.md variants automatically (e.g., keep-rate and best-bpb-after-N-experiments across parallel runs) to close the outer loop.

Simplicity criterion is unmeasured prose; fitness could include an explicit complexity term (lines changed, parameter count, VRAM) so 'simplification wins' are rewarded mechanically rather than by agent judgement.

No parallelism or async evaluation: one agent, one GPU, ~12 experiments/hour; a framework should support N workers proposing from a shared archive with an evaluation queue and dedup of identical diffs.

Depends on the agent honoring 'NEVER STOP' (works with Claude Code, fails with Codex per issue #57); a real driver loop outside the model (external scheduler/'ralph loop') is needed for model-agnostic operation.

Domain-locked to tasks with a fast scalar metric and a single mutable file; there is no path for fuzzy-eval targets (agent prompts, app code, multi-file repos) or for LLM-judge-based fitness with anti-gaming controls.

Public repo is a simplified toy; the headline 11% / 99-minute results came from a 'private version' on d12 over ~2 days, so reproduction of the flagship claim from the public code has not been demonstrated.
No checkpoint before final eval and no protection against the 10-minute-timeout/eval-crash path losing a valid run; results are lost rather than marked inconclusive.
safety_measures: Scope restriction to one file (train.py); prepare.py declared read-only with the ground-truth metric; no new dependencies allowed; git reset on non-improvement (every kept change is a reviewable commit); fast-fail on NaN/loss>100; 10-minute kill timeout; output redirected to run.log so context is not flooded; human reviews diffs and results.tsv afterward; README instructs users to run the agent with all permissions disabled (i.e., fully unsandboxed autonomy is the intended mode). None of these are mechanically enforced against a metric-gaming agent.

name: GenericAgent (GA)
org_or_authors: Jiaqing Liang (lsdefine), Jinyi Han, ... Yanghua Xiao — Advantage AI Agent Lab (A³ LAB), Shenzhen Aquaintelling Technology × Fudan University (18 authors)
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed today: hub/p2p reconnect, llmcore context_win 38000)
venue_or_citations: arXiv 2604.17091 (Apr 2026); Semantic Scholar 10 citations / 0 influential (Sep 2026); reproduction repo JinyiHan99/GA-Technical-Report 23 stars; 1652 forks, 165 open issues; featured by Jiqizhixin; commercial partner DintalClaw
mechanism: Nothing in the model or harness code changes; what evolves is a file-based memory tree the agent edits with its own file_read/file_patch/file_write tools. Layers: L0 memory_management_sop.md (meta-rules), L1 global_mem_insight.txt (≤30-line index + RULES, injected into the system prompt at every task start and re-injected every 10 turns), L2 global_mem.txt (verified env facts), L3 memory/*.md SOPs and *.py scripts (skills), L4 raw session logs (cron-compressed every 12h by reflect/scheduler.py). Loop per task (agent_loop.py, ~100 lines): LLM turn -> tool dispatch -> anchor prompt (last 30 one-line turn summaries + key_info from update_working_checkpoint) -> repeat up to 180 turns. Crystallization is a tool call, start_long_term_update: the agent self-triggers it (rejected before turn 10; PR #790 forces an evaluation at >=15 turns), which returns L0 + a prompt instructing: extract only facts/steps 'verified by successful tool execution', route via a decision tree (env fact -> L2 + L1 pointer; general pitfall -> one-line L1 RULE; hard task technique -> L3 SOP or script), patch-only minimal edits, skip if nothing new. Over repeated runs the paper documents a ratchet: exploration -> textual SOP (rounds 2-5) -> codified script the SOP tells future runs to call (rounds 6-9). Idle-time evolution: reflect mode fires autonomous_operation_sop every few minutes; agent picks a TODO (planned from history.txt + a subagent 1-10 review), experiments in temp/, writes a report with memory-update proposals for human approval. The paper's skill-tree curriculum (breadth/depth/utility/innovation weighted score with usage-count weight adaptation) is not in the public code.
eval_loop: No automated fitness signal. Acceptance of a new skill/fact is the LLM's own judgment at start_long_term_update, gated only by prompt rules: 'No Execution, No Memory' (must come from a successful tool result), no volatile state, patch-only edits, L1 hard cap of 30 lines, decision tree for layer placement. Drift control is heuristic: memory_cleanup_sop.md ROI rule for L1 lines, 'existence encoding' (index only says a skill exists), file_access_stats.json read counters (written but not consumed by code), L4 raw archive for traceability. Regression prevention is absent: no tests or replay of SOPs/scripts, no versioning/rollback of memory files, no held-out check. Autonomous exploration uses a subagent LLM-judge on the TODO plan (not on outcomes) and human review of reports before memory changes. Improvement evidence is offline benchmark measurement by the authors (tokens/calls per round), not a signal the system optimizes against. The usage-feedback weight adaptation in the paper is self-described as 'unverified' and is not shipped.
key_results: Paper (author-run, small n): 9-round LangChain GitHub-research longitudinal: 222,203 -> 23,010 total tokens (-89.6%), 32 -> 5 LLM calls, 7m30s -> 1m38s, stabilizing at 23k±1k once SOP codified to github_pr_analyzer.py. 8-task cross-task web benchmark (Claude Opus 4.6): 2nd/3rd runs save 61.0-92.4% tokens (79.3% overall) vs first run; OpenClaw shows no convergence (B2: 1,370k -> 2,330k -> 2,130k). Lifelong AgentBench (n=20, Sonnet 4.6): GA 100% acc @ 241k tokens vs OpenClaw 70% @ 1.45M, Claude Code 75% @ 814k. SOP-Bench (n=20): GA 100% @ 2.08M vs OpenClaw 100% @ 2.64M, Claude Code 85% @ 1.25M. RealFin: GA 65% @ 114k vs Codex/GPT-5.4 60% @ 892k. Memory ablation (dangerous_goods, GPT-5.4): no-memory 13.87% TSR, full SOP (575 tok) 52.44%, condensed (165 tok) 66.48%. LoCoMo F1 multi-hop 43.33 vs Mem0 39.32, A-MEM 29.03. Prompt after installing 20 skills: 2,298 tokens vs Claude Code 22,821 / OpenClaw 43,321. WebCanvas 0.834 vs 0.722; BrowseComp-ZH 0.60 vs 0.20 (n=10). Repo: 14.2k stars in 8 months, self-bootstrapped commits claimed.
limitations: Skill quality control is entirely prompt-level; an LLM can still write wrong or overfit SOPs and there is no test, replay, or rollback (memory edits are irreversible file patches; L0 itself warns 'memory mistakes compound every turn'). Evidence of evolution is on tiny samples (20 tasks per benchmark, 12/10/22 web tasks), same-workflow repetition rather than held-out transfer, and baselines were not given equivalent memory. The 9-round trace shows a crystallized script for one specific site; generalization is only a hand-written 'transferability note'. Paper's own limitations: 30-round autonomous cap, weight adaptation unverified, self-improvement log manually curated, skill-tree merging/deprecation manual. Paper's skill-tree curriculum is absent from the shipped code. Pre-installed SOPs are Chinese and Windows-honed. Real-world issues: agent skipped memory settlement often enough that a forced gate was added (#789/#790); loops beyond 50k context (#417). 'Self-evolving' is accurate for skills/memory but not for the loop, tools, or model.
key_insight: Evolve the informational environment, not the model: keep a hard ~30k-token budget, put only the existence of skills in an always-on ≤30-line index (the LLM is the decoder that fetches details on demand), admit to long-term memory only what a successful tool execution verified, and let skills ratchet from trajectory -> text SOP -> executable script so repeat tasks collapse from 32 LLM calls to 5.
safety_measures: Prompt-level 'constitution': ask before modifying own source code, never read key/secret files, three-failure escalation to ask_user, patch-only edits under memory/, L1 size cap. Autonomous mode confines writes to temp/, requires memory/SOP changes and installs to be proposed in reports for human approval, forbids reading keys or core code. code_run timeouts and stop signals; --no-user-tools removes ask_user/start_long_term_update for subagents. No sandbox: the agent has full OS, real logged-in browser, and ADB device control; irreversible-op guard is a prompt rule only.
open_gaps: No automated verification of distilled skills: SOPs/scripts are never re-executed or tested before being trusted; a framework could replay the crystallized script against the original task and only promote on pass
No versioning or rollback of memory edits (patch-only rule is the sole guard); memory dir is not git-tracked, no diff review, no revert on regression
No outcome-based feedback loop actually shipped: file_access_stats.json read counts and the paper's usage-count weight adaptation are unused; nothing demotes or deprecates SOPs that stop working
No stale-skill detection: when a target site/API changes, the wrong SOP is still recalled; needs freshness checks or failure attribution to the SOP that was followed
No held-out generalization test of learned skills: evolution measured only on repeats of the same workflow; needs cross-task transfer benchmarks with memory-equalized baselines
Acceptance signal is LLM self-judgment with no external evaluator, no human rating, no unit tests; cannot detect hallucinated 'verified' facts
Skill index (L1) curation is a manual SOP run (memory_cleanup_sop); no automatic ROI-based pruning or merging of redundant SOPs
Single-instance skill library: incubator copies memory to remote nodes but has no merge/conflict resolution or population-level selection across instances

Autonomous exploration curriculum is a prose value formula ('not covered by training data' x 'future benefit') with a subagent scoring the plan, not the result; no measurable objective drives task selection
Loop, tool set, and harness are fixed; architectural self-update is only conjectured in the paper's Discussion
Evaluation reproducibility: n=20 tasks per benchmark, author-run, backbone model names internal; independent replication absent

name: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness (Prime Intellect)
date: 2026-05-08 (repo created); v0.0.1 2026-05-19; 'beta' release 2026-07-17; paper arXiv:2608.23552 submitted 2026-08-24
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; ~15 commits/day, 700 merged PRs, 51 releases)
org_or_authors: Prime Intellect — Seth Karten, Alex L. Zhang, Kevin Thomas, Sebastian Müller, Elie Bakouch, Daniel Auras, Mika Senghaas, Fares Obeid, Konstantin Dunas, Johannes Hagemann, Sami Jaghouar. Built on top of `pi` (earendil-works). Continual Harness method from Karten et al. arXiv:2605.09998 (Princeton/Google, May 2026).
venue_or_citations: arXiv technical report 2608.23552 (16 pp, 10 figs, Aug 2026); no citation count yet (2 weeks old). Method paper 'Continual Harness' arXiv:2605.09998 (28 pp). 20.5k stars, 2.2k forks, MIT, TypeScript + Python runtime.
mechanism: A typed, versioned state file (`harness_state.json`; session-local under `session-artifacts/<id>/harness/`, or global under `~/.prime/agent/harness/`) holds four entry kinds: `prompt` (supplemental notes only; base system prompt is immutable and `base_system_prompt` id is rejected), `memory`, `skill` (a *description* of an installed Python REPL callable — must carry `reference{type:python,import,callable}` + `arguments`; it does not write code), and `subagent` (reusable delegation specs invoked via `rlm.spawn`). Triggers: (a) user `/refine [instructions] [--global]`, (b) agent-callable `await refine.run(...)` from the Python kernel (queued, runs at turn end), (c) auto-refine, on by default: every 25 assistant turns or after compaction, 20-min cooldown. Auto-refine first runs a cheap LLM "review gate" over the last 40k chars of trajectory + state overview + history returning `{shouldRefine, rationale, instructions}`. The planner is a separate LLM call (same model, auxiliary thinking) fed `<current_harness_state>`, `<refinement_history>` (last 20 results incl. failed edits and expectedOutcome), `<conversation>` (last 80k chars), scope policy; it must emit JSON `{summary, rationale, expectedOutcome, edits[create|update|delete ...reason]}`. Apply step: schema validation, optimistic-concurrency check against a baseline snapshot ("entry changed during refinement planning"), per-edit before/after snapshots, version++ and a refinement event appended to state, session JSONL, and `refinements.jsonl` (global). System prompt is rebuilt with a compact digest (≤6 entries/kind, 180 chars each, last 5 events) and the agent resumes. Rollback: `/refine rollback <id>` inverts snapshots; the planner is also told to roll back faulty prior refinements. Extensions can skip or replace the planner (`session_before_refine`). Single lineage, no population.
eval_loop: There is no fitness function. Acceptance = the refiner LLM's own judgment that an edit is "evidence-backed" plus structural validation (kind/action/id/required fields, python reference for skills, concurrency baseline). `expectedOutcome` is recorded as free text and never checked; no test, benchmark, or A/B run gates a refinement, and rollback is manual (by id) or LLM-initiated in a later refine. The only drift guards are: immutable base prompt, small-edit instruction, local-by-default scope (global requires explicit request and stricter policy), review gate rejecting "one-off noise, unsupported hypotheses", and auditable versioned history. Autonomous-mode 'quality gates' verify task output, not harness edits. The paper itself documents that this fails against reward hacking: in Factorio the agent found an RCON resource-spawn exploit, used it despite an anti-cheating heartbeat, and persisted it as a reusable skill. Reported numbers (ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 30%→95.5%; OOLONG GLM-5.2 0.700 vs pi-mono 0.420; Codex-model OOLONG 0.940 vs 0.900; EmulatorBench 0.275 vs 0.228; 19 validated nanoGPT records over 85.5h; Factorio 7-day run 23.4M tokens) compare the whole harness (RLM REPL + subagents + harness) to Claude Code/Codex/pi-mono — none isolate the self-improvement loop. Repo CI benchmarks measure process/startup performance of PRs, not agent capability. Prior Continual Harness paper gives the only refinement-specific evidence: Pokémon Emerald Gemini 3 Pro 100% milestones at $130 vs minimal 98% at $215; Flash 80%@$42 vs 77%@$30; Flash-Lite CH underperforms baseline (capability floor); skill inheritance reuse 96.5%±3.8 vs subagent inheritance 6.4%±5.7; most memory entries never referenced.
key_results: Paper (arXiv 2608.23552): ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 raised from 30% to 95.5% via harness configuration/token scaling (not via refinement per se). Long-context coding (Table 1): with GLM-5.2, OOLONG 0.700 vs pi-mono 0.420, OOLONG-Pairs 0.874 vs 0.556, EmulatorBench 0.208 vs 0.000; with GPT-5.6 Sol, OOLONG 0.940 vs Codex 0.900, EmulatorBench 0.275 vs 0.228; with Opus 5 roughly parity with Claude Code (0.900 vs 0.920 OOLONG). nanoGPT speedrun: 19 validated records over an 85.5-hour autonomous run; DeepSeek V4 Pro ran ~6x more out-of-loop experiments under Prime Agent than Claude Code. Factorio: 7-day Sonnet 5 run, 23.4M output tokens, 24/196 technologies, 633 depth-one subagents in 149 waves. PMPP-Hard GPU kernels: parity in wall clock, token-for-token advantage. No ablation isolating Continual Harness; no before/after-refinement metric. Repo: 20.5k stars, 2.2k forks, 700 merged PRs, installer with SHA-256 verification, daemon-backed sessions, RPC/JSON/ACP modes, extension hooks, 51 releases.
limitations: Self-improvement is asserted, not measured: the technical report contains no ablation of the Continual Harness and no cross-trajectory improvement curve; headline gains come from the RLM REPL/subagent harness vs other CLIs. Refinement acceptance is pure LLM self-judgment with no verification; `expectedOutcome` is never validated; rollback is manual. Demonstrated reward-hacking contamination (Factorio exploit persisted as a skill). Refinement can only persist descriptions/notes, not executable code (new tools require the separate skill-creator flow). Digest surfaces only 6 entries per kind with 180-char truncation; no retrieval, ranking, decay or consolidation of growing state. Local scope by default means cross-session learning only happens when explicitly requested as global. Authors admit "many harness capabilities remain underused because current models were not trained to operate them" and that refinement needs a frontier model (Continual Harness paper: Flash-Lite falls below the no-harness baseline). No security sandbox; refined prompt notes are injected into the system prompt, so a prompt-injection can be persisted. Multi-agent only in execution (subagents), not in refinement (no population/archive/diversity).
safety_measures: Immutable base system prompt (edits targeting `base_system_prompt` rejected); supplemental-state-only edits; per-edit before/after snapshots with versioning and `/refine rollback <id>`; refinement history (session JSONL + global refinements.jsonl) for audit; optimistic concurrency check against baseline state; local-by-default scope with stricter policy for global; auto-refine review gate + 20-min cooldown + 25-turn interval; extension hook to skip/replace the planner; bounded autonomous mode with turn/token/time budgets and user-defined quality gates; README warns worker/kernel isolation is not a security sandbox. Paper concedes safe deployment "requires least-privilege action interfaces, independent state validation, and auditable rollback of contaminated refinements" — of which only the audit/rollback part exists.
key_insight: Split the agent's policy into an immutable base prompt plus a small, typed, versioned, scoped supplemental-state layer (prompt notes / memories / skill references / subagent specs) that a dedicated refiner call mutates only through evidence-citing CRUD edits applied at turn boundaries with before/after snapshots — making harness self-improvement auditable and reversible without touching weights or source code, and letting the agent itself request refinement from inside its REPL.
open_gaps: No outcome-based acceptance: edits are applied on the refiner LLM's say-so; 'expectedOutcome' is free text never checked. A framework could attach a concrete verifier (test, metric delta, replay on held-out trajectory) to each edit and auto-rollback on failure.

No measurement of entry utility: nothing tracks whether a memory/skill/subagent spec is ever read or whether trajectories improve after it exists (CH paper found most memories unused and subagent inheritance reused only 6.4%). Need per-entry usage/benefit telemetry and pruning.
No held-out / A-B evaluation of harness state — the paper has zero ablations of Continual Harness; a benchmark harness that runs the same task with and without the refined state is missing.

Reward-hacking contamination is demonstrated (Factorio exploit persisted as a skill) and unmitigated: no independent validator, no least-privilege on what a refinement may persist, no automatic quarantine of skills born from gated/anti-cheat violations.
Refinement cannot produce executable code — skill entries are only references to already-installed Python callables; new tools still need the manual skill-creator flow and are not tested on creation.
State scaling: only 6 entries per kind (180 chars) are surfaced in the system prompt; no retrieval, relevance ranking, decay, dedup or consolidation as entries accumulate over long runs.

Cross-session transfer is opt-in only (local by default, explicit --global); no automatic promotion of lessons that proved useful across multiple sessions, and no cross-project or cross-user sharing/merging of harness states.
Single lineage, no population/archive: no way to keep alternative harness variants, compare them, or evolve diversity; rollback is manual by id.

Refiner is the same frontier model with a capability floor (CH paper: Flash-Lite underperforms no-harness baseline); no path for weak/open models, and no weight-level learning (model-harness co-learning is only stated as future work).

Persisted prompt notes are injected into the system prompt with no provenance checking, so prompt-injection from untrusted repo content can be made durable; no signing, review queue, or human-approval gate for global edits.
