name: ShinkaEvolve
org_or_authors: Sakana AI — Robert Tjarko Lange, Yuki Imajuku, Edoardo Cetin
date: 2025-09-17 (repo created and arXiv v1 same day)
last_activity: 2026-08-21 (last push: Anthropic response-parsing fix PR #188); last PyPI release v0.0.7 on 2026-06-02; 27 contributors
venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted per README Jan-2026 note); arXiv 2509.19349; ~142 citations per scout (could not verify — Semantic Scholar rate-limited); 278 forks
mechanism: Per generation (async runner overlaps proposal and evaluation): (1) Pick an island, then a parent from its archive by weighted sampling — w_i = sigmoid(lambda*(F_i - median F)) * 1/(1+#children) — or power-law-over-rank / beam search; with prob exploitation_ratio draw from the global archive. Add 1 archive + 1 top-k "inspiration" program to context. (2) An AsymmetricUCB bandit (cost-aware blend) picks which LLM mutates; patch type sampled (diff 0.6 / full rewrite 0.3 / crossover 0.1). Prompt holds parent code, inspirations, evaluator text feedback, and every meta_rec_interval generations a 3-stage LLM meta-review (per-program summaries -> global insights scratchpad -> <=5 recommendations) is appended. Optionally the system prompt itself is sampled from an evolved prompt archive (prompt fitness = mean percentile rank of its correct children; UCB+epsilon sampling; diff/full prompt mutations). (3) Patch applied only inside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers; malformed patches are resampled. (4) Novelty rejection: embed mutable code, cosine-compare to island population; if max sim > eta (0.95 paper / 0.99 default) an optional LLM judge rules NOVEL/NOT_NOVEL, else reject and resample parent up to 3 times before paying for evaluation. (5) Run user evaluate.py -> combined_score, correct flag, public/private metrics, text_feedback; persist to SQLite. (6) Bandit reward = exp(beta*max(score - max(parent, initial), 0)) - 1, so only strict improvements over the parent pay. (7) Only correct programs enter the size-40 replace-worst (or crowding) archive; islands migrate periodically; stagnation can spawn new islands. Coding agents (Claude Code/Codex) join via skills (setup/convert/run/inspect) and as headless mutation providers, not as loop drivers.
eval_loop: Signal is a user-written evaluate.py (run_shinka_eval) returning a scalar combined_score (maximized), a boolean correct from an optional validate_fn, public metrics (visible to the LLM), private metrics (hidden), and free-text feedback; num_runs>1 averages noisy evals. Drift/hacking control: only correct programs enter the archive and elites are never discarded (append-only population, so no rollback is needed); mutations are confined to EVOLVE-BLOCK regions and the evaluator is never evolvable (meta prompt explicitly forbids recommending evaluator changes); private metrics keep the LLM from targeting hidden checks; the bandit only rewards strict improvement over parent/initial; an API-cost cap stops proposals. There is no built-in held-out set — anti-gaming depends entirely on the quality of the user evaluator (circle packing used exact constraint verification; MoE result was validated on 7 downstream benchmarks after evolution).
key_results: Circle packing (n=26): sum of radii 2.636 in ~150 evaluated programs vs AlphaEvolve's 2.635 with thousands. AIME 2024: evolved 3-stage persona/peer-review scaffold hitting max accuracy with 7 LLM queries, transfers to other AIME years and LLMs. ALE-Bench: +2.3% avg over ALE-Agent solutions, one task 5th->2nd on AtCoder leaderboard. MoE: new load-balancing loss beats DeepSeek global-batch LBL (-5.81% routing inefficiency, +1.73% downstream) after ~30 generations. ICFP 2025 (Team Unagi win): Rust SAT encoding sped up 6.5x (18 rooms) and ~10x (24 rooms) in 320 trials, ~$60. Ablations: weighted parent sampling > hill-climb/random; bandit ensemble > single or fixed-mix LLM; embedding rejection gives substantial gains while the LLM novelty judge adds only marginal benefit; meta-scratchpad accelerates learning.
limitations: Claimed vs demonstrated: sample-efficiency claim is vs reported AlphaEvolve numbers, not a head-to-head; results rely on frontier ensembles (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4, o4-mini). "Open-ended" and "self-refining" are aspirational — tasks, evaluators and the search hyperparameters (lambda, alpha, eta, island settings) are fixed by humans and the framework code is not self-modified. Fitness is a single scalar from one evaluator with no held-out split, so overfitting to evaluator quirks is unguarded. Meta-scratchpad recommendations are unverified prose with no credit assignment. Evolution is single-file EVOLVE-BLOCK scope. Software is 0.0.x: Aug-2026 fixes for diff insertions silently corrupting programs (#183) and Rust validation failing on stable (#178); skills cite the wrong arXiv id. Default local execution runs LLM-generated code unsandboxed.
key_insight: Sample-efficiency in LLM-driven evolution comes from search control rather than a smarter mutator: bias parent choice toward high-fitness-but-under-exploited programs, reject near-duplicate candidates by embedding similarity before paying for evaluation, and give the LLM-selection bandit an asymmetric, exponentiated reward that only counts strict improvement over the parent so it chases bold gains instead of safe tweaks.
safety_measures: Immutable code outside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers with marker validation; evaluator is not mutable and meta prompts forbid recommending evaluator changes; private metrics hidden from the LLM; correctness gate on archive entry; append-only population (no destructive self-modification, elites preserved); API cost cap (max_api_costs); optional Docker/SLURM isolation for evaluation; W&B telemetry redaction of secrets; human-in-the-loop confirmation between batches is the default in the shinka-run skill.
open_gaps: No held-out/generalization check inside the loop: fitness is one user evaluator on one objective, so evolved programs can overfit evaluator artifacts without detection

The harness does not evolve itself: parent-sampling lambda/alpha, novelty threshold, island and migration settings, patch-type probabilities are static per run; no online meta-learning of search hyperparameters
No task or objective generation: every run needs a hand-written evaluate.py and initial program, so 'open-ended' is aspirational
No cross-task transfer: archive, meta-scratchpad insights, bandit state and evolved system prompts live in one results_dir and are discarded for the next task
Meta-scratchpad recommendations are never validated: no credit assignment measuring whether a recommendation improved child fitness, so bad advice persists
Diversity is only embedding-similarity within an island; no behavioral/phenotypic descriptors (MAP-Elites style) or multi-objective Pareto search beyond weighted archive ranking
Single-file EVOLVE-BLOCK scope; repo-scale or multi-file evolution is unsupported (shinka-convert flattens a repo into one task)
Correctness is a binary flag from the evaluator; no automatically generated property/differential tests to catch semantically wrong but high-scoring programs

Coding-agent integration is shallow: Claude Code/Codex only scaffold, launch and inspect runs or act as prompt-in/text-out mutation providers; the agent cannot use tools, run tests, or read the repo while mutating
Local job mode executes LLM-generated code unsandboxed; isolation requires SLURM/Docker setup

name: EvoScientist
date: 2026-01-26 (repo created); paper arXiv:2603.08127 submitted 2026-03-09; public debut 2026-03-13
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed); v0.2.10 released 2026-09-05; ~weekly releases
org_or_authors: Huawei Xiaoyi DeepResearch Team + academic collaborators (Yougang Lyu, Xi Zhang, Xinhao Yi, Yuyue Zhao, Shuyu Guo, Wenxiang Hu, Jan Piotrowski, Jakub Kaliski, Jacopo Urbani, Zaiqiao Meng, Lun Zhou, Xiaohui Yan)
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2603.08127 (technical report, v1 only). Self-reported: 6/6 papers accepted at ICAIS 2025 AI Scientist Track (Best Paper + AI Reviewer's Appraisal Award); #1 DeepResearch Bench / DeepResearch Bench II / AstaBench Code & Data Analysis at submission time; #2 ResearchClawBench. Citation count not retrievable (S2 rate-limited).
mechanism: Two layers exist. (A) PAPER SYSTEM (not the repo code): Researcher Agent retrieves top-k_I=2 ideation-memory items by mxbai-embed cosine similarity, runs propose-review-refine tree search (21 candidates, 3 workers), ranks by Elo tournament on novelty/feasibility/relevance/clarity, expands top-1 into a proposal. Engineer Agent retrieves top-k_E=1 experimentation-memory item and runs 4-stage code tree search (budgets 20/12/12/18 attempts, 4 workers), keeping best-performing code per stage. Evolution Manager Agent then writes memory via three prompts: IDE (feasible directions from top-ranked ideas -> MEM_I), IVE (failed proposals -- no executable code within budget, or worse-than-baseline per LLM read of the execution report -> unsuccessful directions in MEM_I), ESE (data-processing + model-training strategies from trajectories and best code -> MEM_E). Next task retrieves updated memories. (B) REPO (deepagents harness, 6 sub-agents): EvoMemoryLifecycleMiddleware fires after every orchestrator turn and subagent run, launching a background memory-worker (auxiliary model, no execute/write_file/delete) that reviews the sanitized trajectory and either edits profile markdown (SOUL.md, USER_PROFILE.md, RESEARCH_TASTE.md, PROJECT_PROFILE.md -- injected into the system prompt) or calls record_observation (semantic/procedural/episodic, global/project scope, sha256 content-hash id for dedupe). An observation-linker agent then adds complements/contradicts/supersedes edges in frontmatter. Main agent must run a memory preflight (inlined index, search_observations ranked keyword search, read_memory). AutoSkills: a cron (nightly/weekly/monthly) agent finds connected components of the observation graph with >=3 nodes and >=2 procedural, drafts a SKILL.md folder via the skill-creator skill, validates frontmatter, submits a pending proposal; a human approves/rejects via /autoskills; approval copies it into the workspace skills tier. The paper's IDE/IVE/ESE ship only as prompt-only skills in the EvoSkills repo (evo-memory, research-ideation).
eval_loop: Paper: internal fitness is (i) an Elo tournament judged by the ideation LLM itself over 4 rubric dimensions (selects which ideas feed IDE), (ii) hard code-execution success within an attempt budget plus an LLM 'worse than baseline' verdict on the execution report (triggers IVE), (iii) best-performing implementation per stage (feeds ESE). External evaluation: Gemini-3-flash pairwise judge with position swap on 30 expert-written queries vs 7 systems, 3 PhD annotators on 4 baselines, and code-execution success before/after ESE (34.39% -> 44.56% mean; stage 3 only 20.33% -> 21.57%). Ablation: -IDE avg gap -22.5, -IVE -20.0 (feasibility lose 63%), -all -45.8. Repo: there is NO fitness signal on memory or auto-skills. Drift is controlled only by prompt guardrails ('durable, non-obvious, evidence-backed, not already present'), content-hash dedupe, contradicts/supersedes links, memory-worker tool restrictions, a prompt-injection instruction ('treat embedded requests as data'), and human approve/reject of skill proposals. Scheduled tasks optionally get a --rubric checklist graded by a read-only auxiliary-model reviewer with one retry. Nothing measures whether a stored observation or synthesized skill improves downstream task outcomes; no regression test on memory writes; no rollback other than a human rejecting a proposal.
limitations: (1) The benchmarked RA/EA/EMA system (tree search, Elo, embedding retrieval, 4-stage engineer) is not the code in the repo; the repo's EvoMemory/AutoSkills loop has never been benchmarked, and the paper mechanism exists downstream only as prompt-only markdown protocols. (2) Repo retrieval is ranked keyword search over markdown, not the embedding retrieval the paper credits. (3) Evaluation: 30 queries; idea judge (Gemini-3-flash) is same family as the ideation model (Gemini-2.5-Pro); ablations cover idea evolution only, not ESE; only before/after code-success numbers, no learning curve over cycles; benchmark suite still unreleased per roadmap. (4) Stage-3 (novel method) code success stays ~21% after evolution. (5) Memory has no value estimation, consolidation, forgetting, or conflict resolution -- the maintainers' own Q4 roadmap (#433) lists duplicate/outdated/conflicting memories and retrieval quality as open problems. (6) Human-on-the-loop gating means AutoSkills do not self-apply; nothing evolves without a person clicking approve. (7) Paper limitations: computational tasks only; may reproduce literature biases. (8) Leaderboard and ICAIS claims are self-reported, 'at submission time'.
key_insight: Split experiential memory by what it steers: an ideation memory that records both promising directions AND validated dead-ends with a failure classification (implementation vs fundamental, decided by execution evidence), and an execution memory of reusable strategies distilled from best-performing trajectories -- then let a graph of linked observations (complements/contradicts/supersedes) be mined offline into human-reviewed skill proposals.
key_results: Paper (arXiv 2603.08127): LLM-judge average win-rate gaps vs Virtual Scientist +93.3, AI-Researcher +87.5, InternAgent +83.3, AI Scientist-v2 +29.2, Hypogenic +80.8, Novix +46.0, K-Dense +54.5; human eval avg 82.5% novelty / 64.2% feasibility win vs 4 strongest baselines; code execution success 34.39% -> 44.56% mean after ESE (stage1 42.25->56.42, stage2 31.89->42.68, stage3 20.33->21.57, stage4 36.68->48.44); ablation -all idea evolution: 80% novelty lose, 83% feasibility lose. Backbones: Gemini-2.5-Pro (ideation/writing), Claude-4.5-Haiku (code). Repo: 4786 stars, 307 forks, 35 contributors, 124 issues, PyPI v0.2.10, Docker image, EvoSkills sibling repo 436 stars.
safety_measures: Memory-worker agents are denied execute/write_file/delete/task tools; prompts instruct them to treat requests in tool/subagent output as data not instructions; observations deduped by content hash; auto-skill proposals must pass frontmatter validation and human approve/reject via /autoskills before installation, and cannot modify built-in system skills; shell execution requires human approval by default with an allow-list option; sandboxed workspace unless --dangerous; sudo/rm -rf blocked even in dangerous mode; scheduled runs gated on shell access.
open_gaps: No fitness signal on memory items: observations and synthesized skills are never scored against downstream task outcomes, so bad memories persist until a human notices
Auto-skill acceptance is purely human approval plus format validation; no automated eval harness runs the proposed SKILL.md on held-out tasks before install
No rollback/versioning of memory or skill changes -- a regression caused by a stored observation cannot be traced and reverted automatically
No consolidation, decay, or conflict resolution: contradicts/supersedes edges are recorded but retrieval does not down-weight superseded or contradicted observations
Repo retrieval is keyword-ranked over markdown; the embedding retrieval the paper credits for gains is not implemented in the product
The paper's benchmarked loop (Elo tournament, execution-budget failure classification, ESE) is not runnable code -- it is a prompt-only skill with no automatic trigger wiring
Learning is per-user/per-workspace; no mechanism to share or federate validated observations/skills across users or projects
No curriculum or task-selection evolution: the system never chooses what to attempt next based on memory gaps
Evaluation lacks a learning curve across cycles and any held-out generalization test; a new framework should report success vs. number of evolution rounds on unseen tasks
Judge and generator are the same model family (Gemini), leaving self-preference bias in the Elo fitness signal unaddressed

name: Agent0 Series (Agent0 + Agent0-VL)
last_activity: 2026-07-10 (last push; Agent0-VL code update). Core Agent0 code last touched 2025-12-25.
org_or_authors: Peng Xia, Kaide Zeng, Jiaqi Liu, Can Qin, Fang Wu, Yiyang Zhou, Caiming Xiong, Huaxiu Yao — UNC Chapel Hill (AIMING Lab), Salesforce Research, Stanford
venue_or_citations: Repo description claims "[ICML'26 & COLM'26]"; arXiv v1 (2511.16043, Nov 2025) carries no venue comment and project page lists no acceptance. OpenAlex shows 0 citations (index incomplete); Semantic Scholar rate-limited. 150 forks, 13 open issues.
mechanism:
Two copies of the same base LLM (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base) alternate in a 2-stage loop, T=3 iterations, hand-driven via shell scripts and manual checkpoint selection.

Stage 1 (curriculum agent, GRPO, 5 steps, batch 128, 4 rollouts): it emits <question>…</question> + boxed answer. Reward = format gate x [ min(p̂, 1-p̂) (uncertainty; p̂ = executor majority-vote agreement over 10 tool-integrated samples, max 4 Python turns via SandboxFusion) + 0.05 x min(#tool calls, 4) (tool-use reward, counted in the proposer's text) - within-batch BLEU-agglomerative-cluster share (repetition penalty, distance threshold 0.5) ]. Executor is frozen.

Stage 2 (executor, ADPO in verl-tool): frozen curriculum generates ~8x1000 questions; executor samples 9 answers each (in evaluate.py, without tools); majority answer becomes the pseudo-label, its vote share p̂ the "score"; keep 0.3<=p̂<=0.8, drop proofs/text answers. Multi-turn RL (16 rollouts, max_turns=4, ~40-100 steps, KL 0.01) with reward I(answer == pseudo-label). ADPO = GRPO with (a) advantage x [0.5 + 0.5*(p̂-0.3)/0.5] (down-weight ambiguous tasks) and (b) eps_high = eps + 0.1*(0.8-p̂)/0.5 (looser upper clip on ambiguous tasks).

Next iteration re-trains the curriculum against the new executor. Reported ratchet: executor pass rate on curriculum sets 64->58.5->51%, avg tool calls 1.65->2.10->2.60.

Agent0-VL variant: one VLM plays Solver and Verifier; Verifier emits (score, conf, critique) per step; confidence-gated self-repair; GRPO on self-generated process reward; needs SFT cold-start data and an external question set (zero external reward, not zero data).
eval_loop: Inside the loop the only signal is self-consistency: the curriculum is rewarded for tasks where the executor's majority vote is ~50%, and the executor is rewarded for matching its own majority-vote pseudo-label. No ground truth or external verifier is used; tool execution grounds computation but never checks correctness. Anti-drift/anti-hacking measures: format gate (must emit question + boxed answer), band filter 0.3-0.8 (rejects trivial/unsolvable), BLEU-cluster repetition penalty (curriculum diversity), KL penalty 0.01, ADPO down-weighting of low-consistency samples, tool-reward cap at 4 calls. Improvement is only verified post-hoc on external held-out benchmarks (AIME/MATH/GSM8K/Olympiad, SuperGPQA/MMLU-Pro/BBEH); nothing in the loop gates or rolls back an iteration — the README says to "manually select the checkpoint". Reported numbers (Qwen3-8B): math avg 49.2->58.2 (55.1/56.5/58.2 per iteration), general 34.5->42.1; ablations: removing curriculum training 58.2->46.8, tool reward ->48.7, repetition penalty ->47.9, ADPO ->56.2, multi-turn ->55.9. Qwen3-4B math plateaus (51.9/52.2/52.5).
limitations: Paper has no limitations section. Demonstrated only on math-style tasks with a single numeric boxed answer (proofs/text answers explicitly discarded); "general reasoning" gains are transfer, not trained. Pseudo-labels from majority vote can be confidently wrong and are reinforced. 'Zero data' still needs a seed prompt dataset (hiyouga/math12k) to trigger generation (issue #21), and Agent0-VL needs SFT tool-usage data. Compute-heavy: 8xA100/H200; a user reports 5 curriculum steps took 24h+ (issue #37). Pipeline is not runnable end-to-end: two separate codebases/conda envs, manual handoff, executor config file missing (issue #26 open). Code/paper mismatches: data-curation scoring runs without tools; ablation table's full-model general avg (36.7) disagrees with main table (42.1); ADPO functional forms only in code. Gains shrink per iteration and 4B saturates after iter 1. Curriculum diversity question (issue #36) unanswered; open security issues (unauthenticated code-exec server, pickle loads). Venue acceptance claimed in repo description but not independently verified.
key_insight: Pairing a task-proposer whose reward is the solver's uncertainty (p̂ near 0.5) with a solver that has real tools, and paying the proposer for tool-dependent tasks, creates an automatic difficulty ratchet; the proposer's self-consistency score should then be reused as a trust signal that scales both advantage magnitude and the PPO clip range when training on pseudo-labels.
key_results: Qwen3-8B-Base: math avg 49.2->58.2 (+18%; beats R-Zero 54.7, Socratic-Zero 56.1, Absolute Zero 52.6), general avg 34.5->42.1. Qwen3-4B: math 42.6->52.5, general 27.1->37.6. Curriculum escalates: pass rate 64%->51%, tool calls/task 1.65->2.60 over 3 iterations. Ablation: curriculum training (-11.4 math), repetition penalty (-10.3), tool reward (-9.5) matter far more than ADPO (-2.0) or multi-turn (-2.3). Agent0-VL-7B: +8.2 avg over Qwen2.5-VL-7B across 3 iterations; also usable as a PRM (+3.6 to +4.7 Best-of-N).
safety_measures: Python execution goes through SandboxFusion (or a subprocess sandbox in Agent0-VL) with timeouts; KL penalty to base; format/band filters. No sandboxing of the self-improvement process itself, no rollback, no human review of generated curricula; open issues flag an unauthenticated 0.0.0.0 code-execution server and pickle deserialization in the data path.
open_gaps: Fitness is pure self-consistency majority vote with no external or tool-based correctness verification, so confidently-wrong majority answers are reinforced; a framework could add executable/verifier-checked ground truth or adversarial verification.
Restricted to single-numeric-answer math (proofs and text answers are dropped in evaluate.py); no mechanism for open-ended, agentic, or multi-step environment tasks (web, code repos, GUIs).
Only model weights evolve; prompts, tool set (a single Python sandbox), harness, and reward functions are fixed — no tool/skill creation or workflow evolution.

No regression gate or rollback between iterations: checkpoints are picked manually and there is no in-loop held-out evaluation; gains plateau (4B: 51.9->52.5) with no stopping criterion or collapse detection.
Requires multi-GPU RL fine-tuning (8xA100/H200, 24h+ per curriculum stage per user report), so unusable by application developers working with API models.
Loop is not automated end-to-end: two codebases (EasyR1-style verl + verl-tool), three conda envs, shell-script handoffs, and a missing executor config (issue #26) — no orchestrator.

No archive or population: each iteration keeps a single curriculum/executor lineage and discards prior curricula; diversity is enforced only by within-batch BLEU clustering with no cross-iteration dedup or memory of solved tasks.
No contamination/leakage audit of generated questions against benchmarks (issue #30) and no measurement of curriculum diversity over training (issue #36 unanswered).

Curriculum reward is a hand-tuned scalar mix (uncertainty + tool count + repetition penalty); the reward/evaluator itself never evolves and tool-call counting is gameable (trivially inserting code blocks).
'Zero data' still depends on a seed prompt dataset (math12k) and, for Agent0-VL, SFT cold-start data plus external question sets.

name: AutoResearchClaw
org_or_authors: AIMING Lab, UNC Chapel Hill (Huaxiu Yao's group; Jiaqi Liu, Shi Qiu et al., 35 authors); 49 GitHub contributors
last_activity: 2026-08-19 (last push; v0.5.0 released 2026-05-20; PR-integration merges Aug 2026)
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.20025 (May 2026), no venue listed; 1669 forks; ARC-Bench dataset on HuggingFace
mechanism: Two loops, neither touches weights or code. INNER (intra-run): a fixed 23-stage linear pipeline (topic -> literature -> hypothesis -> code -> sandbox -> analysis -> paper). Stage 12/13 run generated code in a sandbox; failures trigger targeted LLM repair, then up to 10 "iterative refine" rounds that keep the best version by a single scalar metric_key/direction (`_is_better`). Stage 15 has an LLM choose PROCEED / REFINE (back to 13) / PIVOT (back to 8) with artifact versioning. Optional multi-model debate (stages 8/14/18) and best-of-N tournament (8/9) add breadth. OUTER ("evolution"): only at pipeline END, `extract_lessons()` applies keyword rules to StageResults (failed/blocked stages, PIVOT/REFINE rationale, stderr warnings, NaN/Inf metrics) producing LessonEntry(stage, category, severity string, truncated error text) appended to `run_dir/evolution/lessons.jsonl`. `build_overlay()` ranks lessons by exp(-age*ln2/30d) x2 for stage match x1.5 for errors (90-day cutoff), takes top-5, and appends them as "## Lessons from Prior Runs" text to each stage's user prompt. Because the store lives in the per-run directory, this only recurs on --resume of the same run. True cross-run transfer requires the opt-in MetaClaw bridge (default off): `convert_lessons_to_skills()` asks an LLM once to write up to 3 `arc-*` SKILL.md files into ~/.metaclaw/skills/; later runs inject the first 5 alphabetically-sorted arc-* skills plus keyword-matched registry skills. Skill-effectiveness records are written per run but `compute_skill_stats` is never called; the A-Evolve module (LLM diagnosis + mutation gate + prompt patches) and ALHF InterventionLearner exist but are imported only by tests.
eval_loop: Inner loop signals: sandbox execution success, AST hard-validation (blocks identical ablations/hardcoded metrics), NaN/Inf fast-fail, improvement on one configured scalar metric, VerifiedRegistry that scrubs numbers not present in measurement records, 4-layer citation verification, LLM peer review (7-dim), and an optional PRM gate (3-vote LLM-as-judge returning +1/0/-1 at stages 5/9/15/20; -1 marks the stage FAILED and retries). Outer loop has NO fitness signal: lessons are accepted unconditionally, skills are accepted from a single LLM call with only a "do not duplicate these names" hint, and 30-day time decay is the sole forgetting mechanism; no held-out check that a lesson/skill helps, no rollback. Drift/reward-hacking guard is limited to the anti-fabrication verifier on numbers; the paper itself documents a silent semantic collapse (T10: all conditions output identical zeros that pass the numeric gate). Evidence for the evolution component is a 10-topic best-of-3 LLM-judged ablation (-0.48 quality, -1 completion without it) and a MetaClaw A/B with unspecified n using an author-defined composite score.
limitations: Cross-run learning is off by default and depends on the MetaClaw bridge; the base lesson store is per-run. Lesson extraction is regex/keyword classification of error strings, not root-cause diagnosis; the paper's "severity score s(l) in (0,1] with recommended mitigation" does not exist in code (severity is info/warning/error). Skill injection is capped at 5 alphabetically-first arc-* files, so accumulated skills starve newer ones; no pruning, scoring, or rollback of learned skills. Evaluation is entirely LLM-judged (GPT-5.3-codex is both backbone and judge), on CPU-only <10-min ML tasks; full-auto paper acceptance is 3/10 and mean quality 4.03/10 in the end-to-end test; HEP score 0.489; no human expert review of scientific merit; no cost-per-paper disclosure. Community issue #326 calls it a toy that fails on anything slightly complex. Pipeline topology, stage prompts, and agent code never change.
key_insight: Treat every pipeline failure as a first-class artifact: extract it into a time-decayed natural-language lesson and re-inject it as a prompt overlay (or LLM-authored SKILL.md) so any LLM backbone avoids it next run without retraining - but the ablation shows this cross-run memory buys far less (-0.48 quality) than robust inner loops (debate -1.37, self-healing -40% completion), so long-horizon agents should invest in in-run repair/verification before cross-run evolution.
key_results: ARC-Bench experiment-stage (25 ML topics, LLM judge): AutoResearchClaw CoPilot 0.648, Full-Auto 0.596, AIDE-ML 0.511, AI Scientist v2 0.419 (+54.7% overall, +100.4% on result analysis). Domain tasks: biology 0.912, statistics 0.898, HEP 0.489 (baselines score 0 there). End-to-end HITL (10 topics): CoPilot quality 7.27 / 87.5% accept with 6 interventions vs Full-Auto 4.03 / 25% and Step-by-Step 5.19 / 50% with 23 interventions. Component ablation (10 topics, best-of-3): full 5.62 quality, 10/10 completion, 3/10 accept; w/o debate 4.25 (p=0.003); w/o self-healing 6/10 completion; w/o evolution 5.14, 9/10 completion. MetaClaw A/B (README, n unspecified): stage retry 10.5%->7.9%, refine cycles 2.0->1.2, composite robustness +18.3%. 8 showcase papers across 8 domains. 2699 tests claimed.
safety_measures: Docker/venv sandbox with allowed_imports, memory limits and network_policy (none/setup_only/pip_only/full); AST validation of generated code; immutable harness; NaN/Inf fast-fail; VerifiedRegistry anti-fabrication (unverified numbers sanitized); 4-layer citation verification removing hallucinated refs; 3 HITL gates (stages 5/9/20) with rollback and 7 intervention modes; cost budget guardrails with auto-pause; SHA256 artifact manifests and versioned undo. For self-modification specifically: none - learned lessons/skills are plain text written to ~/.metaclaw/skills without review, gating, or rollback, though they cannot execute code.
open_gaps: Lesson store is scoped to run_dir/evolution; no global store aggregating lessons across artifacts/rc-* runs, so out-of-the-box runs are stateless and cross-run learning requires enabling the MetaClaw bridge

No fitness/acceptance signal on evolved artifacts: lessons accepted unconditionally, skills accepted from one LLM call; skill_effectiveness.jsonl is written but compute_skill_stats() is never called, so harmful skills are never pruned or rolled back
Learned-skill injection takes the first 5 alphabetically sorted arc-* directories; once >5 skills exist newer ones are silently never used, and the library grows unboundedly with name-only dedup

Lesson extraction is keyword scoring over truncated error strings; no root-cause diagnosis, no mitigation field, no dedup of repeated identical lessons (the A-Evolve LLM-diagnosis + mutation-gate module exists but is unwired)
Only prompt-overlay text evolves; the 23-stage topology, stage prompts (prompt_patches.md is written but never read), tool set, and agent code are fixed
Human feedback is not learned from: hitl/learning.py InterventionLearner (ALHF) is never instantiated outside tests, so rejection/edit patterns never change future pause policies
Evolution benefit is not tested for transfer: ablation on 10 same-distribution ML topics with unspecified warm-start; no held-out topic/domain evaluation of whether a lesson from run N helps run N+1
Fitness is entirely LLM-as-judge with the same model family as the backbone; no human expert scoring of scientific validity, and full-auto acceptance is only 3/10
Inner refine loop optimizes a single scalar metric_key, enabling Goodhart failures (paper's T10 silent semantic collapse passes verification)
No token/cost accounting per paper and ~46K tokens of static prompt overhead; not usable for evolving arbitrary application agents outside the research-paper pipeline

name: The AI Scientist-v2 (Sakana AI)
org_or_authors: Sakana AI (Yutaro Yamada, Robert Tjarko Lange, Cong Lu, Shengran Hu, Chris Lu, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, David Ha; with UBC/Oxford/Vector)
date: 2025-04-08 (repo created); paper arXiv:2504.08066 submitted 2025-04-10 (v1 only, never revised)
last_activity: Last push 2025-12-19 (license/README disclosure text only). Last functional code change Oct 2025 (ollama support merged then reverted). Effectively unmaintained: 78 open issues, with June-Aug 2026 bug reports (single failed worker aborts run #122, machine-wide SIGTERM cleanup #123, UnboundLocalError #125/#131, VLM whitelist rejection #133) unanswered.
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (2504.08066). The generated paper was reviewed at the ICLR 2025 "I Can't Believe It's Not Better" workshop (scores 6/6/7, avg 6.33, withdrawn before publication). OpenAlex lists 30 citations (known undercount for arXiv; Semantic Scholar rate-limited during check). Forks: 983. Companion repo AI-Scientist-ICLR2025-Workshop-Experiment: 303 stars. Predecessor AI-Scientist v1: 14.5k stars.
mechanism: Not a self-modifying agent: what evolves is the experiment program (Python "node" code + plotting code) for ONE research idea, within ONE run. Loop (agent_manager.py + parallel_agent.py, AIDE-derived): an AgentManager walks 4 hard-coded main stages (1 initial_implementation, 2 baseline_tuning, 3 creative_research, 4 ablation_studies), each with LLM-generated sub-stages whose goals are synthesized from a metrics/issues summary of the journal (a dynamic mini-curriculum). Each stage runs a ParallelAgent best-first tree search: fill num_workers (4) slots per step by (a) drafting roots until num_drafts=3, (b) with debug_prob=0.5 picking a random buggy leaf with debug_depth<=3 to debug, else (c) expanding the current best good node (stages 1/3) or the frozen best previous-stage node with a unique hyperparam/ablation idea generated in the main process (stages 2/4). Workers get an LLM "memory_summary" of the journal so far. Each node's code executes in a multiprocessing subprocess with a 1h timeout; a feedback LLM (gpt-4o) parses stdout to set is_buggy and extract the metric; separate plotting code produces figures that a VLM critiques, and VLM-flagged problems set is_buggy_plots. good_nodes = neither flag set. Best node = LLM judge (gpt-4o, T=0.3) over good nodes given metric, training analysis and VLM feedback (fallback: max metric). Stage completion = LLM judging VLM feedback against stage goals, plus hard caps (21/12/12/18 nodes). On completion the best node is re-run with 3 seeds, an aggregation node combines plots, and a deep-copied best node seeds the next stage's journal. Then: Semantic Scholar citation gathering (20 rounds), LaTeX writeup, 3 reflection rounds using VLM figure/caption review and page-limit checks, and a final LLM+VLM review written to disk (not fed back).
eval_loop: Entirely LLM/VLM-judged; there is no ground-truth fitness. Signals: (1) feedback LLM parses execution output to decide is_buggy and extract a self-declared metric (the agent itself defines the metric name/direction); (2) VLM critique of generated plots marks nodes buggy for unclear labels/missing legends/misleading visuals; (3) LLM judge picks the best node across candidates using metric + analysis + VLM feedback, explicitly told not to rely solely on validation loss; (4) LLM judges sub-stage/stage completion against natural-language goals; (5) writeup: 3 VLM-driven reflection rounds on figures/captions + LaTeX compile/page-limit checks; (6) final AI reviewer (NeurIPS-style rubric) — output only saved, never used to iterate. Anti-drift/regression measures are structural rather than verified: buggy nodes can never be selected as best; the tree keeps all nodes within a stage (archive); the best previous-stage node is frozen as the root/anchor of stages 2 and 4 so tuning/ablation branch from a known-good program; multi-seed (3) replication of the stage winner; hard iteration caps and a 15h wall clock. Reward hacking is not guarded: the agent chooses its own metric, the same LLM family judges output, and the paper's accepted manuscript had ~57% train/test overlap that no check caught. External ground truth came only from humans: workshop reviewers (blind) and authors' choice of the best of several seed manuscripts.
key_results: Three fully AI-generated manuscripts submitted to the ICLR 2025 ICBINB workshop (43 submissions; reviewers told some might be AI). One scored 6, 6, 7 (avg 6.33, roughly top 45%), above the average acceptance threshold — the first AI-generated paper to pass peer review; the other two were rejected; all were withdrawn before publication. Accepted paper's finding was a negative result (compositional regularization does not help). Authors' own assessment: borderline workshop accept, not conference-level; found citation hallucinations, caption inaccuracies, ~57% train/test overlap, synthetic-data-only evaluation. Cost ~$15-20 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet experiments) + ~$5 writeup per run; several hours up to a 15h limit; ~57 nodes per run (21/12/12/12). No quantitative benchmark, no v1-vs-v2 comparison, no ablations of the tree search or VLM loop; README concedes v2 does not necessarily beat template-based v1 and has lower success rates. Humans selected which ideas to run and which of several seed manuscripts to submit.
limitations: Single-run, single-idea search with zero cross-run learning (no memory, skill, or prompt persistence; issue #119 RFC explicitly requests cross-run memory). All fitness signals are LLM/VLM self-judgment on an agent-defined metric — no held-out test, no reproducibility check, no citation verification (hallucinated citations acknowledged). Only ML-flavored ideas runnable as one Python file on a GPU with HuggingFace datasets (stage prompts hard-code "THREE HuggingFace datasets"). Final AI review is not used to revise. Success rate unquantified and admitted to be low; results were cherry-picked by humans (best of N seeds). No sandbox: LLM code runs via exec() in a multiprocessing subprocess on the host; end-of-run cleanup SIGTERMs unrelated python processes machine-wide (#123). Fragile engineering: single worker failure aborts run (#122), writeup retries delete earlier PDFs (#124), stage summaries only persisted at the end (#127). Requires Linux + CUDA + conda + LaTeX + multiple paid APIs; Bedrock-only Claude path; effectively unmaintained since Oct 2025. Paper never revised (arXiv v1 only); claimed generality "across ML domains" demonstrated on only 3 ideas from one workshop theme.
key_insight: Decompose open-ended research into a fixed progression of stages (prototype -> tune baseline -> explore -> ablate), run an AIDE-style best-first tree search over executable experiment programs inside each stage, freeze and carry forward only the LLM/VLM-judged best node as the root of the next stage, and make figure quality a first-class fitness signal via VLM critique that marks nodes buggy — turning a template-free coding agent into an end-to-end paper producer without any learned component.
open_gaps: No cross-run or cross-idea transfer: every run starts from scratch; no persisted skills, code snippets, failure patterns, or prompt refinements (a framework could bank successful node code/plot code/debug fixes as reusable skills)

Fitness is agent-defined metric + same-family LLM/VLM judgment with no held-out or external verification; nothing catches train/test leakage, seed cherry-picking, or metric gaming (add independent reproduction, data-leakage detectors, statistical tests before a node can be 'best')
Final AI reviewer output is write-only; reviewer scores never drive another experiment or writeup iteration (close the loop: review -> targeted new stage/sub-stage)

Stage structure and stage goals are hard-coded English strings tuned for HuggingFace ML experiments; the manager cannot add/remove/reorder stages or change search hyperparameters (debug_prob, num_drafts, caps) based on observed progress
Citations are gathered but never verified against Semantic Scholar metadata; hallucinated references reach the PDF
No sandbox: exec() in a host subprocess, plus machine-wide process kill on cleanup; an evolving-agent framework needs container-per-node isolation and resource accounting
Journal/tree is per-stage and discarded conceptually after the best node is copied; no archive across stages or runs for quality-diversity style reuse
Single seed per idea in-run; human picks the best of N manuscripts offline — no automated ensemble/selection over multiple runs
Requires Linux+CUDA+conda+LaTeX+Bedrock/OpenAI keys and ~$25/run; not usable by app developers without GPUs; unmaintained with open crash bugs since mid-2026

No quantitative evaluation harness (no success-rate reporting, no benchmark of research quality, no ablation of tree search vs. linear, VLM loop on/off), so improvements to the system cannot be measured
safety_measures: README warns LLM-written code executes with risks (dangerous packages, web access, spawned processes) and tells users to run inside Docker, but the code itself provides no isolation (exec in multiprocessing subprocess, 1h timeout only). Custom 'AI Scientist Source Code License' (Responsible AI License derivative) legally mandates prominent disclosure of AI generation in any resulting paper. Human gates: humans chose the 3 ideas and the best manuscript per idea; workshop organizers/reviewers were pre-informed that some submissions might be AI-generated; all accepted AI papers were withdrawn to avoid setting a precedent for AI-only work entering the scientific record. No guardrails on data leakage, citation verification, or metric gaming.

name: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)
org_or_authors: Fudan University (Jiahang Lin, Shichun Liu, Chengjun Pan, Lizhi Lin, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Gui, Yu-Gang Jiang) with Nex-AGI / Dawning Road (Hang Yan, Zhenhua Han); maintainer GitHub handle Curry09
last_activity: 2026-08-03 (last push: crash-guard fix PR #11); open PRs #16-#19 from Aug-Sep 2026 unmerged; NexAU framework itself pushed 2026-09-10
venue_or_citations: arXiv only (cs.CL, cs.SE), no peer-reviewed venue; ranked #3 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 leaderboard as of 2026-05-15 (NexAU-AHE, GPT-5.5, 84.7%)
mechanism: Outer loop `evaluate -> analyze -> improve`, orchestrated by a 200KB `evolve.py`; base model frozen (GPT-5.4 high). (1) Evaluate: `harbor` runs the code agent (NexAU framework, seed = bash-only single shell tool + 10-line system prompt) with k=2 rollouts on all 89 Terminal-Bench 2 tasks in E2B sandboxes (64-96 concurrent), emitting per-task JSON traces + pass/fail. (2) Analyze: orchestrator computes task-level diff vs previous iteration (flipped / regressed / rollout_regressed) and runs `evaluate_changes()`: for each change in last iteration's `change_manifest.json` it intersects the declared `predicted_fixes` with observed flips and `risk_tasks` with observed regressions, yielding a verdict EFFECTIVE / PARTIALLY_EFFECTIVE / MIXED / INEFFECTIVE / HARMFUL plus `unattributed_regressions`. Agent Debugger (partially closed-source, GPT-5.4, 16 parallel `adb ask` jobs) distills >10M-token traces into `analysis/overview.md` + per-task `detail/*.md`. (3) Improve: Evolve Agent (NexAU meta-agent, GPT-5.4 xhigh, 500 turns, file/shell/web tools, context compaction, "ralph loop" middleware) reads evolution_history, analysis, attribution table and may only edit `workspace/`: systemprompt.md, code_agent.yaml, tool_descriptions/, tools/*.py, middleware/*.py, skills/, sub_agents/, LongTermMEMORY.md. Each logical change = one git commit + manifest entry (id, files, failure_pattern, predicted_fixes, risk_tasks, constraint_level, why_this_component); it runs `validate_agent.py` for schema/import checks. Rollback is prompted ("HARMFUL: must rollback") but executed by the LLM, not enforced by code — `perform_auto_rollback` only fires on manual resume. Optional Best-of-N (off by default): N=2 evolve agents with orthogonal strategy hints (structural vs guidance), both evaluated, higher pass_rate adopted. Stops at target_pass_rate 0.95 or max_iterations.
eval_loop: Fitness = pass@1 on the same 89 Terminal-Bench 2 tasks used for evolution (k=2 rollouts, ~3.2h/iteration); there is no train/held-out split (author confirms in issue #14 that the harness is evolved on the tasks it is scored on). Drift control is (a) falsifiable per-edit predictions checked against next-round task flips, (b) git-tracked file-level components so any edit is revertible, (c) prompt-level bans on task-specific logic / reverse-engineering tests / touching llm_config, (d) a best_ever.json snapshot surfaced to the agent. Reward hacking is only weakly guarded: the evolve agent can write to exp_dir including best_ever.json (issue #15), rollbacks are LLM-decided, and regression predictions are near random (11.8% precision vs 5.6% random) so 6/10 iterations did not improve. Generalization is argued post hoc via frozen-harness transfer to SWE-bench Verified (+0.4pp, -12% tokens) and to 4 other models (+2.3 to +10.1pp).
key_results: GPT-5.4 high on Terminal-Bench 2: 69.7% -> 77.0% pass@1 after 10 iterations (only 4 iterations improved: +0.6, +1.1, +2.8, +1.1); beats hand-written Codex-CLI 71.9%, ACE 68.9% (regresses below seed), Training-Free GRPO 72.3%. By difficulty: easy 100%, medium 88.2%, hard 53.3% (Codex hard 56.7% — no gain on hard). Component ablation (single component swapped into seed): memory-only 75.3%, tools-only 73.0%, middleware-only 71.9%, prompt-only 67.4% (below seed); gains non-additive. Attribution accuracy: fix precision 33.7% vs 6.5% random, fix recall 51.4%; regression precision 11.8% vs 5.6%. Frozen harness on SWE-bench Verified: 75.6% vs 75.2% seed with 461k vs 526k tokens (12% fewer); ACE/TF-GRPO regressed 9-11% there. Cross-model transfer without re-evolution: DeepSeek-v4-flash 51.7->61.8 (+10.1), Qwen-3.6-plus +6.3, Gemini-3.1-flash-lite +5.1, GPT-5.4 medium/xhigh +2.3. README/leaderboard claim NexAU-AHE 84.7% +/-2.1 with GPT-5.5 (not in paper; unclear whether re-evolved).
limitations: Evolves on the evaluation set itself with no held-out tasks; the released evolved harness is visibly benchmark-shaped ("mirror the evaluator", "verifier scripts are source of truth", references to "annealing spans" and cherry-pick recovery that match specific TB2 tasks). Seed is deliberately minimal (bash-only, ~10-line prompt) so a large share of the +7.3pp is recovering basic harness engineering; no gain on hard tasks. Curve is non-monotone and regression-blind; rollbacks are suggested to the LLM rather than enforced; the optimized agent can overwrite orchestrator state (best_ever.json, issue #15). Agent Debugger is only partially open-sourced; sandbox needs a 1-star fork NexAU-harbor and E2B (SaaS concurrency caps or self-hosted cluster); Python >=3.13; ~32h and heavy GPT-5.4 token spend for one campaign; k=2 rollouts is a noisy signal on 89 tasks. Single-lineage (no archive/population except optional Best-of-2). Baseline parity with ACE/TF-GRPO budgets not documented. Repo is mostly docs commits after May; community bug-fix PRs unmerged.
key_insight: Treat every harness edit as a falsifiable experiment: force the optimizer to declare which tasks should flip and which are at risk, then mechanically score those predictions against the next round's per-task deltas and feed the verdicts back — this turns opaque LLM-driven "self-improvement" into an auditable, revertible, evidence-gated loop, and the ablation shows the durable gains live in tools, middleware and long-term memory, not in the system prompt (prompt-only edits regressed).
open_gaps: No train/held-out task split: fitness is pass@1 on the same 89 tasks being optimized, so overfitting to Terminal-Bench evaluator conventions is unmeasured (a new framework should evolve on a train slice and gate acceptance on a disjoint validation slice)
Rollback is advisory: attribution verdicts (HARMFUL/INEFFECTIVE) are shown to the LLM but no code reverts a change or blocks re-adoption; auto-revert to best-ever snapshot only runs on manual resume

Regression prediction is near random (11.8% precision vs 5.6% baseline) and unattributed regressions are just listed, so there is no causal isolation of which edit broke which task (e.g. per-edit A/B or leave-one-out evaluation)
Single lineage with greedy acceptance; no archive/population of harness variants, no Pareto front across task subsets, Best-of-N is n=2 and off by default
Optimizer process can write to orchestrator state (best_ever.json, exp_dir) — no integrity boundary between the evolved agent and its scorer
k=2 rollouts on 89 tasks gives noisy pass@1 (+/-1-2pp) yet single-iteration deltas of +0.6pp are treated as signal; no statistical acceptance test
Requires E2B sandboxes, a private-ish NexAU-harbor fork, and a partially closed Agent Debugger — not reproducible or usable by ordinary app developers; cost (~32h, GPT-5.4 xhigh) per campaign
Evolution only tested from a deliberately minimal bash-only seed with a frontier model; no evidence it improves a mature harness (Codex/OpenCode-like) or works with weaker evolve-agent models
No cross-task/cross-benchmark generalization during evolution — transfer is tested only post hoc on a frozen artifact; no mechanism to detect benchmark-specific leakage into prompts/memory
Evolved knowledge is unstructured (free-text LongTermMEMORY + prompt rules) with no dedup, decay, or conflict resolution across iterations
safety_measures: Edits confined to workspace/ (runs/, verifier, tracer, llm_config read-only); original seed prompt rules non-deletable; prompt bans on task-specific logic, hardcoded solutions and reverse-engineering tests; every change git-committed with a manifest for auditability; validate_agent.py schema/import check before eval; rollouts sandboxed in E2B; best-ever snapshot retained. Paper explicitly says it "does not provide a complete guardrail stack" and is a controlled research prototype; in practice rollback is LLM-discretionary and the evolve agent has write access to orchestrator state files.
sources_read: evolve.py (evaluate_changes, update_best_ever, perform_auto_rollback, select_variant_winner, main loop)

name: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
org_or_authors: Stanford IRIS Lab (Chelsea Finn) — Yoonho Lee, Roshen Nair, Qizheng Zhang, Kangwook Lee, Omar Khattab, Chelsea Finn
last_activity: 2026-07-11 (last push: Harbor meta-harness pilot merged, TB2/text-class aligned with Harbor 0.18)
venue_or_citations: COLM 2026 (per project page). Citation count: scout reports ~170; OpenAlex (lagging) shows 7; Semantic Scholar rate-limited — treat 170 as unverified. Companion artifact repo meta-harness-tbench2-artifact has 1205 stars. 148 forks; 5 listed community reimplementations (HarnessForge, SuperagenticAI/metaharness, Harvey legal-agent HF space, etc.).
mechanism: Outer loop (meta_harness.py, ~600 LOC per domain) is deliberately minimal. Each iteration: (1) spawn Claude Code (Opus 4.6, effort=max, tools Read/Glob/Grep/Agent/Write/Edit/Bash) with a SKILL.md 'proposer prior' and a task prompt pointing at run directories; (2) the proposer reads evolution_summary.jsonl (one row per past candidate: score, hypothesis, delta, components), frontier_val.json (best-per-dataset/task + Pareto list), all prior candidate source files in agents/, and raw execution traces (log.jsonl per dataset/candidate, Harbor trial dirs with full trajectories) using grep/cat — median 82 files, >20 prior candidates per step, ~10M tokens/iter; (3) it must write k new single-file candidates (k=3 memory systems for text classification, k=1 Terminus2 subclass for TB2), each a copy-then-edit of an existing candidate with one falsifiable hypothesis, and is told to prototype in /tmp against real trace examples and self-critique that the change is a mechanism not a parameter sweep; (4) writes pending_eval.json; (5) controller import-checks (and for TB2 smoke-tests 1 trial on 1 task), then benchmarks on the search set (3 datasets online-learning val split; or 89 TB2 tasks x 2 trials, ~$500/iter); (6) appends scores to the summary, updates frontier only if strictly greater. No parent selection, no pruning: every candidate persists on disk as an archive the proposer can inspect. Test set is evaluated once at explicit --test finalization (text-cls); TB2 searches and reports on the same benchmark. Nothing is fine-tuned; the base model (GPT-OSS-120B, Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5) is frozen.
eval_loop: Signal = benchmark score on a search set: mean validation accuracy over 3 classification datasets (online learning, GPT-OSS-120B) or flat pass rate over 89 TB2 tasks x 2 trials (Opus 4.6). Frontier/"best" advances only on strict improvement, but nothing is rolled back — losers simply sit in the archive as diagnostic data. Drift/overfit controls are mostly prompt-level: SKILL.md forbids dataset/task names and task-specific hints; the paper argues code-space overfitting (hard-coded class maps, if-chains) is auditable by reading the code. Held-out test results live in a separate results/ dir 'never exposed during evolution' and are computed once via --test on a frozen run. OOD check: 73.1% on 9 unseen datasets vs ACE 70.2%; math harness transfers to 5 unseen models (+4.7 avg). Ablation (text-cls, median/best): scores-only 34.6/41.3, scores+LLM summary 34.9/38.7, full traces 50.0/56.7 — raw traces are the whole signal. Weaknesses: TB2 search set == final eval set (acknowledged 'discovery problem'); 2 trials per task makes ~1-pt deltas within noise yet frontier accepts any positive delta; no automated leakage detector in the paper code (the July 2026 experimental Harbor pilot adds forbidden-string checks per task, a trusted evaluator subprocess and an eval budget, but scored only on the same tasks used during optimization).
key_results: Text classification (GPT-OSS-120B frozen, 20 iters/40 candidates): 48.6% vs ACE 40.9% (+7.7) with 11.4K vs 50.8K context tokens; matches OpenEvolve/TTT-Discover final accuracy in 0.1x evaluations and beats them by >10 pts at end. Math (250-problem search, 40 iters/109 candidates): discovered 4-route BM25 retrieval harness gives +4.7 avg on 200 IMO-level problems across 5 held-out models (GPT-OSS-20B +3.0, GPT-5.4-nano +8.7, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite +6.3). Terminal-Bench 2: 76.4% Opus 4.6 (#2 among Opus agents, beats Terminus-KIRA 74.7%), 37.6% Haiku 4.5 (#1 among Haiku agents, +2.1 over Goose). The TB2 winner is KIRA + ~80 LOC 'environment snapshot' injected before turn 1; it improved 7/89 tasks, and 6 of the first 7 iterations regressed before the proposer diagnosed a confound and switched to additive-only edits. Proposer context ~10M tok/iter vs 0.002-0.026M for OPRO/TextGrad/AlphaEvolve/GEPA/TTT-Discover. Search runs finish in 'a few hours'; TB2 costs ~$500 per iteration.
limitations: Single proposer (Claude Code Opus 4.6) — the authors say generality across proposers is untested. Framework is two domain-specific scripts, not a library; math example not released; README states code 'has not been tested beyond verifying that it runs'. TB2 search and report on the same 89 tasks; 2-trial evaluation is noisy relative to the 1-2 pt gains claimed; the TB2 discovered artifact is a small prompt-time addition, not a structural harness change. Frontier accepts any positive delta with no significance test; no rollback, no regression suite, no lineage tracking beyond a 'base_system' string. Overfitting defense is prompt instructions plus manual code reading. Very expensive (~$500/iter TB2; hours per iter) and tied to Runloop/Modal + Harbor + Claude Code subscription auth. Citation figure (170) not independently verifiable; OpenAlex shows 7.
key_insight: Give the proposer agent the entire filesystem of prior candidates — source, scores, and raw execution traces — and let it grep/cat selectively (~10M tokens/iter) instead of scalar rewards or LLM summaries; ablations show summaries add nothing (34.9 vs 34.6 median) while raw traces lift median accuracy to 50.0, so 'search with selective access to diagnostic experience' is the actual mechanism, not code evolution per se.
safety_measures: Prompt-level anti-overfitting rules (no dataset/task names, no task-specific hints), import validation, 1-task smoke test (TB2), held-out test in a separate directory evaluated once after freezing the run, proposer disallowed from editing existing agents/controller/wrapper. Experimental Harbor pilot (July 2026): per-task forbidden_references strings + universal denylist (/tests, verifier, /solution, task.toml), generated harness never imported by the long-lived controller (staged in a temp dir, run in a child subprocess), frozen append-only EvaluationState with eval budget. No sandbox restrictions on the proposer itself (has Bash), no automated regression gate, no human-in-the-loop acceptance.
open_gaps: Fitness is a single search-set score accepted on any strictly positive delta with 2 trials/task — no statistical significance test, no repeated-trial confirmation, no held-out regression gate before a candidate becomes 'frontier'

No cross-domain or cross-task transfer of discovered harness components: each run starts from a hand-written baseline and the archive is per-run/per-domain; nothing is distilled into reusable skills or a library of mechanisms

No lineage/credit assignment: candidates record only a free-text 'base_system' and 'components' tags, so the proposer cannot query which mechanisms historically helped across runs (the paper's 'component analysis' is manual)

Overfitting/reward-hacking defense is prompt text plus manual code reading; no automated leakage detector in the released paper loop (the experimental pilot's forbidden-string check is only a string grep, easily circumvented)
Search set == final eval set on Terminal-Bench 2; no protocol for benchmarks without a natural held-out split
Proposer is a one-shot Claude Code session per iteration with no persistent memory of its own reasoning; insights (e.g. the iteration-3 confound diagnosis) live only in ad-hoc report files

The controller/evaluator/proposer prompt (SKILL.md) is fixed — the harness of the meta-loop itself is not evolved, and no meta-level signal detects when the proposer is stuck in parameter tweaking beyond a written rule
Cost is ~$500/iteration and hours of wall-clock with Runloop/Modal sandboxes; no cheap proxy evaluation, active task subsampling, or early stopping of clearly failing candidates

Only a single proposer (Claude Code Opus 4.6) is supported; swapping proposers requires rewriting claude_wrapper.py and the framework has no abstraction for multi-proposer or population-parallel search
No co-evolution of harness with model weights or with the task curriculum; search set is fixed and never adapted toward the failure modes that the traces reveal

name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (companion list to "A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents", arXiv 2508.07407)
mechanism: This repo has NO loop of its own: it is a README-only curated list (README.md + LICENSE + 3 figures, zero code) that indexes ~250 papers under the survey's taxonomy. The mechanism it codifies is the survey's abstract loop: four components — System Inputs I (task-level datasets vs instance-level single queries), Agent System A (LLM, prompts, memory, tools, and for MAS the topology/workflow), Environment E (benchmark or real-world feedback), and Optimiser P — where P is characterised by a search space (which parts of A are configurable) plus a search algorithm, and each iteration maps (I, A, feedback from E) to a new A'. The list then organises concrete instantiations by what P mutates: (1.1) LLM behaviour via SFT/RL (STaR, Self-Rewarding LMs, Absolute Zero, R-Zero, SPIRAL) or test-time feedback/search (CodeT, ToT, AIDE); (1.2) prompts via edit-based (GrIPS), evolutionary (EvoPrompt, Promptbreeder, GEPA), generative (APE, OPRO, PromptAgent, DSPy/MIPRO) and text-gradient (ProTeGi, TextGrad, REVOLVE) optimisers; (1.3) memory (Agent Workflow Memory, A-MEM, Mem0, Memento, ReasoningBank); (1.4) tools via training, inference-time selection, or tool creation (CREATOR, Alita, ToolEVO); (2) multi-agent workflow/topology search (ADAS, AFlow, GPTSwarm, MaAS, EvoAgentX, MermaidFlow, CORAL); (3) domain systems incl. agent-source-code evolution (DGM, AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve, Live-SWE-agent); (4) evaluation (benchmarks, LLM/Agent-as-a-Judge, safety benchmarks). The survey frames a MOP→MOA→MAO→MASE development path and "Three Laws" (Endure = safety, Excel = performance preservation, Evolve = autonomous optimisation) as constraints any optimiser must respect.
eval_loop: None for the repo itself (its only "signal" is community PRs adding entries). The survey's Section 4 catalogues evaluation signals used across the field: benchmark scores (SWE-bench, WebArena, GAIA, AgentBench, OSWorld, ToolBench-style suites), LLM-as-a-Judge and Agent-as-a-Judge for tasks without ground truth, and a safety/robustness benchmark set (AgentHarm, RedCode, R-Judge, AGrail, AutoDAN-Turbo). It states safety/alignment must be "continuous requirements" across the evolutionary lifecycle, but gives no operational recipe for preventing drift or reward hacking — no held-out validation protocol, no rollback criteria, no anti-Goodhart guidance beyond naming the Endure/Excel principles.
limitations: (1) No runnable artifact — purely a bibliography; the survey's framework is conceptual with no formal guarantees or quantitative comparison across methods. (2) Taxonomy is over-inclusive: issue #37 correctly notes OpenHands, CodeAgent, Self-Refine, AgentCoder etc. are iterative workflows, not self-evolving agents; the list conflates test-time refinement, prompt optimisation, RL post-training, and open-ended code evolution under one banner. (3) Maintenance has stalled: last merge 2026-05-16, 22 PRs (Ouroboros, OpenSkill, RewardHarness, Harness-Aware Training, Kapso, etc.) unmerged as of Sept 2026, so it under-represents the 2026 wave of harness/skill-level self-evolution. (4) Known venue/figure errors (issues #40, #61). (5) Self-promotional: the only two "Open-Source Frameworks" listed are the authors' EvoAgentX and MASLab. (6) Safety section is a list of benchmarks, not mechanisms. (7) Sparse on memory/skill evolution for deployed app agents and on cross-task transfer.
key_insight: Every self-evolution method is the same abstract loop — an Optimiser with a declared search space over agent components (prompt, memory, tools, topology, weights, source code) that consumes environment feedback and emits a new agent — so a framework should treat "what is mutable" as a pluggable dimension, and must explicitly enforce the survey's Endure (safety) and Excel (no performance regression) laws as acceptance gates, not afterthoughts.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of the four-component (Inputs/Agent/Environment/Optimiser) loop — a framework could ship the abstract interface so prompt, memory, tool, topology and code optimisers are interchangeable plugins

Endure/Excel laws are stated but never operationalised: no concrete regression-gate protocol (held-out eval, safety suite re-run, automatic rollback) that an optimiser must pass before a mutation is accepted

Taxonomy has no axis for the fitness signal (ground-truth benchmark vs LLM-judge vs execution tests vs human) or for how each method resists reward hacking — a framework should make evaluator provenance and anti-Goodhart checks explicit
No treatment of cross-task/cross-domain transfer of evolved artifacts (skills, prompts, memories) — most listed methods optimise per-benchmark and are re-run from scratch per task

Harness-level evolution (agent scaffolding, tool schemas, permission/sandbox config, hooks) is absent from the taxonomy — pending PRs (Harness-Aware Training, RewardHarness, Ouroboros, OpenSkill) show the field moved there in 2026 but the list stalled in May 2026

No lineage/archive concept for non-code artifacts: population/archive-based evolution appears only for code (DGM, AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve); prompt/memory/tool evolution is presented as single-lineage hill-climbing

No cost/compute accounting dimension — nothing tells a practitioner which optimisers run on API-only budgets vs require GPU fine-tuning (model-weight methods dominate section 1.1 and 1.4.1 but are unusable for most app developers)
Memory section lists storage designs but no method for pruning, verifying, or expiring learned memories, so drift and stale-knowledge accumulation remain unaddressed
Evaluation section lacks any benchmark for the evolution process itself (sample-efficiency of improvement, stability across iterations, catastrophic forgetting) as opposed to end-task score
last_activity: 2026-05-16 (last merged commits); 22 PRs opened through 2026-09-08 remain unmerged
key_results: Survey-only, no experiments. Repo: 2,477 stars, 190 forks, 41 PRs (22 open), 34 issues. Paper arXiv 2508.07407 (v1 2025-08-10, v2 2025-08-31): ~199 Google Scholar citations by Sept 2026. Contributions: 4-component unified framework (System Inputs, Agent System, Environment, Optimisers), MOP->MOA->MAO->MASE development path, "Three Laws" (Endure, Excel, Evolve), taxonomy covering ~250 works across single-agent (behaviour/prompt/memory/tool/unified), multi-agent (construction, workflow/topology), domain-specific (biomed, programming, science, finance/legal) and evaluation/safety.
org_or_authors: ANative-Lab (formerly EvoAgentX org; University of Glasgow — Jinyuan Fang, Yanwen Peng, Xi Zhang, Yingxu Wang, Xinhao Yi, Guibin Zhang, Yi Xu, Bin Wu, Siwei Liu, Zihao Li, Zhaochun Ren, Nikos Aletras, Xi Wang, Han Zhou, Zaiqiao Meng)
safety_measures: None implemented (list only). The survey articulates the "Endure" law (maintain safety and stability during self-modification) and says safety, alignment and robustness are continuous requirements throughout the evolutionary lifecycle; Section 4.3 indexes safety benchmarks and guardrails (AgentHarm, RedCode, MobileSafetyBench, MACHIAVELLI, R-Judge, SafeLawBench, AutoDAN-Turbo, AGrail) but prescribes no concrete verification, sandboxing, or rollback procedure for accepted mutations.
