name: SkillOpt (incl. SkillOpt-Sleep)
org_or_authors: Microsoft Research (Yifan Yang, Ziyang Gong, Weiquan Huang, Qihao Yang, Ziwei Zhou, Zisu Huang, Yan Li, Xuemei Gao, Qi Dai, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Yuqing Yang, Dongdong Chen, Xue Yang, Chong Luo)
last_activity: 2026-09-05 (pushed_at); ~30 commits in the last 3 weeks, active community PRs
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.23904 (27 pages); citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); featured on Microsoft Research blog (2026-07-24), VentureBeat, The Decoder, Synced; integrated by gbrain (29.8k stars) and darwin-skill (5.9k stars)
mechanism: Two loops. (A) Research engine (skillopt-train): a frozen target model + a separate optimizer LLM (default GPT-5.5). Per step: (1) rollout target on a training batch (B=40) with the current SKILL.md -> scored trajectories; (2) reflect: optimizer analyzes failure and success minibatches (size 8, 16 parallel workers) and emits structured add/delete/replace edit patches; (3) hierarchical merge of patches; (4) rank and clip to L_t edits ("textual learning rate", default 4, cosine decay to floor 2); (5) apply -> candidate skill; (6) gate: roll out candidate on a held-out selection split (deterministic 2:1:7 train/sel/test) and accept only if score is strictly greater than the current score (ties rejected). Rejected edits plus the score drop they caused go into an epoch-local step buffer that is fed back to the optimizer. At each epoch boundary (from epoch 2): a "slow update" rolls out previous-epoch vs current skill on 20 shared samples, buckets items as improved/regressed/persistent-fail/stable-success and writes longitudinal guidance into a protected <!-- SLOW_UPDATE --> field (force-accepted by default, slow_update_gate_with_selection=false); and an optimizer-side "meta skill" memory is written but never shipped. Output: best_skill.md = highest selection-score snapshot. (B) SkillOpt-Sleep (nightly cron, separate package): harvest local Claude Code/Codex/Copilot/Cursor/Pi/OpenCode transcripts -> LLM miner extracts recurring tasks with programmatic checks or a rubric (LLM judge >=0.8 = pass) -> split train/val -> replay via backend (opt-in K dream rollouts for contrastive reflection, recall_k similar tasks from a persisted archive, synthetic variants) -> bounded edits to skill then to a long-term memory doc -> gate on val mean (opt-in per-task no-regression) -> stage proposal -> human `adopt`.
eval_loop: Signal = held-out selection-split hard score from a real verifier (exact match, executed openpyxl code compared cell-by-cell, ALFWorld success, MCQ label); soft/mixed metrics and an optional 'semantic density' bonus for imperative words are opt-in and were not used in the paper. Strict-improvement gate (ties rejected) + edit budget + rejected-edit buffer + protected slow-update field + best_skill snapshot that excludes force-injected slow-update text. Sleep adds staged review-then-adopt, evidence.jsonl audit chains, an output-contract guardrail for gate-free mode, opt-in gate_no_regression, and a paired A/B evalkit (McNemar + bootstrap CI). Demonstrated anti-drift value: on GPT-5.4-nano/SearchQA the ungated loop collapsed 0.554 -> 0.026 (learned 'answer with the document title') while the gated twin held 0.570 -> 0.570. But reward hacking is documented in real use: the optimizer reads raw judge regex text and writes it verbatim into the skill (#154), a heading-format judge artifact produced an accepted rule that forbids the skill's own format and dropped a required citation on another task, hidden by the val mean (#174/#175); gbrain-evals cat32 showed a heading-only scorer is gameable (1.00 proxy vs 0.28 independent judge).
key_results: Paper: 6 benchmarks x 7 models x 3 harnesses; best or tied on 52/52 cells; GPT-5.5 direct chat avg 58.8 -> 82.3 (+23.5; SpreadsheetBench +38.9, OfficeQA +39.0, LiveMath +29.3); +24.8 inside Codex, +19.1 inside Claude Code; beats per-cell oracle of 6 baselines (human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, EvoSkill) by +5.4. Only 1-4 edits accepted per run (median 2.5); final artifacts 379-1,995 tokens. Ablations: removing slow+meta update -22.5 on SpreadsheetBench; unbounded rewrite (no LR) -2.5 to -4.6; no rejected buffer -1.6 to -4.6; batch sizes insensitive. Transfer: cross-model +3.0 to +9.4, Codex<->Claude Code +43.6/+59.7, OlympiadBench->Omni-MATH +1.3 to +3.7; target-matched optimizer recovers 56-74% of strong-optimizer gain. Cost 0.6M-46M tokens per test point (21M-214M tokens per run). Sleep (5 nights x 10 tasks, single seed): SearchQA GPT-5.5 +3.1 to +5.6 gated; GPT-5.4-nano +11.9; SpreadsheetBench nano +3.6; 18-cell sweep mean only +0.53 (worst -2.4); gbrain-evals: 4 deficient seed skills 0.00 -> 1.00 held-out on both Claude Code and Codex, but a one-shot rewrite also reached 1.00.
limitations: Requires an automatic verifier or exact-match metric; single-seed results with +/-1-2 pt noise; open reproducibility issue #158 (LiveMath split was 124 vs paper's 125, fixed; DocVQA/OfficeQA/SpreadsheetBench score denominators still unexplained). Gate compares val-slice means so per-task regressions pass (real user: val=4 tasks, accepted edit damaged one task and improved none); optimizer sees raw judge text and Goodharts it into the skill; slow update bypasses the gate by default. Training is expensive (tens to hundreds of millions of tokens per benchmark). Single skill document, no library/composition. Sleep is a preview: 18-cell mean gain within noise, saturates after ~5 nights, no `revert` after adopt (#247), intent-level (non-checkable) improvements are dropped or mangled (#154), sensitivity sweep shows every deviation from the tuned recipe lowers gains. The research engine is offline benchmark prompt optimization (GEPA/TextGrad lineage) dressed in DL vocabulary; 'self-evolving' in the paper title is partly marketing. Only Sleep learns from the agent's own deployment data, and it is human-in-the-loop by default. gbrain-evals notes a one-shot rewrite matched the full loop on its simple tasks, so loop necessity is not shown there.
key_insight: Treat the skill file as the trainable parameters of a frozen agent and borrow optimizer discipline: bound edits per step (textual learning rate), accept only on strict held-out improvement, and feed rejected edits back as negative examples. The strict gate is what makes unattended text-space self-evolution safe (bounded downside vs a -52.8 pt collapse), and most of the gain comes from a handful (1-4) of accepted edits, not from wholesale rewrites.
safety_measures: Strict-improvement held-out gate (ties rejected); edit budget per step; rejected-edit buffer; protected slow-update field with best_skill snapshot kept clean; Sleep: stage-then-human-adopt (auto_adopt off by default, never for fan-out), read-only local harvest, secret redaction, sub-agent/plugin transcripts excluded, per-night evidence.jsonl audit, sandboxed replay (Codex workspace-write, Cursor read-only Ask mode, OpenCode MCP/plugins disabled, synthetic tools for tool-aware replay), no-network mock/handoff backends, output-contract guardrail in gate-free mode, opt-in gate_no_regression, versioned fail-closed adoption manifest with provenance hashes, immutable backups/receipts, cross-night locking, Copilot tools scoped not allow-all, managed-identity credentials restricted to Azure HTTPS.
open_gaps: Gate is an aggregate mean over a small val slice; per-task regressions are accepted (gate_no_regression is opt-in and only in Sleep, absent from the research trainer)
Optimizer receives raw judge/regex source text and copies checks verbatim into the skill (Goodhart); no separation of semantic feedback from scoring criteria
Fitness is a single benchmark's selection split; no in-loop held-out generalization or cross-task test, transfer measured only post-hoc
Epoch-boundary slow update is force-accepted by default, bypassing the validation gate
Single skill document only; no skill library, routing, composition, or cross-task transfer of learned rules (stated future work)
Requires a programmatic verifier; rubric/LLM-judge path is weak and intent-level improvements are dropped or mangled into shallow proxy rules
No revert/rollback after Sleep `adopt`, no online A/B or production monitoring of a deployed skill
Single-seed evaluation with +/-1-2 pt noise and unresolved score-denominator mismatches vs released splits
Cost 20M-214M tokens per benchmark run; no cost-aware or budget-constrained optimization
Does not evolve tools, workflow topology, harness code, or model weights; agent architecture is fixed
Nightly gains saturate after ~5 nights and the 18-cell sweep mean is within noise; no long-horizon (months) evidence
Multi-skill fan-out consolidates each skill independently; no modeling of skill interactions or shared memory writes
Optimizer-side meta skill is discarded per run, not reused across benchmarks or projects
Loop necessity vs one-shot rewrite not established on simple skills (gbrain-evals cat31)

name: CORAL (Human-Agent-Society)
org_or_authors: Human-Agent-Society / compounding-intelligence.ai — Ao Qu, Han Zheng, Zijian Zhou, Yihao Yan, ... Cathy Wu, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Jinhua Zhao, Paul Pu Liang (MIT, NUS, Stanford, Meta SI Lab)
date: Repo created 2026-03-16; public release 2026-03-18; paper arXiv:2604.01658 2026-04-03; COLM 2026 acceptance announced 2026-07-08
last_activity: 2026-09-08 (last push); v0.7.21 released 2026-09-06; new issues 2026-09-09; ~weekly dev→main promotions since March
venue_or_citations: COLM 2026 (accepted); arXiv:2604.01658. Citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); 123 forks, 20 open issues
mechanism: The evolving object is a user-supplied codebase ("other"), not the harness. `coral start` clones the repo, creates one git worktree per agent (branch coral/<id>), symlinks a shared `.coral/public/` (attempts/, notes/, skills/, roles/, agents/) into each worktree as `.claude/` (or `.codex/` etc.), and spawns N external coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code default; Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Kiro, DeepSeek Harness, Pi). Each agent reads a generated CORAL.md and runs plan→edit→`coral eval -m "..."`→reflect. `coral eval` is the only git path: it commits, writes a pending Attempt JSON, and blocks until a separate grader daemon checks out the commit in a detached worktree and writes back score+status (improved/baseline/regressed vs that agent's personal best). All attempts form a parent_hash DAG; agents branch via `coral checkout <hash>` from any attempt (theirs or a teammate's). Knowledge evolves in the shared filesystem: agents must write a note or skill after every eval (create-notes skill with lint), and self-author an evidence-backed role file with a generation counter. A HeartbeatRunner injects prompts on eval-count triggers: reflect (every 1), consolidate (every 10 global: synthesize notes, audit team roles/lanes/postures, extract skills), lint_wiki (spawn librarian subagent), and pivot on a per-agent plateau streak (default 5 non-improving real evals, epsilon-tolerant, cooldown). Agents can rewrite their own heartbeat schedule (`coral heartbeat set`). Optional islands (v0.6) partition agents with island-local shared state; every K global evals the top-scoring agent per island migrates (uniform/round_robin/score/weakest weighting), carrying attempts+role but leaving notes/skills behind. An optional warm-start research-only phase precedes coding. Optional apex_judge grader evolves its own rubric on plateau.
eval_loop: Signal = a user-written scalar grader (TaskGrader.evaluate → ScoreBundle, direction max/min), run by a long-lived daemon in a subprocess with SIGKILL timeout, inside `git worktree add --detach <commit>` under `.coral/private/grader_checkouts/` so concurrent agent edits cannot perturb grading; results written atomically. Hidden data (answer keys) lives in `.coral/private/` (denied to agents; Docker mode runs agents as unprivileged user), while the grader SOURCE is deliberately readable read-only so agents know exactly how they are scored (by design, invites specialization to the grader). Attempts are tagged budget_class real vs tune (`--tune` = cheaper sweep; excluded from leaderboard and plateau counter). Harbor benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, terminal-bench) use tiered eval (5→30→all instances gated on thresholds). Optional LLM rubric judges (static or self-evolving rubric) for open-ended artifacts, with feedback redaction levels. Drift/reward-hacking prevention is structural, not statistical: evaluator isolation, CLI-owned git, sandbox (srt FS/network enforcement or Docker), per-agent best-score comparison, plateau-triggered pivot, restart circuit breaker. There is no held-out set, no automatic rollback of regressions (agents are only told 'regressed' and must `coral checkout` themselves), and no validation of shared notes/skills before other agents consume them (open issues #67, #124).
limitations: Evidence is small-N and single-run: blog reports one run per config (no seeds, variance, or 1/2/4-agent scaling curve); heartbeat ablation is qualitative only ('agents share less without it'); only the notes/skills ablation has a number (-18.6% on kernel task). Erdős 'beats AlphaEvolve' margin is 0.38089 vs 0.38092, and the web-search variant discovered together.ai's published solution rather than deriving it. Baseline is OpenEvolve (open reimplementation), not AlphaEvolve itself; the paper summary also cites EvoX/ShinkaEvolve but exact table values were not retrievable. Cost/tokens not reported in the paper (blog: 'less than half the cost' on Erdős; hours of Opus 4.6 per run). Requires an authenticated external coding-agent CLI per agent (Claude Code/Codex subscriptions). Fitness must be a scalar per task; open-ended tasks depend on an LLM judge from the same model family as the worker. Shared memory has no validation layer, so hallucinated notes can become team doctrine (self-acknowledged in issues #67/#124); maintainers also report stalled attempts and tuning burning attempt budget (#72). Notes and skills do not persist across runs or tasks (each run reseeds from bundled templates). Human steering only at resume, not live. Docker-in-Docker unsupported for Harbor graders.
key_insight: Give a full coding agent the whole RETRIEVE→PROPOSE→EVALUATE→UPDATE loop instead of only PROPOSE (as AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve do), then make the harness's only jobs (a) an unhackable async grader and (b) periodic heartbeat interrupts (reflect/consolidate/pivot-on-plateau) that force agents to externalize knowledge into a shared filesystem — the blog's own finding is that without the interrupts, autonomous agents fixate and never write the notes/skills that make multi-agent gains (1363→1103 cycles) possible.
key_results: Kernel (Anthropic VLIW take-home, Opus 4.6, no web): seed 18,532 cycles; prior best-known 1,363; single CORAL agent 1,350 in 4.6h; 4 agents 1,103 in ~4.5h (24% better than single agent, 18-19% better than prior SOTA); OpenEvolve failed to beat 1,363. Erdős min-overlap C5: CORAL 0.38089 vs AlphaEvolve 0.38092 vs OpenEvolve 0.38111; reached 99% of AlphaEvolve score in 34 min vs 5.2h for OpenEvolve (claimed 10x faster, 7x fewer evals, 2.5x higher improved-attempt rate, <half the cost); with web search 0.380871→0.3808703. Stanford OpenVaccine (MLEBench split): 20.5% better MCRMSE than top human score, beating human in 2 evals. Paper adds: polyomino packing 89.4% coverage vs prior 87%; 36% of successful attempts descended from another agent's commit and cross-agent transfers had 17% improvement rate vs 9% average; disabling notes/skills regressed kernel result by 18.6%; 'best-known solution in 5-20 evals vs 100+ for traditional methods'.
safety_measures: Grader and hidden data in `.coral/private/` denied to agents (Docker: agents run as unprivileged user; host: opt-in `agents.isolate_user`); grader runs in separate venv + subprocess + detached worktree with SIGKILL timeout; CORAL owns git (agents never run git; `coral validate` rejects private data placed inside the visible grader package); workspace guard makes sibling worktrees read-only; optional `srt` sandbox provider with OS-level filesystem/network enforcement and allow-all proxy; optional LiteLLM gateway to intercept/log all model traffic; blocking tools (AskUserQuestion, plan mode) disabled for unmanned runs; manager health monitoring, exit classifier, restart-burst circuit breaker, auto-stop; run-level stop caps (max_real_attempts); constitution prompt asks for honesty/no deception (prompt-level only). No reported reward-hacking incidents; no automated detection of grader gaming beyond isolation.
open_gaps: No validation or quarantine gate on shared notes/skills before other agents consume them — hallucinated or overfit notes propagate as team doctrine (maintainers' own open issues #67, #124)
Fitness is a single visible scalar grader with readable source and no held-out evaluation; agents can specialize to the exact scoring code and nothing measures generalization
No automatic regression handling: a worse attempt is only labeled 'regressed'; no auto-revert, no best-of selection or final-artifact promotion policy — agent must manually `coral checkout`
No cross-run or cross-task transfer: notes/skills/roles live in results/<run>/.coral/ and every run reseeds from static bundled templates; nothing learned in run N is available in run N+1

Harness parameters are hand-set and static (heartbeat cadence every 1/10, plateau 5, migration every 16, prompts): the loop does not meta-optimize its own schedule, prompts, or team composition (issue #74 'gradient-style meta-evolve' open)
Population management ranks migrants by score window only; no novelty/diversity measure (MAP-Elites style), so the 'copycatting' convergence the blog documents is unmitigated
Evidence lacks seeds/variance and an agent-count scaling curve; heartbeat contribution is asserted qualitatively, not ablated numerically
Budget accounting is weak: stalled/infra-killed attempts consume the attempt budget and token cost is not tracked as a first-class metric (issue #72; gateway optional)
Open-ended tasks rely on an LLM judge (optionally self-evolving rubric) from the same model family as the worker with no calibration against judge gaming
Human steering is resume-only; no live human-in-the-loop injection into a running population

name: ACE: Agentic Context Engineering (ace-agent/ace)
org_or_authors: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, ..., James Zou, Kunle Olukotun — Stanford University / SambaNova Systems / UC Berkeley
last_activity: 2026-08-24 (commit 82709de: parallelize ComBEE curator proposals with LLM reducer); ace-appworld submodule pushed 2026-07-24; open PR #40 (DeepSeek provider) 2026-08-15; issue #41 (Terminal-Bench prompts) 2026-08-28
venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted, per team blog post 2026-01-30); arXiv 2510.04618. Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited, arXiv unreachable from this network); widely cited as the reference point for 'evolving playbook' context adaptation. 168 forks.
mechanism: The evolving artifact is a single plaintext 'playbook': markdown sections whose lines are itemized bullets `[slug-00042] helpful=X harmful=Y :: advice`. Per training sample (ace/ace.py `_train_single_sample`): (1) Generator answers with the full playbook in-prompt and self-reports which bullet_ids it used. (2) Correctness is checked against ground truth via `data_processor.answer_is_correct`. If wrong, up to `max_num_rounds` (3) Reflector→regenerate loops run; the Reflector (with GT or, in no-GT mode, only environment feedback) emits error_identification/root_cause/key_insight plus helpful/harmful/neutral tags for used bullets, which are applied by `update_bullet_counts` (pure string counter increment). If correct, the Reflector still runs to tag helpful bullets. (3) Every `curator_frequency` steps the Curator sees playbook + stats + latest reflection and emits JSON operations; `apply_curator_operations` implements ONLY `ADD` (UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE/CREATE_META are commented-out TODOs). Optional `BulletpointAnalyzer` (sentence-transformers + FAISS, cosine ≥0.9) LLM-merges near-duplicates. (4) Post-curate regeneration is logged. Offline mode: iterate epochs over train set, evaluate on val every `eval_steps`, keep `best_playbook` = argmax val accuracy. Online mode: windowed test-then-train on the test stream, no checkpoint selection. ACEBatch/ComBEE (2026): parallel gen+reflect over a mini-batch, augmented shuffling (duplicate reflections p×), ⌊√n⌋ curator groups propose ADDs from the same snapshot in parallel, one LLM 'reducer' call dedups into final ADDs applied once. Single lineage, no population, same LLM (DeepSeek-V3.1) for all three roles.
eval_loop: Signal = per-sample exact/format-normalized correctness against ground-truth labels (finance/Mind2Web) or AppWorld task-goal completion; in 'no_GT' mode the Reflector sees only environment/execution feedback but the retry loop still uses `answer_is_correct` with the target (issue #35 flags this inconsistency). Bullet-level credit is an LLM judgment (Reflector tags bullets the Generator self-reported using) stored as helpful/harmful counters — these are shown to the Curator as stats but never used programmatically to prune. Drift/reward-hacking guards are weak: Curator output is JSON-schema validated and skipped on parse failure; offline mode selects the best whole-playbook checkpoint by held-out validation accuracy (the only regression guard); online mode has none; ComBEE rolls back Phase-2 edits only on API errors, not on accuracy drops. Paper's context-collapse case study (Dynamic Cheatsheet: 18,282→122 tokens at one step, acc 66.7→57.1, below base 63.7) motivates append-only deltas, but the released code's answer is monotone growth rather than verified refinement.
key_results: Paper (DeepSeek-V3.1 non-thinking for all roles): AppWorld ReAct base avg 42.4 → ACE offline 59.4 (w/ GT), 57.2 (execution feedback only) vs ICL 46.0, GEPA 46.4; online ACE 59.5 vs Dynamic Cheatsheet 51.9; +10.6% avg, +17.1% on test-challenge; matched IBM-CUGA (GPT-4.1, 60.3) on leaderboard Sept-2025 and beat it on test-challenge. Finance: FiNER 70.7→78.3, Formula 67.5→85.5 (offline w/ GT), +8.6% avg; without GT FiNER fell to ~67.3 (below base). Ablation: Reflector, multi-epoch, and offline warm-up each add ~2-4 pts (offline ~55.1→56.8→59.4; online ~56.1→59.5 with warm-up). Cost: offline AppWorld ACE 357 rollouts / 9,517s vs GEPA 1,434 / 53,898s (-75.1% rollouts, -82.3% latency); online FiNER -91.5% latency, -83.6% tokens vs DC. Repo-side: 1,310 stars; production use reported at Anyshift (SRE agent, 30% faster RCA) since Oct 2025; third-party issue #26 reports +13.3% val / +8% test on a lending-compliance task but val oscillating 53-93% as playbook bloats. Team blog (2026-04) admits AppWorld playbooks reach ~174k tokens; embedding/LLM retrieval keeps 59-65% of the gain at ~2% of tokens, RLM retrieval hurts.
limitations: Released curator is ADD-only; the paper's 'grow-and-refine' pruning/merging by harmful counters is not implemented (issue #26, roadmap #29 promise DELETE/MERGE 'soon' as of Feb 2026, still absent Aug 2026). Playbook grows monotonically (>100K tokens by ~300 samples, issue #11) and `playbook_token_budget` is ignored by code; long-context cost is deferred to KV caching. Gains depend on reliable feedback: w/o GT, FiNER dropped below the unadapted baseline, showing reflections can pollute context and nothing detects it. Only one regression guard (offline best-val checkpoint); online mode can silently degrade. Bullet credit assignment relies on Generator self-reported bullet_ids and LLM tags (no counterfactual verification). Prompts hand-tuned per dataset; same strong model needed for all three roles. Eval limited to 3 domains (AppWorld, FiNER/Formula, Mind2Web); AppWorld requires a custom fork of the simulator. Not packaged, provider-locked (SambaNova/Together/OpenAI/CommonStack), no local LLM support. Baseline comparisons (GEPA, DC) are the authors' own reimplementations. 'Self-improving' applies to the context only; model and harness are static.
key_insight: Never let the LLM rewrite its accumulated context wholesale: represent experience as an itemized, ID-addressed ledger of bullets with provenance counters, split doing (Generator), diagnosing (Reflector), and editing (Curator) into separate calls, and have the editor emit only small localized deltas — this avoids brevity bias and context collapse, makes each update cheap (tiny curator output, KV-cacheable prefix), and beats prompt optimizers like GEPA at a fraction of the rollouts.
open_gaps: Curator cannot UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE — implement counter-driven pruning (harmful>=helpful, unused-after-N-steps) and LLM merge as first-class verified ops; helpful/harmful counters currently never affect the playbook
No per-delta acceptance test: every curator ADD is applied unconditionally; a framework should A/B each delta (or batch) on a held-out slice and reject/rollback regressions, in online mode too
Fitness is single in-distribution benchmark accuracy; no cross-task or cross-domain transfer of playbooks, no held-out-domain generalization measurement, no shared/hierarchical playbook across tasks
Requires ground-truth labels or trustworthy execution feedback; no mechanism to estimate reflection reliability or quarantine low-confidence insights (w/o GT FiNER fell below baseline)

Whole playbook is injected into every prompt; retrieval only exists as an unmerged PR (#34) and the team's own study shows top-k retrieval loses 35-41% of the gain — need structure-aware retrieval or hierarchical playbooks
Credit assignment is Generator self-reported bullet usage + LLM tags; no counterfactual ablation of bullets, so harmful bullets with zero citations are invisible
Single lineage, no archive/population or crossover of playbooks; ComBEE parallel proposals are reduced by one LLM call with no diversity preservation
Role prompts (generator/reflector/curator) are static and hand-tuned per dataset (issues #37/#38); no meta-level evolution of the reflector/curator instructions
Token budget parameter is ignored by code; no enforced size control, compaction, or tiering of bullets by recency/utility
Not a library: no pip package (#32), provider-locked clients, no local model support (#30); AppWorld path needs a custom simulator fork — hard for app developers to embed in an existing agent loop
No tool/skill evolution: playbook holds text advice only; cannot accumulate executable snippets, tool wrappers, or verified procedures
safety_measures: Minimal: curator JSON is schema-validated and malformed/unsupported ops are skipped (only ADD executed); API-error samples excluded from playbook updates; offline mode keeps best-by-validation checkpoint; ComBEE rolls back Phase-2 edits on Phase-3 API errors. No content filtering of injected bullets, no human review gate, no adversarial-feedback defense, no bound on playbook size; AppWorld runs in its own simulated sandbox.

name: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
org_or_authors: Hexo AI (Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, Alesia Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran)
last_activity: 2026-08-26 (v0.6.0 on PyPI as `sia-agent`; last commits: OpenRouter provider, Windows venv fix)
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.27276; featured on HuggingFace Daily Papers; citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited). 257 forks, 17 open issues.
mechanism: Three LLM roles in a strictly linear chain, `sia run --task X --max_gen N --focus {harness|weights}`. Gen 1: Meta-Agent (Claude Agent SDK / OpenHands / pydantic-ai) reads task.md, sample task descriptions, a reference_target_agent.py and a sample trajectory, and writes `gen_1/target_agent.py`. Each gen: orchestrator runs `python target_agent.py --dataset_dir --working_dir` in a per-run venv (optional Docker sandbox), which calls the target model and logs agent_execution.json; then runs the task's `evaluate.py --gen-dir` against `data/private/` to write results.json; then appends an LLM-written summary + metric deltas + code-size deltas to `context.md`. Feedback-Agent gets: current target_agent.py, task.md, SUCCESS/FAILED status, the full results.json dump, the first 3 trajectories truncated to 1000 chars each, and a pointer to context.md/prior improvement.md files (it can read the filesystem). It must write `gen_{n+1}/improvement.md` and `target_agent.py` (plus optional requirements.txt). Loop repeats until max_gen. In `--focus weights` mode the same loop instead mutates `train.py`: Meta-Agent is given an embedded "RL Integration Guide" and must implement tinker-cookbook Env/EnvGroupBuilder/RLDataset/RLDatasetBuilder (GRPO, LoRA, default Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on Thinking Machines' Tinker; code execution via Modal or SandboxFusion; majority-vote pseudo-reward suggested when labels are hidden). The Feedback-Agent then rewrites reward shaping/env design per generation; a COMPLETED file early-stops. So weights are updated by an LLM-authored RL pipeline that is itself evolved. In code, harness and weights are mutually exclusive per run; the paper's "W+H" interleaving is not implemented as an in-loop policy.
eval_loop: Signal = whatever the task's `evaluate.py` writes to results.json (scored against data/private/), injected verbatim into the next feedback prompt; in weights mode the GRPO reward is defined by the agent-written EnvGroupBuilder. There is NO acceptance gate: gen n+1 is always derived from gen n even if n regressed; no rollback to best, no archive/population, no statistical test. "Best generation" is only computed post-hoc in context_manager.finalize() by max self-reported `accuracy`. Drift/Goodhart prevention is documentation-only (docs/evaluator_design.md checklist; paper names "coupled co-evolutionary Goodharting" as an open risk). Community issues show the loop is exploitable: #59 (evaluator computed accuracy over answered items, so abstaining raised the score to 75% reported vs 4.5% real); #60 (feedback agent sees ~0.3% of trajectory evidence, chosen by filename not outcome; observed 62.1→57.1→46.5% decline over 3 gens); #61 (HTTP 429s indistinguishable from wrong answers); #36 (results.json dump leaks held-out gold answers for longcot-chess into the feedback prompt).
key_results: Paper (single runs, no seeds/variance, generation counts unstated): LawBench charge classification (191 classes) prior SOTA 45.0% → SIA-H 50.0% → SIA-W+H 70.1% (the "56.6%" is relative gain over initial baseline). AlphaFold-3 TriMul Triton kernel on H100: 12,483µs → 1,017µs (91.9% reduction, 14.02x; 12.4% faster than prior 1,161µs). scRNA-seq denoising mse_norm: SIA-H 0.241 → SIA-W+H 0.289 (prior SOTA 0.240; "502%" over initial baseline). README claims #1 on MLE-Bench Hard (chart only, no numbers). No SIA-W-only ablation reported. LoRA checkpoints not released (issue #35 open). Repo ships 4 tasks (gpqa, lawbench, longcot-chess, spaceship-titanic — the last without a bundled evaluator), CI, golden-prompt tests, a live web dashboard.
limitations: Linear single-lineage loop with no selection, rollback, or archive; feedback evidence is 3 truncated trajectories picked by filename; fitness is one task's evaluator with no held-out generalization or transfer check despite the prompt saying "don't optimize for this task"; evaluator can be gamed (abstention inflates accuracy) and can leak gold answers into the feedback prompt; infra failures pollute the signal. Weights mode requires Tinker + Modal/SandboxFusion accounts (no local-GPU path), has zero test coverage, and harness/weights cannot run in the same loop. Paper results are single-run with no variance, no generation counts, no SIA-W ablation, no compute cost, no released weights. Default `--sandbox none` executes LLM-written code on the host.
key_insight: Treat the RL training pipeline (env, reward function, dataset builder) as just another source file the meta-loop can rewrite: by having the Feedback-Agent author `train.py` for a hosted fine-tuning API in the same rewrite-from-logs loop it uses for `target_agent.py`, weight updates become an artifact of harness evolution rather than a separate hand-built system — harness edits shape how the model searches/acts, weight edits build domain intuition prompts cannot instil.
safety_measures: Optional `--sandbox docker` (no network) for target-agent execution; default is host execution. data/private/ held-out split is a convention, not enforced (feedback agent has filesystem access). Evaluator-design checklist (anti-gaming advice) is documentation only. Network calls capped at 60s/2 retries by prompt instruction. No rollback, no diff review, no human-in-the-loop gate between generations. SECURITY.md documents the threat model.
open_gaps: No acceptance gate or rollback: gen n+1 is always built from gen n even when n regressed; add best-so-far parent selection, McNemar/paired significance test, or a population/archive (MAP-Elites style) before promoting

Fitness is a single task evaluator on one private split with no held-out or perturbed slice; no measurement of whether harness improvements transfer to other tasks (each run restarts from the reference agent)
Feedback evidence selection is positional (first 3 trajectories, 1000 chars each): no failure-driven sampling, no full failure transcripts, no clustering of error modes

Self-reported metrics are gameable (abstention raises accuracy; results.json can leak gold answers); need harness-owned coverage floors, gold-stripped eval summaries, and a fixed evaluator the agent cannot author
Infrastructure failures (429/timeouts/truncation) are conflated with reasoning failures in the score; no per-item failure taxonomy
Harness and weights are mutually exclusive per run (`--focus` XOR); no in-loop policy that decides when to spend budget on scaffold edits vs. RL, so the paper's W+H interleaving is manual
Weight updates require Tinker + Modal accounts; no local-GPU/LoRA path, no tests for weights mode, no released checkpoints, so app developers cannot reproduce W results

The evaluator, task set, and curriculum are frozen: the loop cannot generate new tasks, harden its own grader, or co-evolve verifiers against Goodharting (the paper names this risk but offers no mechanism)
No compute/cost accounting or budget-aware stopping in harness mode (fixed max_gen); no memory of failed approaches beyond an LLM-summarized context.md
Single-lineage, single-agent design: no parallel candidate generation, no crossover between runs, no reuse of improvements across tasks

name: Evolver (EvoMap)
org_or_authors: EvoMap (evomap.ai; maintainer handle autogame-17; paper authors Junjie Wang, Yiming Ren, Haoyang Zhang, EvoMap/Tsinghua)
last_activity: 2026-09-06 (push; release v2.0.33; latest issues 2026-09-07)
venue_or_citations: arXiv:2604.15097 (self-authored by EvoMap, not peer-reviewed, citation count unavailable); npm ~5.9k downloads/month; 843 forks
mechanism: Evolver is a Node CLI that runs beside a coding agent (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex hooks) in a git repo. Per cycle (verified in readable v1.28 source; current core is obfuscated): (1) Regex-scan session transcripts/logs/MEMORY.md into string "signals" (log_error, errsig:<hash>, perf_bottleneck, user_feature_request, stagnation flags). (2) Select a Gene from genes.json by counting substring/regex hits of gene.signals_match against signals. A memory-graph JSONL of signal->gene outcomes (30-day half-life) supplies a preferred gene and bans genes with expected success <0.18 after 2+ attempts; FailedCapsules with >=0.6 signal overlap ban a gene after 2 failures; "drift" picks a random top-N gene with probability 1/sqrt(pool size). (3) Build a Mutation (category repair/optimize/innovate from signals plus strategy preset) and a PersonalityState (five scalar dials nudged +/-0.05-0.1 by fixed rules; best key chosen by Laplace-smoothed success rate). (4) Emit a "GEP" prompt embedding the gene's strategy steps, an output schema for five JSON objects, recent history and failed capsules; the host spawns a sub-agent that edits code. (5) Solidify: compute git blast radius vs gene.constraints (max_files, forbidden_paths), run gene.validation commands (node/npm/npx only, 180s), canary-load index.js, optional LLM review; success -> score 0.85 else 0.2 with git stash/reset rollback; append parent-linked EvolutionEvent, Capsule (diff+strategy) or FailedCapsule; add epigenetic mark +/-0.1 per env fingerprint; if nothing matched, auto-create a boilerplate gene keyed by signal hash. (6) Capsules with score>=0.7, streak>=2 and safe blast radius auto-publish to EvoMap Hub, where other nodes fetch and validate them. v2 adds ingest --distill (excerpt session turns into gene strategies) -> review -> inject session-start.
eval_loop: Acceptance is binary pass/fail of gene-declared validation commands plus blast-radius/forbidden-path constraint checks and a canary import; the recorded score is a constant (0.85/0.2), not a task metric. Anti-drift: circuit breaker forces 'innovate' after 3 consecutive failed repairs; signals seen in 3+ of last 8 events are suppressed; genes banned via decayed outcome ledger; history block in prompt says 'do not repeat intent+signal+gene'. Reward hacking is weakly guarded: the agent authors gene validation commands itself (a bundled distilled gene validates with 'node --version'), LLM review is off by default, and hub validators re-run only the proposer's own claimed commands. Paper evidence: 4,590 trials, 45 sci-code scenarios, Gemini 3/3.1 Pro; CritPt 70 problems, 9.1->18.57% and 17.7->27.14% (13/70 and 19/70), single benchmark, same-org authors. An offline trigger-shift replay evaluator exists but is diagnostic only and not wired into selection.
limitations: 27 of 53 core src/gep files are javascript-obfuscated with RC4 string encryption and anti-debug traps; git history was rewritten to start 2026-04-16 and v2 ships as 70-100MB binaries, so the current loop cannot be audited despite 'auditable evolution' branding. Fitness never measures task performance; a change that passes self-declared node scripts is 'success'. Signal extraction is regex on log text; gene selection is keyword counting; auto-created genes carry a fixed generic strategy, so 'genes' accumulate mostly as signal keys, not learned strategy. Independent closed-loop tests (issues #624, #625, N=5 runs) found v2 inject passes only summary labels, not strategy text, so gains vanish, and auto-distilled strategies mix success prose with truncated fixes and can be worse than no injection. 'evolver cycle' refuses runners outside claude/codex/gemini (#627); hub validator tasks fail 91% due to sandbox blocking 'node -e' (#607). Heavy coupling to EvoMap Hub economy (ATP credits, worker pool, leaderboards). Personality 'evolution' is rule-based scalar nudges with no demonstrated effect. Paper is not peer-reviewed, Gemini-only, and CritPt gains are small-N. Hermes similarity dispute and license shift make the project's future openness uncertain.
key_insight: Encode accumulated agent experience as compact structured 'genes' (trigger signals -> strategy steps -> AVOID cues -> validation hooks, ~230 tokens) rather than long skill docs, and make every self-modification a git-scoped, validation-gated, rollback-able event logged in a signal->gene outcome ledger so selection can ban low-yield paths and share validated capsules across nodes.
key_results: Paper (arXiv:2604.15097): across 4,590 trials on 45 scientific code tasks with Gemini 3 / 3.1 Pro, Skill docs gave unstable signal (overview section -4.7pp, workflow +1.5pp) while genes were robust to structural perturbation but sensitive to semantic errors (~49% with wrong algorithm/domain); failure history distilled into compact AVOID cues beat appended raw failures. CritPt (70 problems): OpenClaw+EvoMap went Beta 0% -> v2.1 17.14% -> v2.2 18.57% vs 9.1% base (Gemini 3 Pro), and 17.7% -> 27.14% (Gemini 3.1 Pro), with tokens rising then falling across versions. Repo: 9,055 stars, 843 forks, ~5.9k npm downloads/month, 34 tags since April, v2.0.33 binaries. Third-party N=5 test: strategy-text injection cut trap errors 11->4 and tokens -55%, but the official inject channel gave 4->6 and +13.8% tokens.
open_gaps: Fitness is a constant 0.85/0.2 derived from self-declared validation commands; no task-level or held-out benchmark score enters gene selection
Proposer and verifier are the same agent: genes carry their own validation commands (e.g. 'node --version'), so a gene-independent, tamper-proof evaluator is missing
Gene selection is substring/regex hit counting over regex-extracted log signals; no semantic retrieval or embedding match of situation to strategy

Auto-created genes get a boilerplate strategy and auto-distilled strategies are truncated excerpts of the agent's own turns; no quality gate or LLM refinement that verifies a strategy is actionable before injection
Closed-loop transfer is unverified by maintainers: v2 inject session-start drops strategy text (issue #624), so learned fixes do not reach the next session
No cross-task or cross-project generalization measurement; the trigger-shift evaluator is offline-only and not fed back into selection or gene pruning
Flat gene list with no population/archive of competing variants, no crossover, no explicit exploration budget beyond random drift 1/sqrt(N)
Core loop is obfuscated and v2 is binary-only, and 'evolver cycle' refuses non-allowlisted runners, so it cannot be audited, extended, or used with custom harnesses
Blast radius is file/line counts, not semantic risk; protected paths are a static list
Personality dials and strategy presets are rule-nudged scalars with no demonstrated causal effect on outcomes
Only evidence is a same-org arXiv paper on Gemini models and a 70-problem benchmark; no independent replication of the gene-vs-skill claim
safety_measures: Git-based rollback on failed solidify (stash default since 1.80.8, hard reset or none configurable); validation commands whitelisted to node/npm/npx with no shell operators or command substitution, 180s timeout; canary child-process import of index.js before commit; blast-radius limits (max_files, forbidden_paths) and destructive-change detection on protected core files; --review human-in-the-loop mode; optional LLM diff review (off by default, fails closed since Aug 2026); external hub assets staged in a candidate zone and promoted only with --validated; credential redaction before publishing; EVOLVE_ALLOW_SELF_MODIFY defaults false to keep the evolver from editing its own source; repair-loop circuit breaker; load and active-session backoff guards.
sources_read: https://github.com/EvoMap/evolver (metadata, README, SKILL.md, commits, releases, tags, forks)
https://github.com/bit-cook/evolver (v1.28.0 readable fork: src/evolve.js, src/gep/selector.js, solidify.js, memoryGraph.js, mutation.js, personality.js, prompt.js, signals.js, llmReview.js)

name: SkillClaw: Let Skills Evolve Collectively with Agentic Evolver
org_or_authors: AMAP-ML (Alibaba Amap); Ziyu Ma, Shidong Yang, Yuxiang Ji, Xucong Wang, Yong Wang, Yiming Hu, Tongwen Huang, Xiangxiang Chu
last_activity: 2026-08-17 (last push: batch of bug-fix merges). Open issue #89 (2026-09-09) asks if the project is abandoned; unanswered.
venue_or_citations: arXiv:2604.08377 (cs.AI, cs.CL), preprint only; Hugging Face Daily Papers #2 (2026-04-10), 294 upvotes; 259 forks; citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited).
mechanism: Two components joined only by shared object storage (local FS / OSS / S3 / Nacos) under a group_id. (1) Client proxy: a local OpenAI/Anthropic/Responses-compatible API proxy that the agent (Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, ...) is repointed to. Per request it appends an `<available_skills>` XML catalog (name/description/location, capped ~30k chars) to the system prompt so the model lazily `read`s SKILL.md files; it records every turn (prompt, response, tool calls/results/errors), infers `read_skills`/`modified_skills` from tool calls, optionally scores each turn with a PRM (LLM judge voting +1/0/-1, majority of M samples, adapted from MetaClaw), and uploads session JSON to `{group}/sessions/`. (2) Evolve server polls (default 600s), drains queued sessions and runs a fixed 3-stage `workflow` engine: Summarize (programmatic lossless trajectory + LLM causal summary; optional LLM session judge backfills a 0-1 score weighted 0.55 completion/0.30 quality/0.05 efficiency/0.10 tool-use) -> Aggregate (sessions grouped by each skill they read/modified; no-skill bucket separate) -> Execute (one LLM call per skill group with current SKILL.md + up to 30 sessions of evidence chooses improve_skill / optimize_description / create_skill / skip under a heavily conservative editing prompt; no-skill bucket -> create_skill/skip). Same-name SHA conflicts are LLM-merged. Accepted output overwrites `{group}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, bumps a version registry (content SHA, <=20 history entries), stores a version bundle snapshot and manifest; clients poll/pull and hot-reload. Optional gates: LLM skill verifier (off by default, threshold 0.75) and `validated` publish mode where idle clients replay <=3 single-turn prompts with baseline vs candidate skill in the system prompt, PRM-score both, and accept if candidate_mean >= 0.75 and >= baseline. Alternative `agent` engine: an OpenClaw agent edits a skills/ workspace following EVOLVE_AGENTS.md (history/ ledger, self-validation instructions); every changed file is uploaded with no programmatic gate.
eval_loop: Signal is almost entirely LLM judgment, no ground truth: (a) per-turn PRM = LLM judge majority vote on helpfulness (+1/0/-1) of the response to the instruction; (b) session-level LLM judge (0-1 weighted score) that overrides PRM; (c) the evolver LLM itself decides skip vs edit from summaries + these scores. Acceptance by default is 'direct' publish with verifier OFF, so the evolver's own output is the fitness. Opt-in gates: an LLM verifier (grounded_in_evidence / preserves_existing_value / specificity / safe_to_publish, threshold 0.75) and client replay validation (3 single-turn text replays, no tool execution, candidate vs baseline PRM means, 1 approval / 1 rejection thresholds by default). Drift/reward-hacking mitigation is prompt-based: 'prefer skip', preserve API facts, distinguish skill vs agent vs environment failures, targeted edits not rewrites, LLM merge on conflicts, versioned snapshots (no automatic rollback or post-publish monitoring). The paper claims a sandbox A/B of candidate s' vs deployed s on task success and execution stability with 'monotonic capability growth', but no such benchmark harness exists in the repo (issue #49 confirms the WildClawBench numbers are not reproducible from the code).
key_results: Paper (numbers via alphaxiv overview; arXiv full text unreachable in this session): 8 concurrent users over 6 days on WildClawBench (6 domains) with Qwen3-Max as backbone. Search & Retrieval 22.73% -> 34.55% (+52.0% relative); Creative Synthesis 11.57% -> 21.80% (+88.4% rel); Safety & Alignment 24.00% -> 32.00% (+33.3% rel); Social Interaction +11.7% rel; a 'save report' task 28.3% -> 100.0%. Two domains and the overall average were not surfaced; no ablations, no comparison to other skill/memory-learning baselines, evolver model and initial skill seed not disclosed. Repo: 2.6k stars / 259 forks in 5 months, HF Daily Papers #2 (294 upvotes), integrations for Hermes/OpenClaw/QwenPaw/Codex/Claude Code, dashboard, Nacos lifecycle; a third-party review (issue #56) rated it 70/100 'research tool, not production'.
limitations: No execution-grounded fitness in the shipped loop (all judges are LLMs; replay validation is single-turn text without tools); verifier and validated-publish are off by default, so evolved skills go straight to the group store; no rollback command or post-publish regression detection despite version snapshots; same LLM family generates and judges; one converging skill per name for a whole group (heterogeneous environments get LLM-merged, no per-user forks); attribution is 'skill was read', not counterfactual benefit; evidence capped at 30 sessions/group and 8 for the verifier; session boundaries rely on proxy heuristics unless the agent sends headers; group-wide poisoning surface (any member's sessions steer shared skills; two path-traversal bugs #68/#69 already found); proxy rewrites agent config files on startup (#71); Windows has no installer; paper eval is 8 users x 6 days on one self-built benchmark with low absolute scores and is not reproducible from the repo (#49); maintenance appears stalled since 2026-08-17 (#89).
key_insight: Put the learning loop in a protocol-level proxy between the agent and the model so every real session from every user/agent/device is captured with zero user effort, group trajectories by the skill they actually touched to form natural cross-user control experiments, and let a deliberately conservative 'skill engineer' LLM choose improve / optimize-description / create / skip per group, syncing the result back to everyone through a shared versioned SKILL.md store.
open_gaps: No execution-grounded acceptance: build a sandboxed re-execution harness that replays tool-using sessions with candidate vs deployed skill and measures task success, instead of single-turn text replay scored by an LLM PRM

Regression gate is opt-in and LLM-only; default publish is direct with verifier off — need mandatory pre-publish gating plus post-publish monitoring of per-skill session scores with automatic rollback to the archived version bundle
Attribution is 'skill was read', not 'skill helped': add counterfactual A/B (withhold/inject skill on matched tasks) to estimate each skill's causal value before editing it
Single converging skill per name for the whole group: no per-user/per-environment forks, overrides, or conditional sections; heterogeneous ports/APIs/OS facts get LLM-merged into one document
Generator and judge are the same LLM family with no held-out task set — no defense against the evolver and verifier agreeing on plausible-but-wrong edits
Library-level consolidation missing: near-duplicate or stale skills are only avoided by showing the evolver a list of names; no embedding-based dedup, pruning, or usage-decay of unread skills
Flat catalog injection capped at 30k chars with no retrieval/ranking — will not scale as the shared library grows
Trust/provenance: any group member's sessions (including prompt-injected tool outputs) can steer shared skills; no per-contributor weighting, quarantine, or diff review before group-wide propagation
Evidence budget and cost are unmanaged: 30 sessions/group/cycle, 8 for the verifier, 100k-token summaries, no token accounting or cost-aware scheduling
Evaluation is not reproducible from the repo (no benchmark scripts, seeds, task split, or raw outputs) and lacks ablations (no-validation, single-user vs multi-user, evolver model choice)
safety_measures: Prompt-level conservatism (prefer skip, targeted edits, preserve endpoints/ports/payload facts, do not add generic advice, distinguish skill vs agent vs environment failures); opt-in LLM verifier gate (threshold 0.75) and opt-in 'validated' publish mode with client replay votes (required results/approvals/min mean score/max rejections thresholds); Nacos 'review'/'draft' publish modes for human review; version registry with content SHA, capped history and per-version bundle snapshots (manual restore only); LLM merge on same-name conflicts; agent engine confined to a workspace, instructed to self-validate and keep a history/ evidence ledger; path-safety rejection of unsafe bundle paths (#81); `doctor`/`restore` commands to undo agent-config rewrites; daily quota and idle-only execution for client validation. No human-in-the-loop by default and no automatic rollback.

name: Reef (reef-infra) — continual learning infra for self-improving agents
org_or_authors: Human-Agent-Society (academic collective; ~25 listed members incl. Paul Liang (MIT), Ao Qu, Bo Liu, Zijian Zhou, Hanfei Yu, Haoze He, Xuan Jiang; same org as CORAL, COLM 2026). 19 GitHub contributors.
date: 2026-08-31 (public repo created; PyPI v0.0.1 2026-09-01, v0.0.2 2026-09-02; pre-launch history lived in a private 'reef-archive')
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; ~30 merged PRs in the last 4 days)
venue_or_citations: No paper of its own; GitHub launch (954 stars / 63 forks in 11 days). Cookbook reproduces SAO (arXiv:2607.07508), SkillClaw (arXiv:2604.08377), GEPA, Meta-Harness (stanford-iris-lab), TTT-Discover, OpenClaw-RL, CORAL (COLM 2026).
mechanism: Reef is a serving proxy plus a versioned release pipeline; the actual optimizer is a pluggable 'recipe'. Loop (Serve -> Observe -> Grow -> Commit): (1) Agents call an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint with an `x-reef-scenario` header; every response returns an `x-reef-agent-record-id` receipt and the exchange is stored (for weight training, sampled tokens + rollout logprobs too). (2) Clients POST /reef/report with a score and/or free-text feedback referencing receipts; a processor applies a score window (`max_score`, default keeps only failures for harness evolution) and batches `batch_size` eligible records. (3) A step runs the recipe. Weight path: Slime/Megatron trains (SAO = one rollout per step; OpenClaw-RL, TTT-Discover, CORAL grouped rewards), weights hot-sync to SGLang as a LiveWeightArtifactRef, checkpoints become LoRA/full releases. Harness path (cordis backend): the harness is a composition tree of nodes (rules, skills, config, code_extension; on the native adapter also tools, hooks, subagents and the loop graph); `propose(nodes, samples, models, manifest, rejected, sources, requests)` returns one Mutation (create/update/remove) or a composite sequence; the candidate and the incumbent tree each run every fixed task (`2 x tasks x episode_repeats` headless episodes, interleaved) and `evaluate` scores each; `decide` publishes iff wins - losses > `min_win_margin`, else the snapshot is restored and the rejected proposal is fed back to the next `propose`. (4) Accepted candidates are appended to an immutable git-LFS release chain; running clients (reef-pi, reef-native serve) mount the new release without restart. Extras: `promote_failures` adds real failing prompts to the gate suite; `recheck_every` re-gates the last publish and rolls back one step; `review_kinds` holds code wins as pending releases until a human promotes; bubblewrap sandbox for episodes; `hybrid` mode lets a person request a change in plain words through the same gate.
eval_loop: Per recipe, not universal. Harness path: a fixed, small task suite with a programmatic scorer (tutorial: 3 exact-last-line coding tasks) run paired on candidate vs incumbent; W/L/T tally with a configurable noise margin; rejected proposals are memorised (`max_rejected_history`) so the proposer stops re-proposing them; optional periodic recheck rolls back one bad publish; GEPA recipe uses a Pareto archive + strict mean improvement on a 45-problem validation set; Meta-Harness uses strict mean improvement over the incumbent's admitted score. Weight path: verifier rewards (boxed-answer equivalence, Harbor test verifiers, benchmark judges) drive gradient steps, and the default selector is `AlwaysSelect` — every successfully trained candidate publishes with no behavioural gate (acknowledged in issue #356). SkillClaw reproduction also uses `selection: always`. Anti-gaming/drift: prompts are fenced as `untrusted_text` with a random nonce; promoted failing prompts pass a credential tripwire and an instruction-override screen with a per-client cap; code_extension wins can be held for human review; sandboxed episodes with explicit env forwarding. Known hole (their words, #356): the harness gate pools wins/losses, so gains on added tasks can outweigh regressions on the protected seed suite.
key_results: All results are team-run, single-sample, small-scale. Harness tutorial: Qwen3-8B/pi published one skill after one failure (gate 1W/0L/2T, 63 s); qwen2.5:7b on the native harness published a loop-graph rewrite adding a `check` stage (2W/0L/1T) but the rewrite is the prompt's worked example reproduced; several native runs rejected; seed tree scored the same task 1.0 in traffic and 0.0 in 4/5 gate episodes (gate is noisy). GEPA on AIME-2025 (2 seeds): +16.0 pp mean vs upstream GEPA +12.7 pp; sign of the difference flips between seeds. Meta-Harness on a 30-task Terminal-Bench hard subset: 23/60 selected vs 20/60 baseline; selector replay agreed with upstream 8/8 decisions. SkillClaw (GLM-5.3-Flash, preliminary): pool 9->17 skills over 6 nights; Productivity category +12.05 pts (2.29 sd) over frozen control. SAO on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 48 rollouts: mean reward 0.479 vs base 0.458 vs GRPO(+DIS) 0.417 — ordering matches paper, magnitude tiny; SWE-Bench Verified attempt produced no result. OpenClaw-RL GSM8K stream with Qwen3-4B: adaptation criterion (3 consecutive passes) reached at session 14.
limitations: 11 days public, v0.0.2, 53 open issues including basic install/CI bugs (sqlite locked in CI #377, reef-pi wrapper breakage #374/#375). Weight updates have no evaluation gate by default (AlwaysSelect); behavioural gates for weights, protected regression suites, invalid-evaluation handling and cross-release regression matrices are all open roadmap items (#355, #356, #5). Harness gate uses tiny task suites (3 tasks in the tutorial), one episode per task by default, stochastic verdicts, and one-step rollback only. Every published result is a single unrepeated run with no spread; several 'wins' come from a 7B model reproducing the prompt's worked example. Weight path requires Ray + Slime + Megatron + SGLang + docker on multi-GPU Linux; harness path needs pi/other agent binaries and a provider key; SkillClaw needs docker + multi-GB dataset + paid API budget with no dry mode. Sandbox `egress_hosts` enables network without enforcing a hostname firewall; the local executor enforces nothing. Recipes live outside the wheel (cookbook only). 'Self-improving' is real for the harness path (the served model proposes and is gated end-to-end) but the research methods are reproductions of other groups' papers; Reef's own contribution is the infra.
key_insight: Treat self-improvement as a release pipeline rather than an algorithm: give every inference a receipt, attach feedback to receipts, express both weight updates and harness edits as candidate artifacts that go through the same propose -> paired-evaluate -> decide contract against the incumbent on fixed tasks, and publish only winners as immutable, hot-mountable releases with one-step rollback — so the optimizer (GEPA, SkillClaw, Meta-Harness, SAO) becomes a swappable plugin.
open_gaps: Weight updates default to AlwaysSelect: no behavioural candidate-vs-incumbent gate, metric thresholds, or held-out regression check before hot-swapping trained weights into live serving (#356, #5 open).

Harness gate is a pooled win/loss tally over one small task list; no protected seed-suite floor, so gains on promoted tasks can mask regressions on original capabilities (admitted in #356); no held-out task set distinct from the gate suite.

Rollback is one step deep (only the previous tree is retained as a target) and rechecks are periodic/manual; no cross-release regression matrix or forgetting analysis over the whole release chain (#355 open).

Gate verdicts are single-episode and stochastic (same tree scored 1.0 in traffic, 0.0 in 4/5 gate episodes); no built-in significance test, repeated confirmation, or invalid-evaluation outcome for scorer/infra failures.

Evaluator, proposer prompt and trigger policy are fixed config, not evolvable state (RFC #308 proposes putting them behind a floor but is unimplemented); no mechanism to detect or correct a scorer the proposer has learned to game.

Proposals are single mutations per step from one proposer with no population/archive except in the GEPA and Meta-Harness recipes; the core mechanism has no crossover, no diversity pressure, and no transfer of learned skills across scenarios/deployments.
No independent or repeated measurements: every reported run is n=1 by the authors; no standard Reef benchmark exists yet (#357/#358 open).

Weight path requires a multi-GPU Ray/Slime/Megatron/SGLang stack; no lightweight or hosted-API weight-learning path (MLX and Tinker backends are roadmap only), so app developers are limited to the harness path.

Sandbox egress is not enforced as a hostname firewall and the default local executor has no isolation, so model-written code_extension/tool nodes can only be safely evolved with bubblewrap on Linux plus human review.

Model-version routing (canary, shadow, sticky pinning, teacher fallback) and per-request serve-only opt-out are unimplemented (#24, #32-#34, #39), so a bad release reaches all traffic of a scenario at once.
safety_measures: Candidate never serves until it beats the incumbent on the same tasks; rejected candidates restore the snapshot; `min_win_margin` noise floor; `recheck_every` re-gates the last publish and can roll back; `evolution.publish: review` / `review_kinds: [code_extension]` hold code-touching wins as pending releases until a human POSTs /promote; `native_loop` changes always wait for review; episodes can run in a bubblewrap sandbox with read-only base FS, explicit `env_from` credentials, resource limits and no network by default; recorded prompts are wrapped as untrusted data with nonce delimiters before entering proposer prompts; promoted failing prompts pass a key-shaped-literal tripwire and an instruction-override screen and are capped per client; provider credentials are never written into candidates, checkpoints, or published trees; scenario state and populations commit atomically with the release so failures cannot advance them.

name: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
org_or_authors: Chengsong Huang, Wenhao Yu, Xiaoyang Wang, Hongming Zhang, Zongxia Li, Ruosen Li, Jiaxin Huang, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu — Tencent AI Lab (Seattle) + WashU
last_activity: 2026-02-04 (last commit: README typo fix; last code change 2025-12-10)
venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted 2026-01); NeurIPS 2025 Math-AI workshop; arXiv:2508.05004; ~188 citations / 41 influential (Semantic Scholar, 2026-09); HF Daily Papers #2 on release; 77 forks
mechanism: Two copies of one base model (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base, OctoThinker) are trained alternately with GRPO (verl/EasyR1 fork) for a fixed number of iterations (paper: 3; scripts/main.sh: 5). Per iteration: (1) Challenger phase — the current Solver is frozen and served by 4 vLLM+Flask reward servers; the Challenger is GRPO-trained for 6 steps (batch 16, n=4 rollouts) with a math-competition 'problem setter' system prompt. Reward per proposed question = min(p, 1-p) - repetition_penalty, where p = share of the Solver's 10 temp-1.0 samples agreeing with the majority answer (paper form: 1-2|p-0.5|), repetition_penalty = the fraction of the batch falling in the same BLEU-distance agglomerative cluster (threshold 0.5), and -1 for malformed output. The Challenger's own \boxed answer is discarded. (2) Solver phase — the new Challenger samples 8x1000 questions; the frozen Solver answers each 10 times; majority vote becomes the pseudo-label; only questions whose majority share lies in [0.3, 0.8] (|p-0.5|<=0.25) are kept, pushed to HF Hub, and the Solver is GRPO-trained for 20 steps (KL 0.01, lr 1e-6) with binary accuracy vs. the pseudo-label. Checkpoints at step 5/15 seed the next iteration. No verifier, no human data, no archive: the curriculum lives only in the Challenger's weights, and the evaluator (majority-vote of the Solver) co-evolves with the policy. Runs end-to-end on one 8-GPU node; a GPT API is used only for offline benchmark rechecking.
eval_loop: In-loop signal: Solver self-consistency (majority-vote share among 10 samples) drives both the Challenger reward (target p~0.5) and the Solver's pseudo-labels; the [0.3,0.8] band filter plus a BLEU-cluster repetition penalty are the only guards against degenerate questions. No ground truth anywhere in the loop. Improvement is reported via external benchmarks (AMC/Minerva/MATH-500/GSM8K/Olympiad/AIME + SuperGPQA/MMLU-Pro/BBEH, GPT-4o rechecked) run after each iteration, but they are not fed back — no early stopping, no rollback. Drift is not prevented, only documented: GPT-4o-judged pseudo-label accuracy falls 79.0% -> 63.0% by iteration 3, Qwen3-4B overall peaks at iter 2 (34.92) and dips at iter 3 (34.64), 0.6B collapses after one iteration, and the follow-up R-Few measures question diversity dropping from 35 to <20 within 50 Challenger steps with inflating question length (reward hacking).
limitations: Math-only in practice (prompt hard-codes competition math; requires a single short verifiable answer); pseudo-labels are self-consistency, so confidently-wrong answers are reinforced and label accuracy decays (79%->63%); gains saturate or reverse after 2-3 iterations (model collapse sooner for small models); a large share of the gain comes from an untrained 'Base Challenger' (e.g. OctoThinker-8B 16.81->25.08 of 26.88 total; Qwen3-4B 27.10->30.83 of 34.92); single-model-both-roles variant collapses earlier; ablation numbers exist but the paper's exact ablation table could not be fetched (arXiv unreachable) — secondary sources confirm all three components matter, with the largest loss from removing Challenger RL. Engineering: hard-coded 8-GPU layout, `pkill python`, HF Hub round-trip for the dataset, tokens.json secrets, known math_verify infinite-loop hang, dead code loading a human math example (unused), no LICENSE file, repo effectively dormant since Dec 2025.
key_insight: Turn the learner's own uncertainty into the curriculum signal: reward a proposer for questions where the solver's self-consistency is ~50% (max reward variance), filter training data to that band, and use the solver's majority vote as the label — you get a verifier-free co-evolution loop that works for a few iterations, but because the evaluator is the policy itself, label drift and diversity collapse are built in and bound the number of useful iterations.
key_results: Qwen3-4B-Base: MATH avg 42.58->49.07 (+6.49), overall 27.10->34.92, MMLU-Pro 37.38->53.75, SuperGPQA 20.88->27.92; Qwen3-8B-Base overall 34.49->38.73, math +5.51; OctoThinker-3B 12.27->15.67; OctoThinker-8B 16.81->26.88 (mostly from Base Challenger). Math-trained skills transfer to general reasoning (+7.54 general on 4B). Pseudo-label accuracy 79.0%->63.0% over 3 iters; separate Challenger/Solver beats one shared model. Follow-ups: VisPlay (VLM extension), R-Few (adds 1-5% human anchors to stop diversity collapse).
safety_measures: Difficulty-band filter (0.3<=majority share<=0.8) and BLEU-cluster repetition penalty on proposed questions; GRPO KL penalty to reference policy (kl_coef 0.01); format checks; per-call timeouts on the grader. No rollback, no held-out gate, no ground-truth verification, no human-in-the-loop.
open_gaps: Evaluator is the policy itself (majority vote of the Solver): no independent verifier or held-out gate, so label accuracy decays 79%->63% and nothing detects or halts it — a framework needs an external/anchored fitness signal or drift monitor
No rollback or checkpoint selection: main.sh blindly chains 5 iterations even though the paper shows performance peaks at iter 2-3; needs benchmark-gated acceptance/early stopping

No archive or population of tasks: each iteration's questions are consumed and discarded; the curriculum exists only in Challenger weights, so diversity collapses (35->20 within 50 steps per R-Few) and there is no replay/novelty archive
Domain hard-wired to single-answer competition math via system prompt; no mechanism for open-ended, agentic, or tool-use tasks where majority vote is not a proxy for correctness
Requires 8-GPU RL fine-tuning (verl/vLLM/FSDP) of 4B-8B base models — unusable for app developers or API-only settings; no prompt/skill-level analogue

Fixed hyperparameters (delta=0.25 band, BLEU 0.5, steps 6/20) hand-tuned; the loop does not adapt its own reward or filter, and the 'Base Challenger' baseline already captures much of the gain — the RL Challenger's marginal value beyond iter 1 is small
No cross-run persistence or transfer: nothing learned (question generators, hard cases) is reused across base models or runs
Reward hacking observed (question length inflation, low-entropy clusters) with only a BLEU-cluster penalty as mitigation; no semantic diversity or difficulty-calibration audit
Single-node, brittle engineering (pkill python, HF-hub round-trip, secrets in tokens.json, math_verify hangs, no license) — not a reusable harness

name: OpenRSI / Frontis-MA1 / OpenMLE (Gym + ERL + Evo + Sandbox)
org_or_authors: Frontis AI + Tsinghua University (Junlin Yang, Che Jiang, Yu Fu, ..., Ning Ding, Bowen Zhou, Kaiyan Zhang; 24 authors)
last_activity: 2026-09-08 (gym fixes for task packages; NatureBench eval-contract fix 2026-09-04; EEMA EMNLP announcement 2026-08-25)
venue_or_citations: arXiv 2607.28568 (186 HF Papers upvotes); companion EEMA paper accepted EMNLP 2026 Main (code not yet released); RSI survey on OpenReview; NatureBench arXiv 2606.24530
mechanism: Two nested loops on a shared action space of four program operators (Draft, Improve, Debug, Crossover). INNER LOOP (OpenMLE-Evo, test-time, per task, 12h budget): a FunSearch/REvolve-style island population vendored from Meta's AIRA-Dojo. Default config: 1 island, max 500 nodes, 800 steps, 100 generations x 5 individuals, crossover_prob 0.5, debug chains up to depth 10. Each step picks an operator, then parents by utility U = 1.0*score + 0.4*delta_vs_parent + 0.25*novelty (novelty = 1/sqrt(1+count of same auto-detected method family, e.g. lightgbm/transformers). The model emits a full program; the sandbox runs it and scores submission.csv against a private answer. Each node gets an 'experience card' (operator, parents, score, delta, method family, error signature, token cost); cards aggregate into a 'strategy board' (family stats, repeated errors, underexplored families) which is injected into Improve (3 ancestors + 3 siblings), Crossover (2+2) and Debug (8 cards) prompts. Acceptance: a child joins the island only if fitness >= island mean; worst pruned above max size; the model's self-reported validation score is NOT trusted for selection (trust_model_validation_score=false). OUTER LOOP (OpenMLE-ERL): (1) SFT on 26,259 execution-verified traces, mostly GLM-4.7 teacher rollouts (parallel top-4 + evolutionary segments gated by 'Draft positive / Improve beats parent / Crossover beats stronger parent / endpoint reaches a medal'); (2) GSPO RL with 16 prompts x 16 samples, operators sampled 0.50/0.17/0.17/0.16 from a SQLite Program Database (top-10 per task, exploit/explore/cooling coefficients), reward = clip((s-s_min)/(s_max-s_min),0,1) from leaderboard bounds, plus GPT-judge hack_check, validation/test-gap penalty, and entropic-advantage post-processing. The trained model then drives the inner loop. Only ONE generation was run; MA1 did not retrain itself.
eval_loop: Fitness inside search = sandbox execution score on an agent-constructed validation split (fixed split instructions supplied per task); self-reported scores are diagnostics only. RL reward = leaderboard-normalized sandbox score with a GPT-based hack_check judge that rejects cheating/guessing code (categories valid/hack/hack_verify), a validation-vs-test gap penalty, and entropic advantage normalization per rollout group. Anti-leakage: SFT/RL task descriptions SHA256-deduplicated against all evaluation benchmarks. Outer benchmark: MLE-Bench Lite (22 tasks x 3 seeds, 12h on one RTX 4090 capped at 12GB VRAM; Valid Rate, Medal Average, Human Rank) plus held-out NatureBench Lite (10 tasks, hidden evaluator, 4h budget, Match/Surpass-SOTA). Drift is prevented by external, private-answer scoring only; there is no human-in-the-loop and no LLM judge for quality beyond hack detection.
key_results: MLE-Bench Lite Medal Average with OpenMLE-Evo fixed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 39.39% -> Frontis-MA1-35B 60.61% (+21.22pp); 30B: 34.85% -> 53.03%. With OpenMLE-Evo-Max (MLE-Bench-disjoint experience priors + async multi-GPU search): 71.21% (35B), 66.67% (30B); claimed to exceed GPT-5.5+Codex and approach GPT-5.6 Sol / Kimi K3. Harness effect for fixed models: GLM-5.2 59.09% (Claude Code) -> 62.12% (Evo) -> 66.67% (Evo-Max); MiniMax M3 54.55% (Codex) -> 65.15% (Evo-Max). Search efficiency vs original AIRA-Evo on 66 matched runs: -41.7% model tokens, -50.3% prompt tokens, +84.3% new-best updates per 1M tokens, Improve success 4.73% -> 9.36%. NatureBench Lite transfer: model swap 50% -> 70% Match-SOTA; framework swap 20% -> 50%. Case studies: 85-92% of validation gain came from later Improve/Crossover steps. Training: 8 H200, SFT 3 epochs bs128 lr3e-5 32k ctx; RL 221 policy updates, rollout reward 0.18 -> 0.40.
limitations: Not actually recursive: one generation only; SFT data is distilled from GLM-4.7 (a stronger external teacher) and Qwen, and the trained model never regenerates its own training data or retrains itself. The improver never modifies its own harness, operators, reward, or training pipeline (only task programs evolve). OpenMLE-Evo-Max 'experience priors' are not described or released, yet they account for +10.6pp of the headline. MLE-Bench Lite (22 easiest tasks) and a 10-task NatureBench subset only; 3 seeds. RL validated only as a 2-step smoke on 8xH200 (from a step-669 checkpoint), not a paper reproduction; multi-node profiles unvalidated. Requires a self-hosted distributed sandbox service (Postgres/Redis/NFS/worker containers), external task packages (4,343 of 5,758 tasks are rebuild recipes only), and pinned SLIME image. CC BY-NC 4.0 (no commercial use). EEMA code not yet released. Fitness relies on an agent-built validation split (overfitting/leakage risk mitigated only by instructions and a gap penalty). Single-island default (migration_prob=0) reduces the population diversity story.
key_insight: Align the training action space with the search action space: train the exact same four atomic program-evolution operators (Draft/Improve/Debug/Crossover) with execution-grounded rewards, so post-training directly improves the per-step productivity of a long-horizon evolutionary search rather than one-shot generation, and attribute gains with controlled model-swap vs harness-swap comparisons.
safety_measures: Isolated sandbox worker containers with private answers never exposed to the agent; GPT-judge hack_check that rejects guessing/cheating code in RL; validation/test-gap penalty; self-reported scores excluded from parent selection; benchmark deduplication of training tasks; public configs scanned for credentials; local-execution security boundary documented. No self-modification of harness, so no rollback machinery needed.
open_gaps: No closed loop: the post-trained model's own search trajectories are never selected back into SFT/RL to retrain the next generation (paper shows one generation, seeded by GLM-4.7 teacher data)
The improver only mutates task programs; it cannot mutate its own operators, prompts, parent-selection utility weights, or search hyperparameters, and there is no meta-level fitness for such changes
Experience is per-task and per-run: experience cards/strategy boards are discarded between tasks, and the cross-task 'experience priors' of Evo-Max are undocumented and unreleased
Fitness is a single scalar sandbox score on an agent-chosen validation split; no held-out early-stopping or multi-objective (cost, runtime) selection beyond token accounting
Requires a self-hosted distributed sandbox service plus 8xH200 for training; no lightweight path for application developers to run the improvement loop on API models
Reward hacking defense is a GPT judge and a gap penalty, with no verifiable check that generated validation splits are leakage-free
Only 22 MLE-Bench Lite + 10 NatureBench tasks; no evidence of transfer to non-tabular/ML-engineering domains or to agentic multi-file codebases
CC BY-NC license and EEMA code not released block reuse and extension of the meta-evolution component
Single-island default with migration disabled; no archive-level diversity maintenance (e.g., MAP-Elites) despite novelty term in parent selection
No automatic task/curriculum generation: OpenMLE-Gym tasks are statically curated, not evolved with the agent
