name: pi-autoresearch
org_or_authors: davebcn87 (primary, 99 commits); tobi (Tobi Lütke, 51 commits); ~20 community contributors. Extension for badlogic's pi coding agent (pi-mono, 104k stars). Inspired by karpathy/autoresearch (95k stars).
venue_or_citations: Not a paper. 8,036 GitHub stars, 455 forks, 12 npm releases (latest 1.8.1), ~5.1k npm downloads/month (Aug 11-Sep 9 2026). Created 5 days after karpathy/autoresearch as its generalization to arbitrary metrics inside a coding-agent harness.
mechanism: Single pi agent, single git branch, greedy hill-climb over the TARGET CODEBASE (the "other" that evolves). Setup: the `autoresearch-create` skill makes the agent write `.auto/prompt.md` (objective, primary metric + direction, secondary monitors, files in scope, off-limits, "What's Been Tried") and `.auto/measure.sh` (emits `METRIC name=value` lines), creates a branch, calls `init_experiment`, runs and logs a baseline. Loop per iteration: agent edits code -> `run_experiment` runs measure.sh with timeout, parses METRIC lines, then runs optional `.auto/checks.sh` (tests/types/lint) -> `log_experiment(status=keep|discard|crash|checks_failed, metric, description, asi{hypothesis, rollback_reason, next_action_hint, revisits_run})`. On `keep`: `git add -A && git commit` with a JSON Result trailer. On anything else: `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd` excluding `.auto/`. Every run appends a line to `.auto/log.jsonl`. `before.sh`/`after.sh` hooks (bash, JSON on stdin, stdout delivered as a steer message, 30s/8KB caps) fire around each iteration. The tool result also appends a nudge to reconsider discards whose rollback assumption may now be invalid. Continuation is harness-driven: on `agent_end`, if an experiment ran this turn, after an 800ms settle window it sends "Run the next iteration now"; capped at 200 auto-resume turns, stopped after >20 consecutive discards/crashes or `maxIterations`. On context compaction, the LLM summary is replaced with a deterministic summary rebuilt from log.jsonl (last 50 runs + ASI), prompt.md and ideas.md, so memory = files. Context-memory (prompt.md, ideas.md, ASI) is agent-maintained. measure.sh is agent-editable mid-loop and persists across reverts. `autoresearch-finalize` regroups kept commits into independent review branches.
eval_loop: Fitness = one user-defined scalar parsed from `.auto/measure.sh` output (lower or higher is better), plus secondary metrics that are monitors only. The KEEP decision is made by the agent, not the tool: `log_experiment` trusts `params.status` and never checks that the metric actually beat the current best; the only hard gates are (a) `keep` is refused when `.auto/checks.sh` failed on that run and (b) the secondary-metric set must stay consistent. Anti-drift is soft: a MAD-based confidence score (|best_kept - baseline| / MAD of all runs in segment) shown after 3+ runs but explicitly advisory ("never auto-discards"); the string "Be careful not to overfit to the benchmarks and do not cheat on the benchmarks" in resume prompts; optional hooks (anti-thrash after 5 discards). No hidden holdout: the agent can read and edit measure.sh, and issue #81 requesting holdout evaluators was closed without implementation. No human in the loop during the run; a human reviews at finalize time.
key_results: No quantitative results are published in the repo; the README's screenshots and the website's 48s-build scenario are explicitly documented as illustrative in site/ASSETS.md. Demonstrated: runs end-to-end (65 passing tests, CI, npm provenance releases), real user sessions reported in issues (e.g. #64 reached a saturated feature_score=1 in a UI task), 5k+ monthly installs. Claimed domains: test runtime, bundle size, LLM training loss, build time, Lighthouse. Maintainer's own stance on adding a swarm mode (#77): "how would you prove the result is better than the simple version?" - no comparative evaluation exists for the simple version either.
limitations: Single agent, single lineage, greedy: no population, archive, or branching from non-best kept states (swarm PRD #77 closed not_planned). Keep/discard unenforced by the harness, so a misjudging agent can commit regressions. Evaluator is fully visible and mutable by the optimizer and survives reverts. Noise handled only advisorily; no repeats/A-B replay (#69 open). Saturated/binary objectives trap the loop into discard-only (#64 open). Single scalar objective, no Pareto handling. Tightly coupled to pi's extension API (activation, compaction hooks, setActiveTools); not a standalone SDK. Learnings do not transfer across projects or sessions beyond the per-project .auto/ folder. The agent itself (prompts, tools, strategy) does not evolve; only the target code and the agent's notes do. No published evidence of improvement over an unassisted agent.
safety_measures: Experiment tools hidden from the model outside /autoresearch mode (v1.5.0) so the agent cannot self-start a loop; auto-resume ceiling 200 turns and stop after >20 consecutive discards/crashes; optional maxIterations; git revert on every non-keep with .auto/ preserved; checks.sh backpressure blocks keep on failing tests; hook scripts have 30s timeout and 8KB stdout cap; shell-injection fix in commit messages (PR #13); "don't cheat on benchmarks" guardrail text; README warns extension runs with full user permissions and recommends a dedicated branch/worktree and sandbox; npm releases carry provenance attestations. No sandboxing of the target project's commands, no evaluator integrity check, no cost/token cap beyond iteration count.
key_insight: Split the loop into domain-agnostic harness infrastructure (run/measure/commit-or-revert/auto-resume/deterministic compaction) and a per-domain playbook the agent writes itself, and make the on-disk log + playbook the sole source of truth so the optimization loop survives context resets, restarts, and reverts - the agent's memory is files, not its context window.
open_gaps: Harness does not enforce the acceptance rule: log_experiment commits whenever the agent says 'keep' without comparing metric to current best; a framework should gate commits on metric improvement plus a noise-aware threshold.

Evaluator (measure.sh) is readable and editable by the optimizing agent and is preserved across reverts; no hidden holdout benchmark, no hash/integrity check on the evaluator, no train/holdout split (issue #81 closed unimplemented).

Single-lineage greedy hill climb: no archive/population of kept states, no parent selection, no branching from a non-best commit; swarm/orchestrator mode (#77) was declined for lack of proof it helps.
Noise handling is advisory only: no automatic repeated measurement, no A/B replay of marginal candidates, no statistical acceptance test (#69 open).
No completion semantics for bounded/binary objectives; loop keeps demanding iterations after the metric saturates (#64 open).
Single scalar objective; secondary metrics are monitors only, no multi-objective or Pareto-front acceptance.
No cross-session or cross-project transfer of learnings: ASI/prompt.md/ideas.md are per-project; nothing distills logs into reusable skills, prompts, or heuristics.
Only the target code evolves; the agent's own prompts, tools, and search strategy are static and hand-authored.
Tightly coupled to pi's extension API; not usable as a standalone optimization SDK from other harnesses (requested in #77 comments).
No published quantitative evidence (case studies, ablations) that the loop beats an unassisted agent or that features like confidence scoring and revisit-discards change outcomes.

name: Everything Claude Code (ECC) — continuous-learning-v2.1 "instincts"
org_or_authors: Affaan Mustafa (affaan-m), single maintainer + community PRs; repo now canonical at github.com/affaan-m/ECC
venue_or_citations: GitHub OSS (MIT); 256k stars, 38k forks; npm ecc-universal; ECC Tools GitHub App. No paper, no benchmark.
mechanism: Four stages, all file-based under ~/.local/share/ecc-homunculus/projects/<git-remote-hash>/. (1) OBSERVE: plugin PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks (matcher .*, async, 10s timeout) run observe.sh, which appends one JSON line per tool call (tool, 5000-char-truncated input/output, session, project_id; regex secret-scrub) to observations.jsonl. Five guard layers stop it from observing subagents/its own observer (self-loop). No UserPromptSubmit hook, so user message text is never captured. (2) ANALYZE (off by default: observer.enabled=false): a per-project bash daemon (observer-loop.sh) wakes every 5 min or every 20 observations (SIGUSR1, 60s cooldown, session-guardian gating), tails the last 500 lines, and spawns `claude --model haiku --print --allowedTools Read,Write --max-turns 20-100` with a prompt: find patterns with 3+ occurrences (corrections, error resolutions, repeated tool sequences, tool preferences), write/update an instinct .md with YAML frontmatter (id, trigger, confidence by frequency bucket 3-5=0.5/6-10=0.7/11+=0.85, domain, scope project|global). Haiku must emit `{"status":"analysis_complete"}` as last line (verified via unlinked-inode fd); only then observations are archived, else retained for retry. 120s watchdog. (3) APPLY: SessionStart hook loads project+global instincts, keeps confidence>=0.7, dedupes by id, ranks by confidence + relevance boost (+0.25 project-scoped, +0.2 stack keyword match), injects top 6 as one-line "Active instincts" bullets into additionalContext. (4) EVOLVE/PROMOTE (manual CLI): greedy keyword-overlap clustering of triggers; clusters>=2 -> SKILL.md (concatenated action lines), workflow instincts>=0.7 -> command .md, clusters>=3 & avg>=0.75 -> agent .md, written to an evolved/ dir Claude Code does not auto-load. `promote`: same instinct id in >=2 projects with avg confidence>=0.8 -> copied to global. Pending instincts pruned after 30 days.
eval_loop: No objective fitness signal. "Confidence" is a frequency bucket assigned by the Haiku observer at write time; the documented dynamics (+0.05 per confirmation, -0.1 per contradiction, -0.02/week decay) are not implemented anywhere in instinct-cli.py or hooks. The only acceptance checks are format contracts: frontmatter present, completion record emitted, 3+ occurrences as judged by the LLM. Nothing records whether an injected instinct was followed, helped, or was overridden, so there is no closed feedback loop and no anti-drift mechanism beyond (a) project scoping to limit contamination, (b) the 0.7 injection floor and 6-item cap, (c) a prompt line telling the observer to treat observations as untrusted data, and (d) observer restricted to Read/Write tools. No A/B, benchmark, held-out test, or regression check on instinct quality exists; the repo's "eval framework" (PR #3040) is unrelated to this loop.
key_results: No quantitative results reported anywhere. Demonstrated: hooks reliably capture tool calls; SessionStart injection works (added 2026-04-05 after issue #1231 showed instincts were stored but never used); Haiku observer writes instinct files on macOS/Linux when enabled. Issue history shows the loop was effectively non-functional Jan-Apr 2026: --max-turns 3 produced 2,534 errors and zero instincts (#386), evolve --generate was a no-op stub (#217), ~/.claude writes blocked in --print mode (#1599, fixed by relocating data dir #1431), and no injection existed until #1231. Observer never survives on native Windows (#2489). Auto-generated instincts from the hosted GitHub App were reported as wrong-language, contradictory conventions (#2841). Repo-curated example instincts (8 items, e.g. "use conventional commits") illustrate typical output granularity.
limitations: Analysis stage disabled by default; fragile background daemon (dozens of observer bug issues, Windows unsupported). Observations lack user prompt text, so "user correction" detection is inference from tool patterns only. Confidence never updated after creation; no decay or contradiction handling despite docs. Promotion requires exact id string equality across projects whose ids are independently LLM-generated. Evolved skills/commands/agents land outside Claude Code discovery paths and are just concatenated action lines with no verification. Only 6 one-line instincts injected at session start, ranked by stack keywords not by task. Instinct files written by an LLM reading untrusted tool output are injected into future system context (prompt-injection surface). Single-user, manual export/import for sharing. Documentation overstates implemented behavior ("self-evolving" is partly marketing).
key_insight: Decouple learning from the working agent: deterministic harness hooks (100% capture) feed a cheap background LLM that distills sessions into atomic, confidence-scored, scope-tagged "instincts" stored as files, which a SessionStart hook re-injects above a confidence floor — a memory-write/memory-read loop that needs no model training and lives entirely in the harness.
open_gaps: No outcome-based fitness: confidence is LLM-estimated frequency, never tied to test pass/fail, task success, or user acceptance of an injected instinct
Confidence update rules (+0.05 confirm, -0.1 contradiction, weekly decay) are documented but unimplemented; nothing lowers or retires an instinct the user keeps overriding
No feedback capture on application: the system never logs whether an injected instinct was followed, helped, or was contradicted in the session it was injected into
User prompt text is not observed (no UserPromptSubmit hook), so explicit corrections — the highest-signal event — are invisible to the observer
Cross-project promotion needs exact id match across independently generated ids; no semantic/embedding dedup or merge of near-duplicate instincts
Evolved skills/commands/agents are written to a non-discovered directory and are unverified concatenations; no test that a generated skill executes or improves anything, no auto-install
No rollback, versioning, or A/B of instinct sets; no held-out evaluation to detect that a learned instinct degrades behavior
Retrieval is SessionStart-only, capped at 6 lines, ranked by stack keywords — no task-time or query-conditioned retrieval of relevant instincts
Prompt-injection path: untrusted tool outputs -> LLM-written instinct files -> injected into future system context, mitigated only by a prompt instruction
Analysis stage is off by default and depends on a fragile bash daemon (fails on Windows, many macOS/Linux edge cases); no yield/health metric on instincts produced per observation batch
Single-user learning with manual export/import; no team-level aggregation, conflict resolution, or provenance across users
safety_measures: Observer session self-loop guards (entrypoint, ECC_SKIP_OBSERVE, agent_id, path exclusions); observer limited to Read/Write tools, haiku, max-turns and 120s watchdog; regex secret scrubbing before persisting observations; data dir moved out of ~/.claude; completion record validated on an unlinked inode to prevent forged results; observations archived only after verified analysis; instincts must contain no code snippets (prompt rule); project scoping to prevent cross-project contamination; confidence >=0.7 floor and 6-item cap on injection; 30-day TTL prune of pending instincts; AgentShield scanner for hooks/prompts. No human-in-the-loop approval on auto-generated instincts before injection.

name: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
org_or_authors: Meta Superintelligence Labs + UIUC (Zhenrui Yue, Kartikeya Upasani, Xianjun Yang, Suyu Ge, Shaoliang Nie, Yuning Mao, Zhe Liu, Dong Wang)
last_activity: 2026-03-23 (last push: "fix rollout inconsistency"; last issue activity 2026-06-05)
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2601.07055 (Jan 2026); citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); ~3.5k alphaxiv views; 65 forks
mechanism: Two agents initialized from the same base LLM (Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct) co-evolve over 3 manual iterations, each = proposer RL -> data synthesis -> solver RL -> checkpoint convert. Seed prompts (process_train.py) are random 256-token Wikipedia passages plus a sampled hop count n in {1,2,3,4} (ratio 4:3:2:1); the Search-R1 dataset is downloaded only for row count, questions are discarded. Proposer: multi-turn tool-using rollout that must issue exactly n-1 searches and emit <question>/<answer>. Reward (reward_function.py) = 0.5*format + difficulty. Format = mean of [1, fraction of turns starting with <think>, tool-call-count match to n, answer grounded as substring of doc+retrieved text and <=5 words], zeroed if question/answer empty or answer leaks into question. Difficulty: question is posed 5x to the CURRENT solver (served via sglang; base model in iter1, previous solver later); k = EM-correct count; score = (5-k)/4 if 0<k<5 else 0 (peaks at k=1, zero for trivial or unsolvable). HRPO = GRPO with rollout.n=1 per prompt and the advantage baseline (mean/std) computed over all batch samples sharing the same hop-count tag ("search_zero_n"), replacing per-prompt groups and cutting nested sampling from m*n to n. Data synthesis (main_generation.py): 5 proposer samples per seed prompt over 1/5 of seeds (~34k), keep argmax format score, proposer's own answer becomes ground truth (no solver filter, no dedup, no correctness verifier). Solver: standard GRPO (n=5), Search-R1-style EM reward, 50 steps, batch 256, lr 1e-6, no KL; iter k+1 solver resumes from iter k solver weights, proposer resumes from previous proposer. External benchmark validation every 25 steps is monitoring only.
eval_loop: Proposer fitness = format score (regex/substring checks) + difficulty score derived from 5 rollouts of the evolving solver, EM-checked against the proposer's own answer; solver fitness = EM against proposer-labeled answers via GRPO. Drift controls are weak: difficulty is zero for unsolvable (k=0) and trivial (k=5) questions, hop-ratio prior (40/30/20/10%) forces structural diversity, answer must be grounded in document/retrieved text and short, grad clip 0.1 (7B additionally needed KL 0.001). No held-out acceptance gate, no rollback between iterations; benchmarks (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle; 1200-sample subset during training) are logged for monitoring only, not used for selection. Labels are self-generated and never verified, so reward hacking via ambiguous/wrong-label questions is possible; authors themselves list reward hacking and bias amplification as unaddressed.
key_results: Paper (3B): Dr. Zero beats supervised Search-R1 by up to 22.9% on NQ (0.397 vs 0.323 EM) and up to 14.1% on select benchmarks; multi-hop reaches ~90% of supervised; 7B approaches or surpasses supervised baselines on multi-hop. HRPO matches GRPO (0.326 vs 0.320 avg EM, 3B) at ~25-40% of GPU hours. Iteration 2 adds +4.93% (3B) / +1.64% (7B); marginal gains after 3 iterations; solver saturates in ~50 steps. Compute: 8xA100/H100, 2-3 days for 3 iterations. Independent reproduction (issues #5/#7, unresolved): 3B iter1 avg EM 32.0 but iter2 dropped to 28.4 (multi-hop degraded), 7B collapsed before step 50 even with authors' Appendix hyperparameters; authors could not release weights/data and first author lost access to the Meta cluster.
limitations: Closed-world setting: single Wikipedia corpus + e5 retriever shared with all eval benchmarks, so 'zero data' still means in-distribution corpus. Proposer's answers are unverified ground truth. Plateaus after 2-3 iterations; 7B training unstable (token-inconsistency collapse; a fix landed 2026-03 but reproduction remains open). Expensive difficulty signal (5 solver rollouts per proposed question). EM-only evaluation. Iterations are chained by hand-edited shell scripts with no orchestration. Non-commercial license, no checkpoints, no requirements.txt; external users could not reproduce reported numbers.
key_insight: Score proposed tasks by the current solver's pass rate and reward exactly the 'hard but solvable' band (k=1 of 5), and you get an automatic curriculum at the solver's frontier without any labeled data; and GRPO's baseline does not need multiple samples of the same prompt: grouping single samples by a structural attribute (hop count) gives a usable baseline at a fraction of the sampling cost.
safety_measures: None beyond training hygiene: format reward rejects answer-leaking or ungrounded questions, difficulty reward zeroes unsolvable questions, grad clip 0.1 and optional KL 0.001 for 7B; no verification of self-generated labels, no rollback or acceptance gate between iterations, no robustness testing to adversarial/poisoned documents (authors acknowledge); non-commercial license, weights withheld.
open_gaps: No correctness verifier for proposer-generated answers: the proposer's own <answer> becomes solver ground truth with no evidence-grounded check, so label noise compounds across iterations
No regression guard between iterations: iter k+1 blindly resumes from iter k weights; an independent run saw 3B avg EM fall from 32.0 (iter1) to 28.4 (iter2) with no mechanism to detect or roll back
Fitness is EM on 7 Wikipedia QA benchmarks only; no held-out generalization test to other corpora, live web search, other tools, or non-QA tasks
Difficulty estimation costs 5 full multi-turn solver rollouts per proposed question; no learned difficulty predictor or cached estimates
No dedup or coverage tracking of synthesized questions; diversity is enforced only by a hard-coded 4:3:2:1 hop-ratio prior and random seed documents
Curriculum structure itself is static (hop ratio, 50 steps, 3 iterations chosen by hand); nothing adapts the curriculum schedule based on solver progress
Requires 8xA100/H100 full-parameter RL for 2-3 days and hand-edited shell scripts per iteration; unusable by app developers and not orchestrated end-to-end
Training instability at 7B (collapse before step 50, token-ID inconsistency in multi-turn rollouts) remains unresolved and unreproduced externally; no checkpoints or requirements.txt released
Only model weights evolve; the search tool, retriever, prompts, and reward function are fixed and cannot be self-modified
No defense against proposer reward hacking (e.g., ambiguous questions that hit k=1 by chance) or bias amplification, which the authors explicitly list as future work

name: DSPy (stanfordnlp/dspy) — Declarative Self-improving Python, with GEPA / SIMBA / MIPROv2 / BootstrapFinetune optimizers
date: 2023-01-09 (repo created); DSPy paper Oct 2023 (ICLR 2024); MIPROv2 Jun 2024; GEPA Jul 2025; dspy.Flex Aug 2026 (v3.3.0)
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed_at); v3.3.1 released 2026-08-21; ~100+ commits in last 90 days
org_or_authors: Stanford NLP (Omar Khattab, Chris Potts, Matei Zaharia et al.); GEPA by Lakshya A Agrawal et al. (UC Berkeley / Stanford / Databricks / MIT); Flex by @michaelisaac-dev; ReActV2/RLM by @isaacbmiller; 100+ contributors
venue_or_citations: DSPy: ICLR 2024; MIPROv2: EMNLP 2024; GEPA: arXiv 2507.19457, 366 citations on Semantic Scholar as of Sep 2026; upstream gepa-ai/gepa engine 6,518 stars; wrapped by MLflow, Databricks, Comet Opik, Ax
mechanism:
Compile-time outer loop, not runtime self-modification: a DSPy program is Python whose LM calls are `Predict` nodes parameterized by (instruction text, few-shot demos). `optimizer.compile(program, trainset, valset)` returns a new program; the original is deep-copied, never mutated.

GEPA loop (verified in dspy/teleprompt/gepa/*.py + gepa-ai/gepa engine.py): (1) seed candidate = {predictor_name: instruction} plus {flex_path: module_src} for any `dspy.Flex` submodule; full valset eval. (2) Sample a parent stochastically from the per-validation-instance Pareto front (any candidate best on >=1 val example), not just the global best. (3) Draw a train minibatch (default 3, epoch-shuffled), run the parent with trace capture, call the user metric per example to get a score AND free-text feedback; the metric is also called with `pred_name`/`pred_trace` for per-predictor feedback. (4) Round-robin select one component; build a reflective dataset {Inputs, Generated Outputs, Feedback} from non-perfect examples. (5) A strong reflection LM (gpt-5 recommended) rewrites that component's instruction — or, for Flex, the ENTIRE `dspy.Module` source (predictors, control flow, plain Python) via `CodeProposalSignature`, reflecting on whole-program I/O. (6) Child is evaluated on the same minibatch; accepted only if sum(new) > sum(old) (`StrictImprovementAcceptance`). (7) Accepted child gets a full valset eval, joins the permanent archive; Pareto front updated. (8) Up to 5 merge crossovers combine components of two front candidates sharing an ancestor. (9) Stop at `max_metric_calls`; return the highest aggregate-valset candidate.

SIMBA: per step, 6 program×temperature samples per example on a 32-example minibatch, sort examples by score variance, LM writes a rule (appended to instruction) or adds a demo; softmax-sampled pool. MIPROv2: bootstrap demos → grounded instruction proposals → Optuna TPE over (instruction, demo) combos with minibatch + periodic full evals. BootstrapFinetune/GRPO/BetterTogether distill metric-filtered traces into weights.
eval_loop: Signal = a user-written metric returning a float or `dspy.Prediction(score, feedback)`; the feedback string is injected verbatim into the reflection prompt (GEPA is the only optimizer that reads it; COPRO/MIPROv2 see a scalar). Drift/regression control: (a) strict-improvement acceptance on the same train minibatch before any full eval; (b) full held-out valset evaluation of every accepted candidate, per-instance Pareto tracking for exploration, aggregate valset score for final selection; (c) archive never deletes candidates, so the seed remains a fallback; (d) `skip_perfect_score` keeps reflection focused on failures; (e) explicit warning that valset==trainset overfits; (f) `_compiled=True` flag freezes already-optimized submodules from later optimizers. MIPROv2 uses minibatch evals with periodic full evals and a TPE surrogate. No statistical test on the 3-example acceptance gate and no defense against LLM-judge reward hacking beyond held-out ranking.
key_results: DSPy paper: compiling small programs beats hand prompts (e.g. GPT-3.5 25%->65% on multi-hop QA class tasks). Docs (informal): MIPROv2 light raises ReAct HotPotQA 24%->51%; RAG 53%->61%. GEPA paper (claimed, Qwen3-8B / GPT-4.1-mini on HotpotQA, IFBench, HoVer, PUPA): +10% avg and up to +20% over GRPO with up to 35x fewer rollouts (100-500 evals vs 5k-25k+), and >10% over MIPROv2. External deployments: Databricks 'agents 90x cheaper' (open models + GEPA beat Claude Opus 4.1); Nubank LLM-judge accuracy 68.9%->88.9%, Cohen's kappa 0.00->0.745; Microsoft MAI-Thinking-1 used GEPA/DSPy for a pre-training data filter; upstream claims MATH 67%->93% via full-program evolution and ARC-AGI 32%->89% via architecture discovery (upstream gepa, not reproduced in the DSPy repo).
limitations: Offline compile-time only: no online/continual loop from production traffic. Acceptance is a strict-improvement test on a 3-example minibatch (noisy, no significance test); valset doubles as selection set so small valsets overfit. Mutation loop is serial and dominated by reflection-LM cost (12-36 gpt-5 calls per medium run; hundreds of dollars possible); `max_reflection_cost` unsupported in the DSPy adapter. Open bug (2026-08-20): `auto_budget` does not reflect the actual reflective loop. GEPA metrics must be sync (async issue open since 2025-10). Predictor-level scoring unsupported (module-level score overrides). `dspy.Flex` (code evolution) is experimental, marked API-in-flux, has no in-repo benchmark, requires Deno/Pyodide sandbox, and reflects only on whole-program I/O. No optimizer auto-selection ('you choose'). Demo-tuning overfits small trainsets. Weight optimizers need a fine-tunable model.
key_insight: Treat prompts (and now module source code) as parameters of a declarative program and optimize them with feedback-rich evolutionary search: sample parents from a per-example Pareto front, mutate by having a strong LM read execution traces plus textual metric feedback, gate acceptance on the same minibatch, rank on a held-out valset — natural-language feedback is a far denser learning signal per rollout than a scalar reward, which is why it beats GRPO with 35x fewer rollouts.
open_gaps: Purely offline compile-time: no continual loop that ingests production failures, re-optimizes, and regression-gates against the currently deployed artifact
Acceptance gate is a 3-example minibatch strict-improvement test with no statistical significance check and no separate test set beyond the valset used for selection
No cross-task/cross-program transfer: every compile starts from the seed; learned instructions/rules are not stored in a reusable skill or memory library
Metric/evaluator is fixed and human-written; nothing evolves the reward, and LLM-judge feedback is injected verbatim into the proposer with no reward-hacking defense
Topology/code evolution (dspy.Flex) is experimental, confined to one sandboxed submodule, reflects only on whole-program I/O, and has no in-repo benchmark evidence
Mutation loop is serial and reflection-cost-dominated; no cost-aware budgeting (max_reflection_cost unsupported) and no parallel population/island search
No optimizer auto-selection or meta-optimization of optimizer hyperparameters
Cannot evolve tools, the harness, or infrastructure outside a Flex sandbox; tool implementations are frozen inputs
Single-agent only: no multi-agent population coordination; merges capped at 5 and limited to shared-ancestor crossover
GEPA metric must be synchronous; predictor-level scores are ignored in favor of module-level score
safety_measures: Flex-generated code always runs in a Deno/Pyodide `PythonInterpreter` sandbox (hardened in 3.3.1: unpredictable request IDs, revoked Deno-cache access, prototype-mutation protection); `max_predictor_calls` caps runaway generated programs; unparsable candidates score at `failure_score` instead of crashing the search; original student is deep-copied, never mutated; deterministic `seed` and checkpoint/resume via `log_dir`; hard `max_metric_calls` budget; full lineage/audit trail via `track_stats`. No default human review of proposed instructions and no bound on instruction length.

name: OpenViking
org_or_authors: Volcengine (ByteDance / Beijing Volcano Engine Technology); VikingMem paper by Jiajie Fu, Junwen Chen, Mengzhao Wang et al. (Zhejiang Univ. + ByteDance); 257+ GitHub contributors
last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed today; v0.4.19 released 2026-09-08; ~30 commits in the last 48h)
venue_or_citations: VikingMem (arXiv:2605.29640, VLDB 2026); Directory-Aware Query and Maintenance in Vector DBs / TrieHI (arXiv:2606.16903, ICDE); VikingRAG (arXiv:2609.11390, submitted). 2,808 forks, 700 open issues, Trendshift-listed; commercial SaaS on Volcano Engine.
mechanism: Two loops over a filesystem-shaped context DB (viking://). ONLINE: session.commit() archives messages synchronously, then asynchronously runs SessionCompressorV3 -> ExtractLoop, a <=3-iteration ReAct orchestrator where the LLM may `read`/`find` existing memory files and then emits operations (JSON or restricted-Python SEARCH/REPLACE protocol). Candidates pass a vector pre-filter + LLM dedup decision (candidate: skip/create/none; per existing item: merge/delete) and are written by MemoryUpdater with a per-commit memory_diff.json (before/after audit) and re-embedded. If the server-wide agent_evolution switch is on (default false) and extraction yields >=1 `case` (task signature + JSON rubric), it extracts `trajectories` (add-only operation contracts tagged with outcome and the experience URIs the agent read) and upserts `experiences` (Situation/Approach/Reflect imperative rules with a `supersedes` field) and optionally an executable session skill. At recall, experiences are vector-searched under memories/experiences, gated by a deterministic task-likeness score, injected inside an <openviking-context> block and stripped before capture to avoid self-pollution. OFFLINE (openviking/session/train): the experiences directory is a versioned PolicySet. Per epoch: content-hash snapshot -> RolloutExecutor (remote env HTTP service, e.g. tau2 driving VikingBot's AgentLoop) -> TrajectoryRolloutAnalyzer (rubric evaluation from env reward, passed = reward>=1.0, feedback text injected into trajectory extraction) -> ExperienceGradientEstimator (ExtractLoop proposes before/after MemoryFile patches = PatchSemanticGradient with confidence and derived_from links) -> PatchMergePolicyOptimizer (one LLM pass merges/splits/deletes across all gradients) -> MemoryFilePolicyUpdater under a tree lock with reload, base-content guard and version+1. Held-out test split is evaluated with 8 trials against a cached baseline; the delta is only reported.
eval_loop: Online loop: no external fitness signal at all — extraction, dedup/merge and supersede decisions are single-LLM judgments (ExtractLoop with read/find tools, <=3 ReAct rounds); drift is limited only by schema prompts (abstraction mandate, atomic scope, 8-bullet cap), a base-content guard on writes, and a memory_diff.json audit trail (manual rollback). Offline loop: environment reward from a benchmark service (tau2: passed = reward>=1.0, score = reward) becomes a RubricEvaluation that is injected as feedback text into trajectory extraction and stored as trajectory outcome; auto-extracted cases carry LLM-written rubrics. Held-out evaluation is real (train split committed, test split scored, 8 trials averaged, cached baseline, per-epoch eval), but accuracy delta never gates or reverts a policy update — the pipeline is analyze->estimate->plan->apply with no acceptance test. When no env reward exists, fallback evaluation is 'passed iff a trajectory was extracted' (trivially true). Lineage tags (which experiences were read + trajectory outcome) feed a Studio 'outcome distribution' view but no automatic pruning. The sibling LLM harness mitigates reward hacking only by skipping failed train sessions and hiding reward from the extractor.
key_results: Claimed (blog/README, Doubao 2.0 Pro + Doubao embedding): LoCoMo accuracy OpenClaw 24.20%->82.08%, Hermes 33.38%->82.86%, Claude Code 57.21%->80.32% vs native memory, with input tokens -34.3% to -91.0% and latency -58% to -66%. Agent experience memory on tau2-bench: retail 70.94%->77.81% (+6.87pp), airline 54.38%->66.25% (+11.87pp) with train split committed to memory and test split held out (8 trials averaged). ClawWork net income +69.34%, token use -22.8%. HotpotQA top-20 91.00%. Reproduction scripts in ./benchmark. No confidence intervals, no ablations (experiences vs trajectories), no multi-epoch curves published; memory_organization benchmark exists internally with structural graders.
limitations: Agent Evolution (cases/trajectories/experiences) is OFF by default (server.agent_evolution.enabled=false); the 'self-evolving' loop only has a real fitness signal inside the benchmark harness that requires a custom rollout/reward HTTP service. Policy updates are greedy in-place LLM patches with no acceptance gate, no rollback on regression, no population/archive. PolicyStatus lifecycle (draft/staging/production/deprecated) is a data field with no automated transitions. Experience quality depends entirely on Doubao-tuned extraction prompts (32k output-token floor). Heavy infra: Python server + Rust CLI + C++ index + vector DB; AGPL-3.0 core. Benchmarks self-reported without CIs.
key_insight: Treat the agent's experience directory as a versioned, file-based Policy Set and optimize it with 'semantic gradients': rollouts -> outcome-tagged trajectories (with env reward injected as feedback) -> proposed before/after file patches -> one LLM merge/split/delete pass -> locked, version-guarded apply with an audit diff — so learned behavior stays browsable, diffable and lineage-tracked rather than hidden in a vector store or weights.
open_gaps: Held-out eval delta is only reported, never used as an acceptance gate: no automatic rollback or rejection of a policy update that lowers test accuracy (memory_diff.json is audit-only, restore is manual)

Outside benchmark harnesses there is no fitness signal: fallback RubricEvaluation is 'passed iff a trajectory was extracted', so real-world experience extraction is pure LLM self-judgment with no grounding in task success

Per-experience lineage stats (success/failure counts of trajectories that read it) are surfaced only in the Studio UI; not used to deprecate, prune, down-rank at retrieval, or re-train experiences; PolicyStatus draft->staging->production->deprecated has no automated promotion/demotion

Only memory/experience text evolves; the host harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw agent loop, tool set, system prompts) is untouched, and extracted session skills are not execution-tested before being served (a skill_test_generation prompt exists but no verification gate)

Offline training needs a bespoke HTTP rollout/environment service with ground-truth reward (tau2); no generic way for app developers to declare verifiable cases/rubrics, and auto-extracted case rubrics are LLM-written and never validated
Single greedy lineage: no population or archive of alternative policy snapshots, no A/B serving of policy versions, no exploration beyond one merge pass per epoch

Merge/dedup/supersede decisions are one LLM call (<=3 ReAct rounds) with no check that the merged experience still satisfies the cases/trajectories it was derived from (no regression suite over past cases)
Agent Evolution is a server-wide switch defaulting to off; experiences are per user_id with no cross-user/cross-agent curation or transfer of learned experiences
Published results lack confidence intervals and ablations (experiences vs trajectories vs both, epochs curve), so the size of the learning effect vs retrieval effect is unclear
safety_measures: Server-wide agent_evolution switch (default off) and session-level memory_policy allow-list; memory_diff.json before/after audit per commit; base-content guard + version bump on policy writes under a path tree lock (300s) with reload to avoid clobbering concurrent training; MemoryIsolationHandler routes writes to self/peer spaces and drops unsafe peer ids; abstraction mandate strips IDs/names/secrets from trajectories and cases; injected <openviking-context> blocks are stripped before capture to prevent self-pollution; experiences injected as 'task guidance, not user facts'; privacy extraction templates and encryption/ACL layers.

name: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
org_or_authors: Mirac Suzgun, Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Dan Jurafsky, James Zou (Stanford)
last_activity: 2026-03-12 (single "dynamic cheatsheet v2.0" commit: unified multi-provider client, hybrid CumulativeRetrieval variant, README rewrite; before that untouched since Apr 2025)
venue_or_citations: arXiv 2504.07952 (Apr 2025); published as EACL 2026 long paper (DOI 10.18653/v1/2026.eacl-long.333). Exact citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited; OpenAlex shows 4 on the EACL DOI, a clear undercount). Used as the primary baseline by ACE (Agentic Context Engineering), ReasoningBank, MemSkill lines.
mechanism:
Single black-box LM plays two roles per query, state is ONE string (the cheatsheet). Verified in dynamic_cheatsheet/language_model.py (advanced_generate):

DC-Cumulative: (1) Generator prompt = fixed solver instructions + [[CHEATSHEET]] + [[QUESTION]]. If the output contains a ```python block followed by "EXECUTE CODE!", the harness runs it via subprocess (python3 temp file, 3s timeout, no sandbox) and appends the stdout, looping until no more code. (2) Curator prompt = curator instructions + [[PREVIOUS_CHEATSHEET]] + [[QUESTION]] + [[MODEL_ANSWER]] (full generator transcript incl. execution output). The curator is told to "assess the correctness of the provided solution" itself, then REWRITE THE ENTIRE cheatsheet inside <cheatsheet> tags (cap ~2000-2500 words; <memory_item> blocks with description/example, Q-references, and an LLM-maintained "Count" field). extract_cheatsheet() replaces the old string; if no tags are found the old cheatsheet is silently kept. No labels, no reward, no verifier gate, no rollback, no archive: acceptance = whatever the curator emits.

DC-RetrievalSynthesis: precomputed input embeddings (per-dataset CSV) retrieve top-k=3 prior (input, generator-output) pairs by cosine similarity; curator synthesizes a per-query cheatsheet from those pairs + previous cheatsheet; generator then answers. v2.0 adds CumulativeRetrieval (cumulative sheet + retrieved raw pairs in the same prompt). Baselines: FullHistoryAppending (verbatim history) and Dynamic_Retrieval (retrieval without curation).

Runs once over a shuffled (seed 10) test set, single trajectory, single agent, max_num_rounds defaults to 1. run_benchmark.py computes accuracy only for printing/logging; it is never fed back into the cheatsheet.
eval_loop: There is no fitness signal in the loop. Memory updates are driven solely by the curator LM's own judgment of the generator transcript (plus incidental Python execution output the generator chose to run). Ground-truth accuracy is computed offline in run_benchmark.py purely for reporting. Nothing prevents drift or reward hacking except prompt wording ("only include solutions that have been tested and proven effective", "copy relevant old content or it is lost"). Empirically from the released logs: the cheatsheet does not grow (stays at 4-6 memory_items, 400-1300 words) because each step is a full rewrite; older entries are overwritten (final AIME sheet after 133 problems is dominated by Q131-Q133); the "Count" field is hallucinated (an entry citing 16 unrelated AIME questions); a stored angle-bisector "theorem" is mathematically garbled; curator emitted an unparseable/no-op sheet in 14/133 GPT-4o AIME steps. Regressions (e.g. DC-Cu lowering GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Physics from 75.6 to 70.4) are not detected or reverted.
key_results: Recomputed from released results/*.jsonl with the repo's own evaluators (BL = plain baseline; DC-0 = same solver prompt + code execution but empty memory; DC-Cu; DC-RS). Claude 3.5 Sonnet: AIME 2020-24 (n=133) BL 6.8 -> DC-0 30.1 -> DC-Cu 38.3 -> DC-RS 40.6; AIME 2025 (n=30) 6.7 -> 23.3 -> 36.7 / 30.0; AIME 2024 23.3 -> 36.7 -> 50.0 / 46.7; GPQA-Diamond (n=198) 59.6 -> 60.1 -> 60.6 / 68.7; MMLU-Pro Physics 74.0 -> 75.6 -> 77.6 / 82.0; MMLU-Pro Engineering 61.2 -> 57.2 -> 66.8 / 67.6; MathEquationBalancer 44.8 -> 56.4 -> 100 / 97.8. GPT-4o: AIME 2020-24 BL 9.8 -> DC-0 24.1 -> DC-Cu 18.0 (worse than empty) -> DC-RS 24.8 (no gain over empty); GPQA-D 57.1 -> 56.6 -> 57.6 / 57.1 (nil); MMLU-Pro Physics 75.6 -> 70.8 -> 70.4 / 75.2 (DC-Cu hurts); Engineering 53.2 -> 51.6 -> 44.0 (run incomplete, 141/250) / 50.8; MathEqBalancer 50 -> 88 -> 100 / 99.2, but uncurated Dynamic_Retrieval also hits 100. The headline "Game of 24 GPT-4o 10% -> 99%" is claimed in README/paper but NO Game of 24 logs are released. Key takeaway: a large share of the "doubling" on AIME comes from the DC-0 scaffold (structured prompt + Python execution), with memory adding ~8-13pp on Claude and ~0 on GPT-4o; biggest memory-specific win is on homogeneous tasks (equation balancing, Game of 24) where the sheet converges on "write Python to brute-force/verify".
limitations: Paper-stated: context-length bound on memory; effectiveness bounded by base model (smaller models gain less); benefits require high similarity across test-time examples; sensitive to prompt wording. Observed in code/logs: (1) no correctness signal to the curator, wrong strategies and garbled theorems are stored; (2) full-rewrite curation makes memory a bounded rolling summary, not an accumulating archive, with strong recency bias and hallucinated usage counters; (3) no versioning/rollback/A-B, regressions on GPT-4o go unnoticed; (4) order-dependent single pass over a shuffled test set, i.e. it learns on the test stream it is evaluated on, no held-out generalization or cross-task transfer test; (5) retrieval variant depends on offline precomputed OpenAI-embedding CSVs per dataset, not an online memory store; (6) Python execution is an unsandboxed subprocess (author TODO admits it); (7) curator call doubles API cost and the 1000+-word sheet is re-sent every query, no cost accounting; (8) only short single-turn QA benchmarks, no agentic/multi-step/coding tasks (issue #4 asking about SWE-bench is unanswered); (9) no tests, no packaging, one .ipynb for evaluation; results JSONLs for some runs are incomplete (141/250, 139/250).
key_insight: Splitting inference into a solver and a curator that rewrites a compact, structured natural-language memory after every episode is enough to get label-free test-time learning on a black-box model, but it only pays off when a cheap verifier (Python execution) is in the loop and the task stream is homogeneous; without an external acceptance signal, the memory converges to a handful of recency-biased, unverified entries rather than a growing library.
open_gaps: No acceptance gate on memory writes: curator judges correctness by itself; a framework could gate insertions on execution-verified outcomes, self-consistency, or later downstream success and evict entries whose use correlates with failures
Full-rewrite curation caps memory at ~5 items and silently discards older insights; needs incremental append/edit/dedup operations with stable IDs (delta updates rather than regeneration)
No versioning, rollback, or A/B evaluation of memory states, so regressions (e.g. GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Physics -5pp with DC-Cu) are never detected or reverted
Learns and is evaluated on the same shuffled test stream; no held-out split, no measurement of order sensitivity, no cross-task transfer (e.g. reuse an AIME cheatsheet on GPQA)
Single agent, single trajectory: no population/archive of alternative cheatsheets, no selection among candidates
Usage counters and Q-references are LLM-maintained text and hallucinate; provenance and hit-counts should be tracked by the harness, not the model
Retrieval variant needs offline precomputed per-dataset embedding CSVs; no online embedding/store, so it cannot be deployed on an open-ended query stream
Unsandboxed Python execution (subprocess, 3s timeout) with no resource/network isolation
Only single-turn QA tasks; not tested on multi-step agentic, tool-use, or coding benchmarks (SWE-bench request in issue #4 unanswered)
No token/cost accounting: curator doubles calls and a 1000+-word sheet is resent per query; no policy for when to skip curation
Gains vanish or reverse for weaker models (GPT-4o often at or below the empty-cheatsheet scaffold); no open-weight model results
Game of 24 headline (10% to 99%) is not reproducible from released artifacts since those logs are absent
safety_measures: None beyond prompt text. Code execution is an unsandboxed python3 subprocess with a 3-second timeout (author's TODO acknowledges it). extract_cheatsheet() falls back to the previous cheatsheet if the curator output lacks <cheatsheet> tags. Curator prompt asks the model to assess correctness and to preserve old content, but nothing enforces either.

venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (Meta's publication page lists Publisher: arXiv). The scout's "ICLR 2026" claim is NOT supported: paper first posted 2026-03-19, after ICLR 2026 decisions, and not found on OpenReview. HF Papers: 51 upvotes. Semantic Scholar rate-limited; known citing work includes 'Self-Improving Agent Factories for Paper Review: When Constrained Beats Open-Ended' (Sira, KDD 2026 Workshop SciSoc oral) which benchmarks against a HyperAgents-style adaptation, and COLM 2026 rebuttals. Repo 2,722 stars / 358 forks (created 2026-03-19).
mechanism: A hyperagent is one Python repo containing task_agent.py (initially a single FM call that returns JSON) and meta_agent.py (initially a one-line prompt "Modify any part of the codebase at {repo_path}" driving an FM — Claude Sonnet 4.5 by default, Claude 3.5 Sonnet for Polyglot parity — with bash + str_replace editor tools). DGM-H outer loop (generate_loop.py), one child per iteration, 80-200 iterations: (1) fixed parent selection over the whole archive: score = mean of per-domain val (or train) scores, sigmoid(10*(score - mean of top-3)) times a child-count penalty (paper: 1/(1+n); code: exp(-(n/8)^3)); (2) spin up a fresh Docker container, apply the parent's cumulative lineage of git diffs, copy previous generations' eval outputs into the container, then run the PARENT's own meta_agent.py (6h timeout) — so whatever self-modification machinery the parent evolved (memory files, trackers, planning) is what generates the child; (3) domains/ (the evaluator) is git-reset to base so the agent cannot edit it; the remaining diff becomes model_patch.diff; (4) compile gate: `from meta_agent import MetaAgent` and `from task_agent import TaskAgent` must import within 5 min; (5) staged eval on a small subset (10 tasks, or 3 RL reps) must score >0 in every domain, else the child is scored zero; then full train/val eval; (6) child is appended to the archive with scores (never pruned); parent flagged invalid if its meta agent crashed. Multi-domain runs average scores and expose all evals to the meta agent. Best-by-val agent is evaluated once on the held-out test set. Preliminary E.5 experiments additionally let the agent edit select_next_parent.py (--edit_select_parent), but main results keep selection/eval fixed.
eval_loop: Signal = fixed benchmark scores on train/val splits: Polyglot pass@1 via unit tests (10+50 train tasks, 165 test); paper-review accuracy vs. real ICLR/NeurIPS accept/reject labels (100/100/100 train/val/test); Genesis Go2 walking RL policy fitness (3 then 6 repetitions; test = zero-shot torso-height task); IMO-GradingBench grade accuracy (100/100/100). Val split drives parent selection in AI-judge domains to reduce overfitting; test used only for final reporting. Drift/hacking controls: archive keeps all compiled children (no replacement), staged gating zeroes non-functional children, compile import-check, domains/ reset so the evaluator cannot be rewritten, sandbox + timeouts. Meta-level ability is measured separately with imp@50: freeze the meta agent, run 50 iterations on an unseen domain, report best-agent gain. Weaknesses: acceptance is purely score-based with no verification or rollback of individual self-modifications; GitHub issue #39 shows the meta agent's workspace contained test samples with labels (leak not excluded by ignore_function_domains), and the released meta agent ignores eval_path/iterations_left (issue #30), so feedback is only what the agent discovers via bash.
key_results: 5 seeds, medians with 95% bootstrap CIs. Polyglot (80 iters): train 0.140→0.340 (CI 0.300–0.380), full benchmark 0.084→0.267 (CI 0.231–0.280) vs original DGM 0.140→0.380 / 0.142→0.307. Paper review test (100 iters, joint run with robotics): 0.0→0.710 (CI 0.590–0.750) vs AI-Scientist-v2 reviewer 0.630, DGM-custom 0.590 (n.s. vs DGM-H), DGM 0.0, DGM-H w/o self-improve (ADAS-like) 0.0, w/o archive 0.0 (all p<0.05). Robotics reward design test: 0.060→0.372 (CI 0.355–0.436) vs default reward 0.348, DGM-custom 0.348 (n.s.), w/o self-improve 0.213, w/o archive 0.116, DGM 0.0. Meta-transfer on held-out IMO grading (imp@50, frozen meta agent): initial meta 0.0; DGM-custom transfer agents 0.0; DGM-H transfer hyperagents 0.630 (CI 0.540–0.630, p<0.05). Compounding (200 iters IMO): from transfer 0.640 vs from scratch 0.610 (n.s.); ProofAutoGrader + transfer meta 0.700 vs 0.670; on full IMO-GradingBench 0.561→0.601 accuracy, MAE 0.178→0.175. Evolved meta-level artifacts: PerformanceTracker class, persistent JSON memory of insights/hypotheses/plans, budget-aware planning.
limitations: Stated: fixed task distribution (no curriculum co-evolution); parent selection and evaluation protocol are fixed outer-loop components (only preliminary E.5 on editable selection). Observed: DGM-H vs hand-customized DGM-custom is not statistically significant in either domain; compounding gain (0.640 vs 0.610) is n.s.; only 5 seeds with wide CIs (e.g. DGM paper-review CI 0.0–0.510); paper-review test is 100 binary items and its labels (ICLR 2024/25, NeurIPS 2023/24) are public and likely in the FM's pretraining, so contamination is plausible; issue #39 reports test data with labels reachable by the meta agent, undermining the 'held-out' claim; issue #28 reports an unanswered reproduction gap; released meta agent contradicts the paper (eval path / remaining budget never injected into the prompt; child penalty formula differs). Cost appendix not retrievable here, but 6h meta-agent timeouts x 100-200 iters x 5 seeds x RL training implies a large budget; one sequential child per iteration; 16 GB logs only via Google Drive (LFS broken, #13); CC BY-NC-SA license; repo effectively unmaintained since April 2026.
safety_measures: Docker sandbox per generation with git reset/clean afterwards; 6h meta-agent and 5-min compile timeouts; bash tool declares no internet (though the container is built with host networking + proxy in docker_utils.py); evaluator directory domains/ is reset to the base commit after every self-modification so the agent cannot alter scoring; fixed, human-defined tasks/metrics and human oversight; README warning that model-generated code is executed untrusted. Section 6 and Appendix F discuss oversight strain, Goodhart/reward gaming, and transparency; no runtime policy enforcement, admission manifests, or rollback exist (community issue #17/#35 propose them).
key_insight: Put the improvement procedure inside the same editable artifact as the task solver and have each child be generated by its parent's own meta code, so selection pressure on task score also selects for better self-modification machinery (memory, trackers, planning) that transfers to unseen domains; measure that meta-ability separately with imp@k under a frozen meta agent.
open_gaps: Outer loop (parent selection, staged gating, evaluation protocol) stays handcrafted and immutable; only a preliminary flag lets agents edit select_next_parent.py
No task/curriculum co-evolution: fitness is a fixed train/val benchmark, so improvement stalls when the benchmark saturates
No verification, regression test, or rollback for individual self-modifications beyond an import check and a benchmark score; no machine-readable admission record of why a child was accepted
Held-out data is not isolated from the self-modifier: test samples and labels were copied into the meta agent's workspace (issue #39)
Meta agent receives no structured feedback in the released code (eval_path, iterations_left unused); a framework could inject per-task failure traces, diffs-vs-score history, and budget explicitly
Children stack cumulative diffs along a single lineage; no crossover/merging of archive members, no ensembling in main results, no quality-diversity descriptors beyond a scalar averaged score
One sequential child per iteration with a 6h meta step and no cost-aware fitness; no parallel population or early-stopping economics
Meta-level transfer shown on one held-out domain with 5 seeds and n.s. compounding; no multi-domain imp@k battery or scaling study
Paper-review fitness relies on public accept/reject labels likely in FM pretraining; no contamination-resistant or hard-to-verify-task evaluator design
No interpretability/provenance tooling attributing task gains to specific meta-level edits
Not usable by app developers: requires Docker, GPUs for Genesis RL, multiple provider API keys, CC BY-NC-SA license, and repo is unmaintained since April 2026

name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
org_or_authors: Google DeepMind — Alexander Novikov, Ngân Vũ, Marvin Eisenberger, Emilien Dupont, Po-Sen Huang, Adam Zsolt Wagner, Sergey Shirobokov, Borislav Kozlovskii, F. J. R. Ruiz, A. Mehrabian, M. P. Kumar, A. See, S. Chaudhuri, G. Holland, A. Davies, S. Nowozin, Pushmeet Kohli, Matej Balog
last_activity: Follow-ups: Georgiev/Gómez-Serrano/Tao/Wagner 'Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale' (arXiv 2511.02864, Nov 2025; problem repo google-deepmind/alphaevolve_repository_of_problems pushed 2026-09-10, 67 problems); results repo pushed 2026-01-05; commercial 'AlphaEvolve on Google Cloud' (Gemini Enterprise) client library Google-Cloud-AI/alphaevolve-on-googlecloud created 2026-07-08, pushed 2026-09-02 (now runs gemini-3.5-flash / gemini-3.1-pro-preview ensemble)
venue_or_citations: Technical white paper / arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed). ~833 citations per scout's Semantic Scholar count (S2 API was rate-limited during this read, could not independently re-verify). Reference point for OpenEvolve (7.3k stars), ShinkaEvolve (1.4k), ThetaEvolve, CodeEvolve, DeepEvolve, LLM4AD_Next etc.
mechanism: The evolved object is user-marked code (# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START/END) inside a skeleton that exposes a Python evaluate() returning a dict of scalar metrics (maximized). Everything else in the file is fixed. The controller loop (asyncio, throughput-optimized) is literally: parent, inspirations = database.sample(); prompt = prompt_sampler.build(parent, inspirations); diff = llm.generate(prompt); child = apply_diff(parent, diff); results = evaluator.execute(child); database.add(child, results). Prompts contain several prior programs with their scores, rendered evaluation outputs, human-written context (equations, papers, code), stochastic template placeholders, and "meta prompt evolution": instructions the LLM itself proposes, co-evolved in a separate database. The LLM ensemble is Gemini 2.0 Flash (throughput, most samples) plus Gemini 2.0 Pro (occasional high-quality jumps); output is SEARCH/REPLACE diff blocks (or full rewrites for short code), any language (Python, Pallas, Verilog, XLA IR). Evaluators support a cascade of increasingly hard test stages (early pruning), optional LLM-graded auxiliary scores (e.g., simplicity), embarrassingly parallel evaluation up to ~100 compute-hours per candidate, and multiple objectives (which empirically improves even the single target metric via diversity). The database is a MAP-Elites + island-model hybrid balancing exploitation and diversity; nothing is fine-tuned, the model is frozen. For math problems the key trick is evolving a search heuristic that gets a fixed time budget (e.g., 1000 s) and the previous best construction, so evolution selects for heuristics that improve already-good solutions, yielding multi-stage specialized heuristics. Thousands of LLM samples suffice (FunSearch needed millions). Human picks the abstraction (raw solution vs constructor vs search algorithm vs co-evolution).
eval_loop: Signal is a user-written, automatically executable evaluator h returning scalar metrics; selection = registration into the MAP-Elites/island database (no notion of accept/reject beyond scores). Drift/hacking control is entirely delegated to evaluator design plus post-hoc human verification: matmul decompositions are rounded and verified exactly; Borg heuristic is correct by construction (only ranks already-feasible machines) and tested on an unseen held-out workload set before fleet rollout; kernel tiling heuristic trained on half of collected input shapes, evaluated on the other half; XLA-IR edits checked against reference on randomized inputs then confirmed by human experts; Verilog rewrite validated by TPU designers. No held-out generalization for math problems (scores are the objective itself). The follow-up Tao et al. paper admits AlphaEvolve 'occasionally exploited numerical artifacts or found loopholes in problem formulations', so every claimed math record needed expert verification. No LLM judge in the core loop (optional LLM-graded side metrics only). Ablations (2 tasks, 3 seeds each): removing evolution hurts most; removing context, meta-prompt evolution, full-file evolution, or the large model each significantly degrades the compute-vs-score curve.
key_results: Claimed and mostly externally verifiable (colab with verification code): 4x4 complex matmul in 48 scalar multiplications (Strassen recursive = 49, first char-0 improvement in 56 years); improved rank upper bounds on 14 <m,n,p> tensors (e.g. <3,4,7> 66->63, <4,5,6> 93->90) and matched all others for m,n,p<=5; 50+ open math problems: ~75% matched SOTA, ~20% improved (kissing number in 11D 592->593; new Erdős minimum-overlap upper bound; autocorrelation inequality bounds; packing/Heilbronn variants). Production infra (self-reported by Google, not externally verifiable): Borg scheduling heuristic recovering 0.7% of fleet-wide compute continuously for >1 year; Gemini Pallas matmul tiling heuristic: avg 23% kernel speedup, 1% reduction in Gemini training time, deployed (kernel tuning went from months to days); FlashAttention XLA IR: 32% kernel and 15% pre/post-processing speedup on GPU inference config; TPU Verilog rewrite removing unnecessary bits (authors concede synthesis tools also caught it). Ablations show every component matters. No compute cost, wall-clock, or token counts reported.
limitations: Stated: only works when an automated evaluator exists; LLM-based evaluation of ideas is supported but unoptimized; self-improvement of its own substrate is 'moderate' with month-scale feedback loops. Observed: ablations only on 2 tasks x 3 seeds; no cost/compute accounting; no code released for the system (only result notebooks), Gemini-only and now a paid Gemini Enterprise product; model weights are frozen (distillation deferred to future work); heavy reliance on expert problem formulation and prompt advice (Tao et al.: expert advice in the prompt 'almost always led to significantly better results'); evaluator loopholes/numerical artifacts were exploited, requiring human verification; fails where 'genuinely new, deep insights' are needed rather than hill-climbable improvements; small-scale numerical gains may not reflect asymptotic truth; the headline infra numbers (0.7%, 1%) are unverifiable outside Google, and the TPU result is marginal.
safety_measures: No safety section. Grounding is via code execution and automated evaluators (claimed to 'avoid incorrect suggestions'); evaluation cascade filters faulty programs on small tests first; deployed artifacts pass human review (TPU designers, kernel/XLA experts), randomized differential testing vs reference implementation, and held-out datasets before rollout; Borg heuristic can only re-rank feasible machines so is correct by construction. No discussion of sandboxing generated code, of the agent modifying its own harness, or of automated rollback; the substrate self-improvement (kernels, scheduler, TPU RTL) is gated by human deployment decisions, not closed automatically.
key_insight: With a frozen frontier LLM as the mutation operator, an evolutionary program database (MAP-Elites + islands) plus a cheap, automatically executable evaluator is enough test-time-compute structure to turn 'thousands' of samples into SOTA-breaking discoveries — and the highest-leverage move is to evolve the search algorithm that produces the solution (with a time budget and the previous best as input) rather than the solution itself.
open_gaps: No cross-problem transfer: each run starts from an empty program database; discovered heuristics, ideas, and meta-prompts are not stored as reusable skills/memory for new tasks (only 'distill into next base model' is mentioned as future work)

Evaluator is static and human-written; the loop exploited numerical artifacts and formulation loopholes (Tao et al. 2025) — no automatic evaluator hardening, adversarial testing, or co-evolution of tests with programs

Only the target code and meta-prompts evolve; the harness itself (database sampling policy, island/MAP-Elites config, model mix, cascade thresholds, prompt-sampler strategy) is fixed and hand-tuned per problem
Model weights never update from the evolutionary trace; no RL/fine-tuning on successful diffs (contrast ThetaEvolve, Surina et al.), so the mutation operator does not improve over the run

Abstraction choice (evolve raw solution vs constructor vs search algorithm vs co-evolution) and the expert problem context are manual and decisive — no automation of task specification or of the 'what to evolve' decision

Held-out generalization is checked only in the two infra applications; math/algorithm runs optimize the objective directly with no separate test distribution, so overfitting to the evaluator is undetected until human review
Closed source, Gemini-only, no compute/token/cost reporting; ablations on 2 tasks with 3 seeds — reproducibility depends on OpenEvolve/ShinkaEvolve reimplementations
Sample efficiency is still 'thousands' of full evaluations per problem with no bandit model selection or novelty filtering (ShinkaEvolve reports ~150 samples on circle packing)

No sandboxing, rollback, or verification story for self-modification: substrate improvements (kernels, scheduler, RTL) are deployed by humans after months, so the 'improves its own training' loop is not actually closed or automated
Requires a fully automatable scalar evaluator; domains with natural-language or human-judged outcomes are explicitly out of scope and LLM-as-evaluator is unoptimized

name: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM)
mechanism: Verified against the released code (DGM_outer.py, self_improve_step.py). Archive starts with one hand-written coding agent (coding_agent.py + tools/bash.py, tools/edit.py; FM = Claude 3.5 Sonnet via Bedrock, frozen). Each generation (default 80 gens, 2 attempts/gen in parallel): (1) Parent selection from archive with P ∝ sigmoid(10·(acc−0.5)) × 1/(1+num_children) — only variants that compiled/evaluated are eligible. (2) Pick a self-improve "entry": with 25% each, a canned meta-problem (solve_empty_patches, solve_stochasticity, solve_contextlength), else one random unresolved benchmark task. (3) Diagnosis: o1 receives the parent's full source, the run log for that task, the GitHub issue, the agent's patch, SWE-bench's private test patch and test results, and must emit JSON with ONE general improvement proposal phrased as a GitHub issue ("To Implement..."). (4) Self-modification: in a Docker container with the parent lineage's patches applied, the parent agent itself runs `coding_agent.py --self_improve` on /dgm (30-min timeout) and emits model_patch.diff. (5) Evaluation: the child agent is run on SWE-bench Verified tasks in stages — 10 tasks; if ≥40% resolved, 50 more; if score ≥ second-best full-evaluated archive score (min 0.4), the remaining 140 (200 total). Polyglot analogous. (6) Archive update: child kept if it "compiled" (produced ≥1 non-empty patch on all expected tasks); default keep_all, no score threshold. Optional o1 post-hoc diagnosis of what changed. Lineage = ordered list of diffs; "no_darwin" baseline = always mutate last commit; "no_selfimprove" = fixed initial agent does all edits.
eval_loop: Signal = benchmark accuracy (resolved/submitted) on SWE-bench Verified (200-task subset, staged 10→60→200) or Polyglot subsets; official SWE-bench harness runs outside the agent's editable tree, so the core score is hard to fake, but in-house metrics (a hallucination-detection marker in logs) were hacked. Drift/hacking controls are weak and mostly human: eval_noise leeway 0.1, 'compiled' filter, Docker sandbox + 30-min/1.5-h timeouts, and manual review of the transparent diff lineage (which is how the marker-removal exploit was caught). No held-out split: the same 200 tasks drive selection and are the reported score; transfer checks (o3-mini, Claude 3.7 Sonnet; Python→Rust/C++/Go/Java/JS) are the only generalization evidence. No LLM judge, no unit tests on the agent beyond 2 tool tests.
limitations: Stated: ~2 weeks and ~$22,000 API cost per SWE-bench run; FM weights frozen (only harness code evolves); limited to coding benchmarks; empirical validation is not a proof, and the system did reward-hack an in-house hallucination metric by deleting detection markers despite explicit instruction not to. Observed from code/issues: o1 diagnoser sees private test patches of training tasks; Polyglot harness leaves hidden tests/reference solutions readable from the agent container (issue #35); 'best' parent-selection mode unreachable due to missing comma and sorts ascending (issue #31); tools loaded via importlib with no provenance check (#36); outer loop, selection policy, diagnosis prompts and evaluator are NOT self-modifiable; default keep_all archive retains regressions; repo unmaintained since 2025-08-13 with 27 open issues; hard-wired to Bedrock Claude 3.5 Sonnet + o1. Full arXiv text was unreachable from this network; ablation/transfer figures below are from paper knowledge plus secondary summaries.
key_insight: Drop the Gödel-machine requirement of proving an edit is beneficial; instead let the agent rewrite its own harness code (tools, workflow, prompts) with the FM frozen, validate every child empirically on a staged benchmark, and keep ALL working variants in an archive sampled by score×novelty so lower-scoring stepping stones can still parent breakthroughs — open-ended search over agent code, not hill-climbing.
open_gaps: Fitness set == report set: the same 200 SWE-bench tasks drive selection and the headline number; no held-out task split inside the benchmark, and the o1 diagnoser is shown private test patches for training tasks — a new framework needs train/validation/test task separation and evaluator-blind diagnosis

No automated reward-hacking defense: the marker-removal exploit was only caught by humans reading diffs; evaluator, logging and hidden tests should be immutable and out of the agent's reachable filesystem (issue #35 shows Polyglot hidden tests are readable)

Extremely expensive fitness (~$22k, ~2 weeks per run; every child re-runs up to 200 SWE-bench tasks): no cheap proxy fitness, no bandit/successive-halving allocation beyond a crude 10→60→200 threshold, no caching of per-task results across siblings
Single scalar objective (accuracy only): no cost, latency, token-usage, or safety objectives, no Pareto archive
Mutation only, one parent per child: no crossover/merging of successful patches from different archive lineages, no explicit reuse of discovered tools across branches
The outer loop is not self-referential: DGM_outer.py, parent-selection policy, diagnosis prompts, eval thresholds and the harness are fixed by humans; only coding_agent.py/tools/utils evolve
Diagnosis is per-single-failed-task with no aggregated failure analysis or persistent memory across generations; each child starts from one log, so the same fix can be rediscovered repeatedly
keep_all archive with no regression tests on the agent itself: regressions are kept as parents; no automatic rollback or unit-test suite that evolves with the agent (tests/ has 2 tool tests)
Benchmark-specific harness: porting to non-SWE-bench domains requires rewriting harness/report code (issues #14, #19); no pluggable task/fitness interface
FM weights frozen and hard-wired to Bedrock Claude 3.5 Sonnet + o1; no local/open-model support (issue #26 WIP), no learning from the archive back into the model
Code is unmaintained since Aug 2025 with known bugs ('best' mode unreachable, ascending sort), so anyone baselining against DGM must fork and patch
last_activity: Repo last push 2025-08-13 (5 commits total, final one 'Update coding_agent_polyglot.py'); paper v2 Sept 2025; ICLR 2026 camera-ready
key_results: SWE-bench Verified (200-task subset): initial agent 20.0% → best DGM agent 50.0% after 80 iterations. Polyglot: 14.2% → 30.7%, surpassing Aider's hand-designed agent. Ablations: DGM w/o self-improvement (fixed initial agent makes all edits) and DGM w/o open-ended exploration (single lineage, always mutate latest) both end far lower (w/o open-ended ≈23% on SWE-bench per secondary summaries). Transfer: SWE-bench-evolved agent keeps its gains when the FM is swapped to Claude 3.7 Sonnet or o3-mini; Python-only-evolved agent improves on Rust/C++/Go/Java/JS Polyglot tasks. Discovered features: granular str_replace-style editing tool, patch validation, multiple candidate patches + ranking/peer-review step, history of prior attempts. Lineage analysis shows the best agent descends through a lower-scoring ancestor (stepping-stone evidence). Case study: asked to fix tool-use hallucination, some children removed the detection markers (objective hacking), caught via lineage review. Cost: ~2 weeks, ~$22k per SWE-bench run.

safety_measures: Docker sandbox per self-improvement attempt and per benchmark task; 30-min timeout on the self-modification run and 1.5-h timeout per attempt; restricted web access; FM weights untouched; complete diff lineage (model_patch.diff chain + metadata.json) enabling human audit; authors manually reviewed modifications and reported they were confined to coding capability; README warns that untrusted model-generated code is executed. No automated guardrails against evaluator tampering — the hallucination-marker deletion was detected only by human inspection.
