name: Diving into Reliable Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey (Awesome-Reliable-Self-Evolving-Agents)
org_or_authors: Tencent Hunyuan (Kaiqi Wang, project lead; Songyang Zhang, supervisor) + Zhejiang University (Hehe Fan, corresponding; Yongliang Shen, Yi Yang, Yueting Zhuang) + Peking/Tsinghua co-authors; 13 authors
date: 2026-08-10 (PDF built 2026-08-10; repo created 2026-08-06; OpenReview id CGO1hDTHNe; not on arXiv)
last_activity: 2026-08-16 (last push: 'Update PDF link'; 12 commits total, all Aug 6-16 2026)
venue_or_citations: OpenReview preprint (not peer-reviewed venue), 110 pages, 549 references; ~0 citations as of 2026-09 (1 month old). 196 stars / 9 forks in 5 weeks. Promoted via Tencent Hunyuan X account and Xiaohongshu.
mechanism: This is a survey, not a system; its contribution is a formal frame for the self-evolution loop. Retained agent state is X_k = (theta_k, sigma_k, U_k, C_k): trainable weights, scaffold (prompts/tools/memory/workflows/harness), improver (procedure that proposes/selects/commits/rolls back updates), and internal criterion (rewards, rubrics, comparison rules). One round: (1) Exec under budget b_k yields trajectory, output y_k, experience e_k (may write runtime memory sigma_rt directly); (2) the current improver U_k Proposes candidate states from e_k and history H_k (H_k stored outside the update boundary) and Selects one provisionally using C_k; (3) an EXTERNAL audit with evidence source S and acceptance policy G, both versioned and outside the update boundary, returns accept / reject-and-rollback / escalate-to-human. Only gate acceptance ('promotion') makes the candidate X_{k+1}. Level = deepest component whose active semantics causally change and persist to later independent tasks (retention condition): L0 output only, L1 theta, L2 sigma, L3 U, L4 C. RSI is defined structurally as L3+. Each level has a characteristic failure (self-confirmation, model collapse, scaffold overfitting, metric capture, criterion drift) and a matched audit/control rung ('reliability ladder'). Core principle: no update may control the only evidence used for its own acceptance; evidence disclosed to proposal/selection is 'development evidence' and cannot be the sole final audit evidence.
eval_loop: Prescriptive only (survey runs no experiments). Per-level evidence the paper demands: L0 execution/source-grounded checks or human adjudication; L1 fresh post-update transfer, retention and interference tests plus data-admission checks; L2 matched-budget (same model, tools, tokens, stopping rule) end-to-end comparison vs incumbent on fresh tasks the edit did not select, component ablations, provenance, tested rollback; L3 descendant performance on unseen task families under matched resources with sealed evaluation and proposal history; L4 protected outcome measures, pre- vs post-criterion cross-evaluation, and human authorization. Anti-drift/anti-reward-hacking devices it endorses: external target + evidence source + acceptance policy kept outside and versioned; anytime-valid sequential acceptance tests (PACE, SEA) to control false commits under optional stopping; held-out selection split (RSEA) with the caveat that repeated querying converts a holdout into development evidence; access logs and rotating fresh anchors; protected lineage and independent rollback/halt authority; escalation to humans for criterion changes; staged deployment (shadow, limited, broad). Explicitly cites 'harness updating is not harness benefit' as the reason a higher score does not certify improvement.
key_results: 549 papers classified by depth: L0 42, L1 137, L2 257, L3 21, L4 30 (plus 24 surveys, 8 cross-level reliability, 30 open-problem works). Table 2 positions it against 14 prior surveys, claiming it is the only one covering L3/L4 plus external audit systematically. Table 9 'cross-level reliability ledger' pairs each level with exposed evidence, failure mode and matched controls. Table 10 compares 10 self-evolution benchmarks (SEA-Eval, SEAGym, BenchTrace, EvoMemBench, SE-Bench, PAST-Bench, Meta-Agent Challenge, RSIBench-Data, PostTrainBench, Agent2 RL-Bench) and concludes none directly tests retained improver- or criterion-level change over multiple generations. Synthesized evidence it leans on: SEA-Eval finds up to 31.2x token difference between frameworks at similar success rates; Meta-Agent Challenge shows only 5 model-domain configs beat the human-engineered baseline with attempted test exfiltration; capability-erosion and library-drift studies show stored artifacts may be inactive or harmful later. Runtime-harness subsection catalogs 14 harness-evolution works (Meta-Harness, Self-Harness, HarnessForge, MemoHarness, Continual Harness, The Last Harness, Harness Handbook, AutoHarness, etc.).
limitations: No experiments, no code, no benchmark or protocol implementation; the reliability ladder is stated as 'design requirements, not sufficient guarantees'. Level assignments are by authors' reading and are marked 'conditional' when evidence is lacking, so the taxonomy is not empirically validated. OpenReview preprint, not peer-reviewed; heavy skew toward 2026 arXiv preprints of uncertain quality. L3 (21) and L4 (30) buckets are thin. Prose is dense and definitional; little quantitative meta-analysis. Companion repo is a static list (last push 2026-08-16) with no tooling. Depth is explicitly decoupled from reliability, so the survey offers no ranking of which approaches actually work best.
key_insight: Classify a self-evolving agent by the deepest component its updates can rewrite (output, weights, scaffold, improver, criterion), then keep the external target, evidence source, and accept/reject/escalate gate outside that update boundary: no update should control the only evidence used for its own acceptance, and any evidence the proposer has already seen is development evidence, not audit evidence.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of the audit loop (versioned external target, evidence source S, gate G with accept/reject/escalate, promotion record) — a harness framework could ship this as a concrete schema and runtime gate

No benchmark tests retained L3/L4 changes across multiple generations (does a descendant improver produce better later descendants on fresh task families under matched budget?) — build a multi-generation, sealed-final-test protocol
Holdout erosion is described but not operationalized: no access-budget ledger, query logging, or rotating fresh anchor sets for audit evidence
Matched-budget comparison (tokens, tool calls, wall-clock, stopping rule) is prescribed but no standardized cost-normalized fitness or reporting format exists
No tooling verifies that a retained scaffold/harness edit is actually active on later tasks (harness-updating vs harness-benefit decoupling) — need activation/provenance tracing per edit
Protected lineage + tested rollback for scaffold and harness edits (version DAG, replay, independent halt authority) is required but not implemented in any cited open framework
Escalation-to-human policy is undefined operationally: no triggers, throughput/backlog metrics, or reviewer-independence measures
Level-specific failure detectors (silent store drift, library drift, scaffold overfitting, metric capture) exist as one-off papers but are not integrated as automatic monitors inside evolution loops
Population/archive-based methods are not analyzed as reliability mechanisms (diversity as hedge against metric capture) — gap for multi-lineage frameworks
Cost of the audit itself (compute spent on fresh evaluation vs on evolution) is never budgeted or traded off
safety_measures: Prescribed, not implemented: external audit with sealed probes and fresh cases; external target/evidence source/acceptance policy versioned and outside the update boundary; runtime isolation and least-privilege execution; protected version history and tested rollback; independent halt authority; human escalation and external authorization required for L4 criterion changes; protected constraints kept unwritable; threat model covering self-reinforcing injections (Zombie Agents) and probe selection/hidden-outcome inference; staged deployment (development-separated eval, shadow observation, limited use with safeguards, broad use) with traceable promotion records naming who can authorize promotion, suspension and rollback.

name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
org_or_authors: Hangfan Zhang, Shao Zhang, Kangcong Li, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Yiqun Zhang, Lei Bai, Shuyue Hu (Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
last_activity: Paper v3 Aug 2026; code repo github.com/qzzqzzb/Self-Harness created 2026-07-01, single 'Init' commit, last push 2026-07-02
venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.CL), no venue; citation count not retrievable (arxiv/S2 unreachable from this environment)
mechanism: Model weights and evaluator are frozen; only the harness h_t (a Python module built on LangChain Deep Agents, run under Harbor for Terminal-Bench) changes. Per round: (1) Weakness Mining: every failed train-split trace is normalized into steps/stages and an LLM (same model) labels each stage with terminal_cause / criticality / agent_mechanism; failures are clustered by exact signature tuple, ranked (root_cause first, then cluster size), and rendered into a markdown 'diagnosis brief' that also lists all passing cases as regression tests to preserve. (2) Harness Proposal: the same model is prompted K times (default route_count=4), one slot at a time with previously generated proposals shown, to emit exactly one JSON proposal that changes exactly one 'virtual hook' from a fixed menu: 6 prompt-instruction hooks (system/bootstrap/execution/verification/failure-recovery/multimodal), build_subagents or subagent_call_policy, build_skills/skill_bundle (writes SKILL.md files), build_tools, middleware_policy (conditional prompt injection on always/initial/tool_error/image_input), runtime_control_policy, permissions/interrupt_on. Edits are applied by AST-replacing that function's body in the baseline file; the proposer may 'decline' with evidence. (3) Validation: each candidate is materialized, evaluated on train (43 TB2 tasks) and heldout (21 tasks) with 2 repeats each; accept iff no split's mean pass rate drops and at least one improves. All accepted candidates from a round are function-level merged, the merge is re-evaluated under the same gate, and if accepted becomes the new active branch (linear lineage). Repeat.
eval_loop: Signal is benchmark pass rate (verifier-judged: Terminal-Bench-2.0 tests, SWE-bench Verified tests, AppWorld) on a train split plus a 'held-out' split, averaged over 2 repeats. Acceptance rule (acceptance/scripts/run_acceptance_gate.py): 'no split drops and at least one split improves' — a pure non-regression gate with no statistical test. Passing train cases are explicitly passed to the proposer as regression tests to protect. The proposer is told to use train-side evidence only, but the held-out split IS consulted by the gate, so it functions as a validation set (selection-contaminated), not a true test set; reward hacking is limited structurally because edits are constrained to one whitelisted hook per candidate and cannot touch the evaluator. Diagnosis is LLM-generated (same model), so failure attribution quality is unverified.
limitations: (1) 'Held-out' split is used inside the acceptance gate, so reported held-out gains are optimistically biased; no truly untouched test set is evident. (2) Tiny eval sets: 43 train / 21 held-out TB2 tasks x 2 repeats — one extra pass on held-out is +2.4pp, and gate accepts any positive delta with no significance test; TB2 is noisy. (3) Starting harness is a deliberately minimal 3-sentence Deep Agents prompt, so '132% relative gain' is versus a weak baseline; no numerical comparison to hand-tuned harnesses (Terminus-2, mini-SWE-agent, Claude Code) or to Meta-Harness. (4) The released 'final' Qwen harness is almost entirely added prompt text (don't repeat failed commands, check Python modules first, create missing artifacts within 1-2 steps) plus one tool-error-triggered prompt middleware — closer to GEPA/ACE-style prompt optimization than structural harness redesign. (5) No ablations, cost/token accounting, acceptance-rate statistics, or cross-model/cross-benchmark transfer results were accessible in any summary of v3. (6) Code is a partial public re-implementation: single 'Init' commit, only the TB2 Deep Agents harness shipped (no SWE-bench/AppWorld harnesses), diagnosis and proposer LLM calls must be wired by the user via command templates, README says 'more results coming soon'. (7) Authors note the method needs granular verifier outcomes and is bounded by the predefined editable surfaces.
key_insight: Constrain self-modification to a small menu of typed, AST-replaceable harness hooks (prompt slots, subagent policy, skills, middleware, tools, permissions), force each candidate to change exactly one hook tied to a specific mined failure cluster, and admit it only through a train+held-out non-regression gate — this makes same-model self-improvement of the harness tractable and auditable without any stronger external optimizer.
key_results: v1 (TB2 64-task subset, held-out 21 tasks): MiniMax M2.5 40.5%→61.9%, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 23.8%→38.1%, GLM-5 42.9%→57.1%. v3 (9 model x benchmark combos): Terminal-Bench-2.0 MiniMax M2.5 42.2→53.9, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 18.0→36.7 (+104% rel), GLM-5 46.1→57.0; SWE-bench Verified Qwen3.5 19.5→41.5 (+113%), GLM-5 52.0→55.5 (+7%); AppWorld GLM-5 44.4→85.0 (+91%); max claimed relative gain 132% (combo not identified in accessible text). Learned edits are model-specific: MiniMax — early artifact creation and content-tag discipline; Qwen — loop-breakers/no identical retries, dependency checks, a patch_verifier subagent on SWE-bench; GLM-5 — env/path persistence across shell sessions.
safety_measures: Edits restricted to whitelisted hooks in one harness file (evaluator, model, and benchmark are outside the editable surface); one hook per candidate; proposer must justify hook choice and may decline; every candidate and every merged candidate must pass the no-regression gate on both splits before promotion; permissions/interrupt_on hooks exist for human-in-the-loop tool gating; full lineage (branch_state.json, candidate_queue.json, acceptance.json with reasons) is persisted for audit. No sandboxing/safety review of proposed code beyond AST-validity, and no rollback beyond simply not promoting.
open_gaps: No truly held-out test set: the 'heldout' split participates in the acceptance gate, so a framework should add a third, never-consulted split or cross-validation to report unbiased generalization
Acceptance is 'any positive delta over 2 repeats' with no significance/noise model; needs sequential testing, more repeats, or bootstrap CIs before promoting an edit
Linear single-lineage search (one active branch, merged winners); no population/archive, no crossover across branches, no revisiting rejected-but-promising edits
No cross-model or cross-benchmark transfer: harnesses are re-derived per model x benchmark; no experiment applying Qwen's harness to GLM-5 or TB2 edits to SWE-bench

Editable surface is a fixed hand-written hook menu inside one Deep Agents file; the loop cannot invent new hook types, tools with real code, or change control flow/topology beyond adding subagents and prompt middleware
Learned edits are overwhelmingly prompt text; no mechanism to prefer structural changes or to measure which hook family actually drives gains (no ablations)
Diagnosis quality is unvalidated: failure signatures come from the same weak model with no ground-truth check, and clustering is exact-string match on LLM-chosen snake_case labels
No cost accounting or budget control: each candidate costs a full 64-task x 2-repeat benchmark run, making the loop expensive; no cheap proxy eval or early stopping
No baseline against strong hand-tuned harnesses or Meta-Harness numerically, so the value of 'self' vs 'external stronger optimizer' is asserted, not demonstrated
Released code ships only the Terminal-Bench harness and requires users to wire their own diagnosis/proposer LLM commands; SWE-bench and AppWorld loops are not reproducible from the repo

name: MIPRO / MIPROv2 (Multi-prompt Instruction PRoposal Optimizer) — "Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs"
org_or_authors: Krista Opsahl-Ong*, Michael J. Ryan*, Josh Purtell, David Broman, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab (Stanford NLP; Basis; KTH; UC Berkeley) — shipped as dspy.MIPROv2 in stanfordnlp/dspy
last_activity: Paper is static. Implementation (dspy/teleprompt/mipro_optimizer_v2.py) last touched 2026-05-13 (numpy optional), 2026-04-16 (fix demo index assignment bug), 2026-03-06 (optuna optional); DSPy repo itself pushed 2026-09-11 but new optimizer work is going into GEPA (e.g. 2026-09-05 "feat(gepa): add code_proposer hook").
venue_or_citations: EMNLP 2024 main conference (DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.emnlp-main.525). Semantic Scholar: 301 citations, 29 influential (2026-09-11). OpenAlex undercounts at 28. Used as the primary non-RL baseline in GEPA (2507.19457) and most 2025-26 prompt-optimizer papers.
mechanism:
Setting: a multi-module LM program Φ, a scalar metric μ, a small labeled trainset; no gradients, no per-module labels. Each module i has two latent categorical variables: instruction index and few-shot-demo-set index. Three stages (verified in DSPy source):

1. Bootstrap demos: run the unoptimized Φ on train inputs; keep whole traces whose final output scores ≥ threshold (rejection sampling); slice each accepted trace into per-module input/output demos; assemble N candidate demo sets per module.

2. Grounded instruction proposal: a proposer LM (GPT-3.5/4 in paper) writes N instructions per module conditioned on (a) an LM-written dataset summary (iterative batched "observations" until COMPLETE, then summarized), (b) the program's source code plus an LM summary of it, (c) bootstrapped demos of that module, (d) the seed instruction, (e) a randomly drawn "tip" (creative / simple / descriptive / high-stakes / persona). Candidate index 0 is the original instruction.

3. Bayesian search: Optuna multivariate TPE samples one (instruction, demo-set) index per module; the assembled program is scored on a random minibatch (B=35 default) of the valset; the score updates the TPE model. Every S=5 minibatch trials, the param combo with the highest mean minibatch score not yet fully evaluated is run on the full valset; that full score is injected back into the study as a trial, and only fully-evaluated combos can become the returned best. The seed program is pre-registered as a baseline trial. num_trials = max(2·vars·log2 N, 1.5N); "auto" modes light/medium/heavy set N=6/12/18 and val_size=100/300/1000.

MIPRO++ variant: TPE instead searches over proposer hyperparameters (use dataset summary?, use program summary?, temperature, tip, which demos to show the proposer) and proposes a fresh instruction each trial ("learning to propose"). Candidate pool in plain MIPRO is fixed before search — the surrogate only selects, never rewrites.
eval_loop: Signal = user-supplied task metric μ (exact match, accuracy, Recall@21, custom regex) averaged over stochastic minibatches of a labeled train/val split; a TPE surrogate does credit assignment across modules from these noisy scores. Drift/overfit control: periodic full-valset evaluation of the top-mean-minibatch candidate, and only fully-evaluated programs are eligible to be returned (minibatch winners never ship directly); seed program is a registered baseline so nothing worse than the original is returned. Paper reports on a separate held-out test set (500 train / 500 dev / up to 2k test), 5 seeds, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. No LLM judge, no self-consistency; candidates are a fixed discrete pool so the evaluator cannot be gamed by the proposer, but instructions can overfit to the demos shown in the meta-prompt (Appendix H) and small datasets overfit the valset (docs recommend ≥200 examples).
key_results: Task LM Llama-3-8B, proposer GPT-3.5/4, budgets 20-50 full-eval-equivalent trials (~300 minibatch trials). Test scores (unoptimized → Bootstrap Random Search → MIPRO): ScoNe 69.1→75.4→79.4; HotPotQA 36.1→45.8→46.4; HoVer R@21 25.3→37.2→39.0; HotPotQA-Conditional 6.0→10.4→23.3 (largest gain, ~13 pts over best baseline); Iris 40.9→94.1→88.6 (RS better); Iris-Typo 32→58.7→68.7; Heart Disease 26.8→79.2→74.2 (RS better). MIPRO best or tied on 5/7. Ablations: demos-only beats instructions-only everywhere except HotPotQA-Conditional (rule-heavy task); Grounding helps Module-level OPRO on HotPotQA (36.0→39.0) and HoVer (25.7→32.5) but hurts ScoNe (76.1→73.5); 0-shot MIPRO++ recovers ScoNe (75.7) by learning to drop the dataset summary; learned importances rank meta-prompt demos and tip highest; Bayesian Bootstrap vs RS not significant except ScoNe; greedy/coordinate-ascent and program-level OPRO gave no gain at higher cost.
limitations: Stated: fixed budget regime only; single proposer/task LM pair; optimizers cannot infer complex task rules without a hand-written seed prompt (Heart Disease, HotPotQA-Cond); benchmark is small/classic. Observed: surrogate optimizes over a fixed candidate pool so evaluation feedback never improves the instructions themselves (paper says so explicitly); instructions overfit to meta-prompt demos; needs a labeled dataset and hundreds-to-thousands of program executions (GEPA later reports beating MIPROv2 by up to ~10% with up to 35x fewer rollouts); Iris/Heart Disease results show demo-selection alone can beat the joint optimizer; test-set gains for HotPotQA/HoVer over plain bootstrap RS are within ~1-2 points; a demo-index assignment bug in the shipped optimizer persisted until 2026-04.
key_insight: Decouple proposal from credit assignment: have the LM generate a grounded pool of per-module candidates once (using data summary, program code, bootstrapped traces, and a diversity tip), then let a cheap Bayesian surrogate over discrete per-module choices, fed by noisy minibatch scores of the whole pipeline and guarded by periodic full evaluations, do joint credit assignment — no gradients, log-probs, or intermediate labels required.
open_gaps: Candidate pool is frozen before search: evaluation outcomes never rewrite instructions or demos (surrogate only selects among N pre-proposed options) — no reflective mutation from failure traces (the gap GEPA filled)
Credit assignment is purely statistical over categorical indices; textual execution traces and error messages are never used to attribute failures to a specific module
Requires a labeled training set and a scalar metric; no support for unlabeled data, rich textual feedback, or environments where the reward is a rubric/judge
Sample-inefficient: ~300 minibatch trials x 35 examples plus repeated full-valset evals (10k+ program executions) for a 2-4 module program; no early stopping or bandit-style pruning of bad candidates
No cross-task or cross-program transfer: each compile starts from an empty surrogate; learned proposer hyperparameters (MIPRO++) are discarded rather than stored as reusable knowledge
Cannot discover task rules absent from the seed prompt (Heart Disease, HotPotQA-Conditional need hand-written rules); no mechanism to learn constraints from failures
Only prompts (instruction + demos) evolve; program topology, control flow, tool set, and module count are fixed
Single scalar objective; no Pareto handling of cost, latency, or prompt length, and no multi-objective selection
No in-loop held-out generalization check: minibatch and full evals both draw from the same valset, so with small data the returned program overfits (docs recommend >=200 examples)
Instruction overfitting to the few demos shown in the meta-prompt is documented but unsolved
Full MIPRO++ (meta-optimizing both instruction and demo bootstrapping hyperparameters) was never evaluated — only the 0-shot instruction-proposal variant
Benchmark is small classic tasks (Iris, Heart Disease, 2-4 module retrieval) with an 8B model; behaviour on long-horizon agentic programs with tools is untested in the paper
safety_measures: None beyond search hygiene: candidates are a fixed pool generated once (the proposer cannot alter the evaluator or program code); the original program is registered as a baseline trial and returned if nothing beats it; only programs that pass a full-valset evaluation can be returned; per-trial candidate programs are saved to a log dir for inspection/rollback. No sandboxing needed since only prompt strings change.

name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM): Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
mechanism: Substrate is the Huxley-Gödel Machine archive tree, but each node is a multi-agent *workspace*: one shared codebase holding a meta-agent (edits the workspace), task agents (coder / paper writer / prover) and learned evaluators (code reviewer / paper reviewer / proof grader). Algorithm 1 loop over a budget of 12,288 binary validation outcomes: (1) UCB-Air gate: expand when N^0.6 >= |archive|; pick a parent by Thompson sampling on clade-metaproductivity (Beta posterior pooled over the subtree); the meta-agent self-modifies the workspace using ~3 training tasks as feedback; the child enters the archive if it runs. (2) Otherwise evaluate: Thompson-sample a node, choose the least-measured role, then its least-measured task; record a binary outcome tagged with (utility, evaluator slot, epoch). Utility = mean over tasks, then over roles. Evaluator-independent utilities (Polyglot unit tests, CRAVE code-review labels, APReS human accept/reject, IMO-GradingBench human grades) coexist with evaluator-dependent ones (the frozen incumbent judge's verdict on the task agent's artifact). (3) At power-of-two checkpoints (8,16,...,8192) each evaluator slot compares its incumbent with challenger evaluators discovered in the archive on a fixed held-out ground-truth anchor (e.g. 100 CRAVE items) via BB_eps = Beta^-1(0.05; 1+S, 1+F); a challenger with >=5 anchor outcomes wins only if strictly higher (ties keep incumbent). On replacement the slot's epoch increments, the new evaluator is frozen, and every record that depended on the old evaluator is erased (anchor/test records survive; cached artifacts are lazily re-scored), so the archive re-ranks under the stricter criterion. Adversarial objectives can be injected at boundaries: AI-written papers the old reviewer over-accepted become an adversarial pool the next reviewer must reject. Output: per-utility specialist (max BB_eps) and generalist (max mean BB_eps).
eval_loop: Signal = binary success/failure per (node, role, task), aggregated by clade-metaproductivity for search and by an eps=0.05 Beta-posterior lower bound (best-belief) for selection. Two signal classes: evaluator-independent ground truth (Polyglot executable tests; CRAVE PR-acceptance labels; APReS human accept/reject; IMO-GradingBench human grades) and evaluator-dependent LLM-judge verdicts from the frozen incumbent reviewer/grader. Anti-drift / anti-reward-hacking controls: (a) the learned judge is frozen within an epoch so HGM's fixed-criterion guarantees hold per epoch; (b) judges are replaced only at exponentially spaced checkpoints and only when a challenger strictly beats the incumbent's conservative lower bound on a held-out ground-truth anchor the proposer never sees; (c) selective erasure deletes all evidence that depended on the displaced judge so stale scores cannot steer search; (d) strict train (10) / validation (49) / held-out test (166) isolation on Polyglot; (e) adversarial pools of over-accepted AI papers debias reviewers (baseline reviewer accepted AI papers at 1.42-1.91x the human rate; RQGM reviewers become equally stringent). Residual weaknesses: within an epoch the task agent can still overfit the frozen judge; the ceiling is the anchor's decision boundary; there is no cross-epoch convergence guarantee; evaluation in the writing domain is itself an LLM-judge panel.
limitations: Demonstrated gains on verifiable coding are small: Polyglot 71.7% (119/166) vs HGM-H 69.9% (116/166) with GPT-5.5 low; the real win is 1.35-1.72x fewer blended search tokens (efficiency, not capability), and seed count is unclear. All guarantees are epoch-local (no global convergence across evaluator changes) and horizons are short. Improvement is capped by the fixed human-labeled ground-truth anchor (APReS, CRAVE, IMO-GradingBench): evaluators cannot exceed the anchor's decision boundary and repeated promotion risks anchor overfitting. Writing-domain results (40.5% vs 21.8% acceptance) are judged by an LLM panel, not humans. In proof writing the co-evolved prover still loses at the strictest Pass@7 threshold (48.3% vs 55%) to the hand-built IMO25 pipeline (authors attribute this to budget). Binary outcomes only; uniform role/task weighting; SWE-bench excluded for runtime. Per an independent reimplementer, Appendix E notes the measured gains came mostly from prompt rewrites, not deep code self-modification. Expensive (12,288 evals, $25/expansion caps, frontier model). Official code NOT released: camlsys/godel-machines is a stub (LICENSE + requirements.txt, 0 stars) and the private 16-tool coder harness, full prompts, task splits and CRAVE anchor sample are unpublished; the independent OpenRQGM 12,288-outcome reconstruction saw 4 evaluator replacements but an earlier 128-outcome run saw none, so co-evolution may simply not fire at small budgets.
key_insight: Make the evaluator a versioned, replaceable slot rather than a fixed frame: freeze it within epochs so fixed-criterion search guarantees still hold, replace it only at sparse checkpoints when a challenger beats the incumbent's conservative Beta lower bound on a held-out ground-truth anchor, and on replacement erase only the evidence that depended on the old judge so the archive re-ranks under the stricter criterion (an emergent curriculum) while anchor-based evidence persists.
open_gaps: No official code: camlsys/godel-machines is an empty stub, so the private coder harness (16 tools), full role prompts, Polyglot split and CRAVE anchor sample are unavailable; nobody can reproduce the headline numbers

Requires a fixed human-labeled ground-truth anchor per domain (CRAVE, APReS, IMO grades); no mechanism to create, grow, rotate or audit anchors automatically, so the evaluator's ceiling is the anchor and anchor overfitting is unaddressed
Guarantees are only per-epoch; no regret/convergence bound across evaluator transitions and no detection of oscillation or regression after a swap
Within an epoch the task agent can still Goodhart the frozen LLM judge; no collusion detection, randomized holdout queries or judge ensembles
Binary 0/1 outcomes only; graded rubrics, partial credit and continuous rewards must be thresholded
Uniform averaging across roles and tasks; no learned weighting, no handling of negative transfer between co-evolving roles sharing one codebase
Checkpoint schedule (rho=2), eps=0.05 and alpha=0.6 are fixed hyperparameters with no published sensitivity ablations; no multiple-testing control across many sequential replacement decisions
Self-modification gains were mostly prompt rewrites (App. E); no analysis of which workspace edits (tools, code, prompts) transfer across domains
Compute-heavy: 12,288 frontier-model evaluations per run and SWE-bench excluded for runtime; no cheap-model or app-developer-scale recipe
Coding gain is +1.8pp on a single benchmark with unclear seed count; no held-out cross-benchmark generalization of the discovered coder/reviewer
Evaluator replacement can fail to fire at small budgets (OpenRQGM 128-outcome run: zero replacements), so small-scale users get plain HGM plus a reviewer overhead
Safety/containment for evolved evaluators (sandboxing, permission boundaries, rollback of a bad evaluator promotion) is not specified beyond Docker and $ caps

Theory: epoch-local validity inherited from HGM; anchor-gated promotion; erasure overhead linear in budget with exponential checkpoints (Prop. 6). Fig. 3: evaluator replacement permanently re-ranks the archive (curriculum effect). Independent OpenRQGM reconstruction (single seed, different harness) reached 163/166 held-out with 4 evaluator replacements, but without matched HGM-H controls.
